**Commands.** `family_doc.visibility.set(element_ids[], {coarse, medium, fine, plan, front_back, left_right, only_when_cut, visible_param?})` · `family_doc.draw_order(element_ids[], "front"|"back"|"forward"|"backward")` · `family_doc.preview_visibility.toggle(view_id?) -> ()`

**Acceptance criteria.**
- [ ] A door family whose panel is visible only at Medium and Fine, and whose swing symbolic line is in Plan only, shows the correct geometry at all three detail levels in a project plan and elevation.
- [ ] With Preview Visibility on in the family's Ref. Level plan at Coarse, the same door shows exactly what a Coarse project plan shows, and turning it off shows all elements again.

### 2.8.12 Special family kinds
**ID:** DM-FSPEC-001 … 006 · **Priority:** see table · **Ref:** research/05 §5.1–§5.8; screenshots/platform/edit_label_dialog_2026.png

| ID | Kind | Priority | Requirements |
|---|---|---|---|
| DM-FSPEC-001 | **Annotation families: tags and symbols** | P0 (shipped tag families, used as is) / P1 (editing) | 2D families with lines, filled regions, text and **labels**. A label binds text to one or more parameters, each with prefix, suffix, sample value, spaces before it, line break after it, and optional unit-format override. Labels may contain **calculated values** (formulas, §2.8.7, over the tagged element's parameters). Tag families have a target category. **Multi-category tags** read shared and built-in common parameters from any category, and can be the default tag for *Tag by Category* and *Tag All Not Tagged*. Families set rotate-with-component and fixed-rotation flags. Leader behaviour is defined in DOC. **Edit Label** dialog: category parameters on the left; label parameters (Spaces, Prefix, Sample Value, Suffix, Break) on the right. |
| DM-FSPEC-002 | **Title block families** | P0 (shipped title blocks) / P1 (editing) | Sheet-size templates. They contain border lines, images (logos, RXD assets) and labels bound to **Sheet**, **Sheet Collection** and **Project Information** parameters (including shared parameters). They can have an embedded revision schedule (DOC), several types, and Yes/No-driven visibility. A type property overrides the "As indicated" scale text. Title-block parameters are available to sheet list schedules (DOC). |
| DM-FSPEC-003 | **Profile families** | P1 | 2D closed loops used by sweeps, wall sweeps and reveals, slab edges, fascias, gutters, railings, mullions (several loops allowed), stair nosings and custom structural sections. Profiles may have types and parameters. Loops must be closed, non-self-intersecting and drawn in the template's single plane; open or crossing loops are refused on save with the offending curves highlighted. The template's origin is the insertion point used by hosts. A *profile usage* type parameter (generic, mullion, rail, nosing, reveal, slab edge) filters which tools list the profile. In IFC, a profile type used by a profiled element becomes an `IfcArbitraryClosedProfileDef` (or `IfcArbitraryProfileDefWithVoids`) referenced from `IfcMaterialProfile`. |
| DM-FSPEC-004 | **Detail item families** | P1 | 2D, category Detail Items, placed in views. Contents: detail lines, filled and masking regions, text, labels and nested detail items, with types and parameters. Line-based detail items stretch between two picked points and support **repeating details** (DOC). Draw order inside the family and against other view elements is kept (§2.8.11). Detail items can be tagged, keynoted and scheduled. They never appear in 3D or in IFC exchange exports. Storage: RXD documents (`families/…` for the definition; `views/annotation/<viewId>` for placed instances). |
| DM-FSPEC-005 | **MEP connectors** | P1 | Connector elements in families: duct, pipe, cable tray, conduit and electrical. Each has system classification, shape (round, rectangular, oval), size linked to parameters, flow configuration (calculated, preset, system), flow direction (in, out, bidirectional), loss method, and electrical properties (voltage, poles, apparent load, power factor). One connector may be *primary*. Connectors can be *linked* for pass-through flow. In IFC: `IfcDistributionPort` nested in the type (`IfcRelNests`) with `FlowDirection`, `PredefinedType` and `SystemType`, plus `Pset_DistributionPortCommon` and the port-type psets. The detailed behaviour is in the MEP chapter. |
| DM-FSPEC-006 | **Mass families** | P2 | Built in the CME (§2.8.13), as loadable families or in-place masses. In projects: *Show Mass* toggle, **mass floors** by level (one per selected level that cuts the mass), gross floor area, volume and surface area reported as read-only parameters, and **by-face** creation of walls, floors, roofs and curtain systems, with *Update to Face* (ARC chapter). Masses are hidden in views unless shown, and are excluded from exchange exports by default (§2.11.4). Mass floor areas feed area schedules and energy analysis (ANA). |

**Commands.** `family_doc.label.create(position, params[{param, prefix?, suffix?, sample?, spaces?, break?}], text_type_id) -> element_id` · `family_doc.label.edit(label_id, params[])` · `family_doc.connector.create(kind, face_ref | work_plane, props) -> element_id` · `family_doc.connector.set(connector_id, props)`

**Acceptance criteria.**
- [ ] A door tag family with a label "Mark" plus a calculated value `text(Width, "unit:mm;dp:0") & "x" & text(Height, "unit:mm;dp:0")` shows "D-104" and "915x2134" for a tagged door.
- [ ] A title block label bound to a shared project-information parameter "Client Reference" shows the project's value on every sheet.
- [ ] A pipe elbow family with two pipe connectors linked to a "Nominal Diameter" parameter exports two `IfcDistributionPort`s nested in its type.

### 2.8.13 Adaptive components and the conceptual massing environment (CME)
**ID:** DM-CME-001 … 005 · **Priority:** P2 · **Ref:** research/05 §5.5, §5.6, §6; screenshots/platform/adaptive_component_repetition_2026.png, screenshots/platform/conceptual_divided_surface_patterned_2026.png, screenshots/platform/conceptual_uv_grid_2026.png

**Purpose.** A 3D-first environment for masses, adaptive components and pattern-based panels, used for façades, trusses and complex repeated geometry.

#### DM-CME-001 — Conceptual environment
- Uses 3D levels and work planes, reference points (free, hosted on curves or faces, driving), a 3D snapping system, a 3D move gizmo (drag along or across axes) and **X-Ray** mode (shows the form's profiles, path and edges).
- **Create Form** (solid or void) from selected curves and references. It infers the form type:
  - one closed profile → **extrusion** (one open profile → surface);
  - two or more profiles on non-intersecting planes → **loft**;
  - profile + path → **sweep**;
  - profile + line in the same plane → **revolve**;
  - several profiles along a path → **swept blend**.
  If several results are possible, a chooser appears (thumbnails of the options).
- **Direct editing**: push and pull faces, edges and vertices with the gizmo. *Add Edge*, *Add Profile*, *Dissolve* (back to profiles), *Rebuild*.
- Forms are either **reference-based** (driven by references and parameters) or **unconstrained** (directly editable).
- OCCT: lofts use `BRepOffsetAPI_ThruSections` (smooth); sweeps use `BRepOffsetAPI_MakePipeShell`; surfaces use `BRepFill`/`GeomFill`. IFC: `IfcAdvancedBrep` (B-spline surfaces); `IfcTriangulatedFaceSet` as a fallback.
- **Workflow.** (1) Create a family from the Mass, Generic Model Adaptive or pattern-based template; the document opens in a 3D view with two reference planes and a level. (2) Draw model or reference lines on a work plane or on 3D levels, or place reference points. (3) Select curves and choose *Create Form › Solid* or *Void*. (4) Edit the result with the gizmo, or add profiles and edges. (5) Flex parameters in Family Types (§2.8.6) and load into a project.
- **Work planes in 3D.** Clicking on a face, level or reference plane makes it the active work plane for the next sketch (*Set work plane automatically*, default on). Reference points host their own three work planes. The 3D snapping set adds face, edge, point-on-curve and mid-point snaps.
- **Model lines vs reference lines.** Forms built on model lines consume them (the lines become form edges). Forms built on reference lines stay driven by them, so moving the reference line or changing a parameter on it reshapes the form.
- **Edge cases.** Self-intersecting or zero-area profiles are refused with the curve highlighted. A loft whose profiles have different vertex counts uses automatic vertex matching, which the user can edit in X-Ray. A form that fails to rebuild after a parameter change keeps its last valid shape and raises a warning naming the failing step (§2.7.4).
- **Data.** RXD document `families/<id>` (`forms[]` with kind `cme_form`, the referenced curves and points, and whether each form is reference-based or unconstrained); evaluated geometry per type in IFC as in §2.8.14.
- **Acceptance.** Moving a reference line that drives a loft reshapes the loft in the same transaction; deleting a model line used by a form is refused with a message naming the form.

#### DM-CME-002 — Divided surfaces and paths
- **Divide Surface** creates a UV grid on a face. Each direction is set by number, or by distance (with justification, grid rotation and belt offset). Alternatively, the surface is divided by **intersecting references** (levels, reference planes, lines), and the *Face Manager* edits which references are used.
- **Divide Path** places nodes along curves (by number, distance, or intersections).
- **Surface representation** controls show and hide the original surface, nodes, U/V grid lines, pattern lines and pattern fill.

#### DM-CME-003 — Patterns and pattern-based panels
- Built-in **patterns** for divided surfaces: Rectangle, Rectangle Checkerboard, 1/2 Step, 1/3 Step, Arrows, Hexagon, Octagon, Octagon Rotate, Rhomboid, Rhomboid Checkerboard, Triangle (bent and flat), Triangle Checkerboard (bent and flat), Zigzag.
- **Pattern-based panel families** (template *Curtain Panel Pattern-Based*) define a tile with adaptive corner points. Applied to a divided surface, they populate each tile, adapting to the node positions. Border tiles: *Partial*, *Overhanging*, *Empty* (per surface).

#### DM-CME-004 — Adaptive components
- Family template *Generic Model Adaptive*. **Reference points** can be made **adaptive**: they are numbered placement points, plus optional *shape handle* points. Geometry is built between them from reference lines and forms. Orientation options for each point: global, host, instance, and their combinations.
- **Placement**: the user clicks N points in a project, on a divided-surface node, on a divided-path node or on any surface. The instance adapts to them. The command form is `instance.place_adaptive` (§2.2.5).
- **Repeat** distributes an adaptive component across a divided path or a surface node grid, following the pattern of the first placement. The repeater is one element with a *repeater* type.
- In IFC, each placed adaptive instance is an occurrence with its own representation (geometry is unique per placement). Its adaptive point positions are RXD element data (`adaptive`).

#### DM-CME-005 — Masses in projects
- See DM-FSPEC-006. Energy-analysis use of masses is in the ANA chapter.

**Commands.**
`cme.form.create(curve_refs[], solid=true, choice?) -> element_id` ·
`cme.form.push_pull(subelement_ref, vector)` ·
`cme.form.add_edge(face_ref, p1, p2)` · `cme.form.add_profile(form_id, parameter)` · `cme.form.dissolve(form_id)` ·
`cme.divide_surface(face_ref, {u, v} | {references[]}) -> element_id` ·
`cme.divide_path(curve_refs[], spec) -> element_id` ·
`cme.surface.set_pattern(divided_surface_id, pattern, border_tiles?)` ·
`cme.surface.apply_component(divided_surface_id, panel_type_id)` ·
`cme.point.create(position | host_ref, adaptive=false) -> element_id` · `cme.point.make_adaptive(point_id, index?)` ·
`cme.repeat(adaptive_instance_id) -> element_id`

**Acceptance criteria.**
- [ ] A loft created from three closed profiles on parallel planes can be dissolved back to the profiles and re-formed with the same result.
- [ ] A curved façade divided 20 × 10 and populated with a 4-point adaptive panel produces 200 panels that follow the surface when its control profile moves.
- [ ] A 2-point adaptive beam repeated along a 50-node divided path creates 49 instances, and these export to IFC as occurrences with unique geometry.

### 2.8.14 Family package file format
**ID:** DM-FFMT-001 · **Priority:** P0 (reading packages for placement) / P1 (writing from the Family Editor) · **Ref:** research/05 §4.9, §11.1, §16.9; TECH_STACK §3.1; spec/02a_extension_data_format.md

**Purpose.** Families are stored as **IFC type libraries**, so that any IFC tool can use a family's types and geometry, while Reviera keeps the full parametric definition as RXD.

**Behaviour & rules.**
- A **family package** is a valid IFC4 file (IFC4X3 optional, matching the target project schema). Recommended names: `<Family>.family.ifc` for one family, `<Library>.library.ifc` for a collection, `<Name>.familytemplate.ifc` for templates. `.ifczip` is allowed.
- **IFC content.** The package shall contain:
  1. one `IfcProject` (Name = the family or library name), with SI units and the representation contexts of §2.3.1. It contains no spatial structure, and no occurrences except as noted below;
  2. one `IfcProjectLibrary` per family (the **primary** family, plus every nested family it needs), declared by the project with `IfcRelDeclares`;
  3. each family's types, as `IfcTypeObject` subtypes declared by the family's library with `IfcRelDeclares`. Each type carries:
     - its type-parameter values as property sets (§2.3.3);
     - its evaluated geometry for that type's values: `RepresentationMaps` for `Body` (Fine, plus `Body-Coarse`/`Body-Medium` when different), `Axis`, `FootPrint`, plan `Annotation`;
     - its material assignments: `IfcMaterialLayerSet`, `IfcMaterialProfileSet` or `IfcMaterialConstituentSet`;
     - its ports (`IfcDistributionPort`, nested) for MEP families;
     - its classification (`IfcRelAssociatesClassification`);
  4. every `IfcMaterial` used, with its properties and styles (§2.10.5);
  5. for annotation, title block, detail and profile families, which have no IFC type class: no IFC types. Their whole definition is RXD.
- **RXD content** (carried as `02a` defines; logical content only here):
  - an RXD document `families/<id>/package` (the package manifest):
    - package format version and minimum Reviera version;
    - the primary family GUID and the list of contained families;
    - the template flag and the source template GUID;
    - a preview image (RXD asset, PNG, 512 × 512);
    - author, licence (an SPDX expression, optional for content but recommended), description and keywords;
  - one RXD document `families/<id>` per family, holding: `name`, `category`, `template`, `placement_mode`, `flags` (§2.8.2), `parameters[]` (§2.8.6, with formulas), `types[]` (name, values, link to the IFC type GUID), `references[]` (§2.8.3), `sketches[]`, `forms[]` (§2.8.4), `dimensions[]` and `constraints[]` (§2.8.5), `symbolic[]` (2D elements with view orientation), `nested[]` (§2.8.10), `arrays[]`, `controls[]`, `connectors[]`, `labels[]` (annotation families), `lookup_tables[]` (§2.8.8), `adaptive_points[]`, `divided_surfaces[]` (CME), `subcategories[]`, `views[]` (family views and their settings).
- **Informative skeleton of `families/<family-guid>`:**

```json
{
  "schema": "reviera.family", "schema_version": "1.0.0",
  "guid": "3vB2…", "name": "Single-Flush Door", "category": "cat.doors",
  "template": "door", "placement_mode": "wall_hosted",
  "flags": { "shared": false, "room_calculation_point": true, "ifc_predefined_type": "DOOR" },
  "parameters": [
    { "id": "p1", "name": "Width",  "data_type": "length", "group": "dimensions", "instance": false,
      "ifc_home": ["Pset_DoorCommon", null], "attribute": "OverallWidth" },
    { "id": "p2", "name": "Frame Width", "data_type": "length", "group": "construction", "instance": false },
    { "id": "p3", "name": "Leaf Width", "data_type": "length", "group": "dimensions", "instance": false,
      "formula": "Width - 2 * Frame Width" }
  ],
  "types": [ { "name": "0915 x 2134", "ifc_type": "1xH4…", "values": { "p1": 0.915, "p2": 0.05 } } ],
  "references": [ { "id": "r1", "name": "Left", "is_reference": "left", "plane": { "origin": [-0.4575,0,0], "normal": [1,0,0] } } ],
  "forms": [ { "id": "f1", "kind": "extrusion", "sketch": "s1", "start": 0, "end": { "param": "p5" },
               "material": { "param": "p9" }, "subcategory": "Panel",
               "visibility": { "coarse": false, "medium": true, "fine": true } } ],
  "nested": [], "lookup_tables": [], "connectors": []
}
```

- **Consistency rule.** On save, the IFC types and their geometry shall be regenerated from the RXD definition, so the two always agree. On load, if the RXD is missing (for example, the package was re-saved by a tool that strips unknown property sets), the family loads as a **static family**. Its types and geometry are usable, but parametric editing is unavailable, and the user is told why.
- **Third-party type libraries.** Any IFC file whose `IfcProject` declares an `IfcProjectLibrary` with types (or declares types directly) can be loaded as static families, one family per library, or per type class when there is no library.
- **Embedding.** Inside a project, an embedded family is exactly the same content: an `IfcProjectLibrary` + types in the project's IFC, plus the `families/<guid>` RXD document. *Save Family As* writes a package from it unchanged.
- **Versioning.** Each family has a `family_version` (semver) that increases on every save from the Family Editor. On load, Reviera compares family GUID and version (§2.2.3).

**Commands.** `family.package.inspect(path) -> {families[], types[], has_rxd, version, licence}` · plus `family.load`, `family.save_as` (§2.2.3) and `family_doc.save` (§2.8.0).

**Acceptance criteria.**
- [ ] A family package saved by Reviera passes IFC4 schema validation. It opens in at least two other open-source IFC tools (for example IfcOpenShell-based Bonsai, and one web viewer), which show its types with correct geometry and property values.
- [ ] Re-saving a package through a tool that strips unknown property sets, then loading it, gives a static family with all types, and the user is told that parametric editing is unavailable.
- [ ] *Save Family As* from a project, followed by loading into a new project, gives types and instances that match the original exactly (the same geometry hashes).

### 2.8.15 Library browser
**ID:** DM-LIB-001 · **Priority:** P1 (local folders) / P2 (organisation libraries over HTTPS or git) · **Ref:** research/05 §4.9 (load family, content library), §11.1, §16.2; spec/01 (Insert › Load from Library)

**Purpose.** Find, inspect and load families and types from local folders and from organisation libraries without knowing file paths. It is the open counterpart of a vendor cloud content library.

**Workflow.**
1. Insert › Load from Library › **Browse Library** (`library.browse(query?, source?)`), or *Load Family…* › *Browse library* in the file dialog. The **Library** panel opens docked to the right (it can float).
2. Pick a source in the tree, or search across all sources. Narrow the results with filters.
3. Select a result. The preview pane shows the family, its types and its key parameters.
4. Choose **Load** (opens Specify Types when the family has many types, §2.8.9), **Load and Place** (loads, then starts placement with the chosen type), or **Open** (opens the package in the Family Editor; not available for read-only sources unless saved as a copy).

**UI.**
- **Sources tree**: *Reviera Library* (shipped content), *My Libraries* (user folders), *Organisation* (configured remote libraries and network folders), *Favourites*, *Recently loaded*. Each source shows its state (indexed, indexing n %, offline, error).
- **Search box** with free text over name, type names, category, keywords and description; **filters** for category, placement mode (§2.8.1), IFC class, discipline, licence, author or publisher, and "has types matching" (for example `Width >= 900 mm`, using the collector's operators, §2.13.3).
- **Results** as a thumbnail grid or a list (Name, Category, Types, Source, Version, Licence, Modified), sortable, with the count of matches.
- **Preview pane**: an interactive 3D preview (orbit, zoom; plan and front views for 2D families) rendered locally from the package geometry; the type list with each type's values for up to 8 key parameters chosen by the family's author (default: the dimension group); the licence (SPDX), author, version and description from the package manifest (§2.8.14); and warnings (for example "Static family: no parametric data", "Requires Reviera 1.3").
- Context menu: Add to / Remove from Favourites, Show in folder, Copy path or URL, Properties.

**Behaviour & rules.**
- **Indexing.** Each source is indexed in the background into a per-user cache (`<cache_dir>/reviera/library-index.sqlite`). The index stores, per family: package path or URL, content hash, family GUID and version, name, category, placement mode, type names and key values, keywords, licence and the 512 × 512 preview image from the manifest. Re-indexing is incremental by modification time and hash. A 10,000-family folder indexes once and is searchable within 200 ms per query afterwards.
- **Library files.** A `<Library>.library.ifc` holding several families shows one result per family. Third-party IFC type libraries are indexed as static families (§2.8.14) and marked so.
- **Organisation libraries (P2).** A remote library is a static JSON index (`reviera.library-index`, version 1) at an HTTPS URL or in a git repository: one entry per package with URL, SHA-256, family GUID, version, licence and preview URL. Packages are downloaded on demand into the cache and verified against the checksum; a mismatch is refused. Sources can be pre-configured by an administrator policy file, and those cannot be removed by the user. No vendor service is needed.
- **Duplicates.** When the same family GUID appears in several sources, results group them and show the highest version first; the user can pick another version.
- **Loading** uses `family.load` (§2.2.3) with its reload rules: if the family is already in the project, the comparison of GUID and version is shown before loading.
- **Licence display.** Packages without a licence are shown with "Licence not stated". A package whose licence forbids redistribution is still loadable for private use, but a notice is shown once per package.
- **Offline.** Cached remote packages remain loadable offline; uncached ones are listed but greyed.

**Data (storage).** No model data. Sources, favourites and the index are per-user application data (UI chapter, preferences). Loaded families are embedded as usual (§2.2.3). The source URL and package hash are recorded in `families/index` so *Reload from library* can find a newer version.

**Commands.**
`library.browse(query?, source?)` (opens the panel) ·
`library.search(text?, filters?, source?, limit=100) -> library_item[]` ·
`library.source.add(path_or_url, name?) -> source_id` · `library.source.remove(source_id)` ·
`library.refresh(source_id?)` ·
`library.load(item_ref, type_names?, place=false) -> family_id`

**Acceptance criteria.**
- [ ] Adding a local folder of 2,000 family packages indexes it in the background without blocking editing; a search for "door 900" then returns matching door families within 200 ms.
- [ ] Selecting a result shows a rotatable 3D preview and its types without loading the family into the project (the model version is unchanged).
- [ ] A remote library whose package checksum does not match its index entry is refused with an error naming the package, and nothing is loaded.
- [ ] *Load and Place* on a door with 30 types opens Specify Types, then starts door placement with the chosen type.

### 2.8.16 Stamps: placing components again and again (Place Component)
**ID:** DM-LIB-002 · **Priority:** P1 · **Ref:** owner requirement (2026-10-14); DM-LIB-001, DM-IMP-015, ARC-COMP-001; Reviera's own design

**Purpose.** Make custom geometry quick to reuse. Any custom object (DM-IMP-015), family type or saved group in a library can be picked up as a **stamp**, and every click in a view inserts another copy. *(Owner requirement, 2026-10-14: "a library system so that custom objects can be used as a stamp to easily insert a duplicate of the object".)*

**Workflow.**
1. Open the **Library** panel (DM-LIB-001). Its **Stamps** strip, at the top of the panel, shows thumbnails of pinned stamps and the most recently used ones.
2. Click a stamp, or double-click a library result. The **Place Component** tool (CM, as for components generally, ARC-COMP-001) starts with that component: a see-through preview follows the cursor, snapping like other placement tools.
3. Click to insert a copy. The tool stays armed, so each further click inserts another, until Esc or another tool.
4. While stamping:
   - Spacebar turns the next copy by 90°; Shift+Spacebar mirrors it.
   - *Click and drag* sets the direction of that copy.
   - `[` and `]` step through the Stamps strip, and the digit keys 1–9 pick pinned stamps.
5. **Pick a stamp from the model**: in Place Component, Alt+click an existing instance, or select it and choose *Stamp This*. That instance's type becomes the stamp, with its rotation and offset.

**Behaviour & rules.**
- **What can be a stamp:**
  - a custom object type (DM-IMP-015);
  - a family type (DM-LIB-001);
  - a model fragment: a set of related elements, for example a desk with its chair and lamp, or a whole bathroom (DM-LIB-003).
- **Adding to the library:**
  - **Add to Library** (on a selected instance or type) copies the type into a library folder, with a thumbnail rendered from it.
  - **Create Component** turns any selection into a new component (DM-LIB-003): an IFC file of the model fragment, saved into a library folder. Alternatively it merges the selection into one custom object.
  - Library items carry a name, a category, tags and a description, all searchable.
- **Libraries:**
  - **My Library** is per user, in the user data folder.
  - **Project Library** holds the types already in the open project.
  - Further library folders, including network or WebDAV folders shared by a team, can be added as sources (DM-LIB-001).
  - Pinned stamps and recent stamps are kept per user.
- **Copies are duplicates of one type.**
  - The first stamp of a library item into a project loads its type once. The type keeps the library item's GUID, so it isn't duplicated if stamped again later. Later stamps reuse it.
  - Every stamped copy is an instance of that type: changing the type (materials, scale, Reload from File) changes every copy.
  - **Make Unique** gives one copy a type of its own.
  - When a newer version of the item is in the library, the project offers to update the type (*Reload from library*, DM-LIB-001).
- **Where copies go:**
  - In a plan, on the plan's level, at the type's default offset.
  - In a 3D view, on the face under the cursor: floors, roofs, decks, terrain and the tops of other objects. Optionally the copy turns to the face's slope.
  - On a work plane when one is set.
  - A copy's base level is the level it is placed on, or the nearest level below the face it lands on.
- **Variation (P2).** For planting and scattered objects, a stamp can vary each copy: a random rotation, a random scale within a range (for example 90–110 %), or a choice among several stamps in a set.
- **Rows of stamps (P2).** Shift+drag stamps a row of evenly spaced copies along the drag. The spacing is the stamp's width plus a gap, or a typed distance; the count shows while dragging.
- **Undo.** Each click is one undo step; a row or a scatter is one step.

**Data (storage).**
- A library item is a file in a library folder (DM-LIB-004):
  - a 3D file as it is, such as OBJ, STL, PLY, glTF/GLB, 3MF or OFF;
  - an IFC file: a family package (§2.8.14), a fragment (DM-LIB-003), or any IFC file.

  Stamping a mesh file the first time imports it into the project as a custom object type (DM-IMP-015), with the import options from its manifest entry or folder. Later stamps reuse that type.
- In a project, a stamped type records its library source and the item's content hash in `families/index`, so the Library panel can tell when it is out of date.
- Pinned and recent stamps are per-user settings, not model data.

**Commands.**
`library.add_item(element_or_type_id, library?, name?, tags?) -> item_ref` ·
`component.place(type_id | {library, item}, points[], level, offset?, rotation?, mirror?) -> element_ids[]` (ARC-COMP-001's command, extended: a library item, one copy per point) ·
`component.place_row(type_id | {library, item}, start, end, spacing?, count?) -> element_ids[]` (P2) ·
`component.scatter(sources[], points[], rotation_range?, scale_range?, seed?) -> element_ids[]` (P2) ·
`element.make_unique(element_id) -> type_id`.
The Place Component tool is the UI over `component.place`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- [ ] A custom chair added to My Library appears in the Stamps strip with a thumbnail. Clicking it and then clicking ten times in a plan inserts ten chairs, and the saved IFC holds one chair type with ten instances.
- [ ] Undo after the tenth click removes only the tenth chair.
- [ ] Alt+click on a placed table in Place Component makes the table the stamp; the next click inserts a table with the same rotation.
- [ ] In a 3D view, stamping a lamp on a sloped roof places it on the roof face, and with *Align to face* on, its up direction is the roof's normal.
- [ ] A desk, chair and lamp added to the library as a fragment stamp as three elements together.
- [ ] Changing the chair type's material in the project changes all ten stamped chairs. After Make Unique on one, changing the type no longer changes that one.
- [ ] Stamping the same library item in a second session reuses the type already in the project, not a second copy.

**Implementation note (2026-10-14, first build).**
- **Placing:** the Component Library panel's thumbnails are the palette. Clicking one starts Place Component, which repeats until Esc, and Spacebar turns the next copy 90°.
- **Where copies land:** in plans on the plan's level, snapped; in 3D on the surface under the cursor, or on the lowest level's plane over nothing.
- **First copy:** a library component is loaded as a type on its first copy, and the tool then places that type.
- **Properties:** they show the placement (rotation, mirror, offset) and the component's details, which are edited into the manifest.
- **Command:** `component.place` extends ARC-COMP-001's command with a library item and several points.
- **Not built yet:** pinned and recent stamps, Alt+click to pick a stamp from the model, Shift+Spacebar mirroring (Properties has Mirrored), rows and scatter, drag from the palette, and stamping fragments.

### 2.8.17 Model fragments in the library
**ID:** DM-LIB-003 · **Priority:** P1 · **Ref:** owner requirement (2026-10-14); DM-LIB-001, DM-LIB-002, ARC-GRP-001 (Save Group, Load as Group); Reviera's own design

**Purpose.** Let a library hold whole pieces of buildings, not only single objects: a bathroom with its walls, door, fixtures and room; a stair core; a kitchen run; a balcony with its railing; a façade bay; or part of a consultant's or manufacturer's IFC model. Like a family in the reference product, a library item is a named, reusable definition that can have several variants. Unlike a family, it may be a full IFC **model fragment** of many related elements. *(Owner requirement, 2026-10-14: "may include full IFC model fragments. A selection of objects in a model could be added to the library.")*

**Behaviour & rules.**
- **Kinds of library item.** Every item has one of three kinds, shown with a badge in the Library panel:
  - **Object**: one type, such as a custom mesh object (DM-IMP-015) or a family type.
  - **Fragment**: a set of related elements, stored as a group template (ARC-GRP-001).
  - **Collection**: a folder of items (DM-LIB-004).
- **Create Component from any selection.** *(Owner clarification, 2026-10-14: "any subselection of objects can be used to create a new component; it is just an IFC with the model fragment".)*
  - **What can be selected:** any selection of objects in a model, of any categories and any number. This includes a sub-selection:
    - some of a group's or a placed component's members, picked with Tab;
    - elements of an imported or linked IFC model.
  - **Create Component** (first in the middle-click quick modify menu, UI-SEL-006; also on the Modify tab, the right-click menu, and Library › Create Component) writes the selection as a new component: **an IFC file of that model fragment**, and nothing else.
  - **Where it goes:** into a folder of an open library, where it becomes a library item at once, or to any path.
  - **In the dialog:** name, destination (a library folder, or a file path), tags and description, and the options below.
  - **Kind**: *Fragment* (default for several elements) or *Object* (merge into one custom object, DM-IMP-015).
  - **Base point**: the selection's bottom-centre, a picked point, or the project's base point. It becomes the fragment's origin, the point the cursor holds when stamping.
  - **Include hosts and hosted**, on by default:
    - selecting a wall brings its doors, windows, openings, curtain panels and wall-hosted fixtures;
    - selecting a door or window brings its host wall;
    - selecting a stair brings its railings, and a roof its dormers, skylights and openings.
  - **Include rooms**: the rooms enclosed by the selected walls (on by default).
  - **Levels.** A fragment on several levels keeps each member's level as a **relative level**: 0 for its lowest, then 1, 2… by elevation, with each level's height above the lowest.
  - **Outside references.** Each reference to an element outside the selection is listed, then dropped (with the element left as it is) or brought in. Such references include a wall attached to a roof, a join to another wall, or a stair opening in a floor. The dialog shows the list before saving.
  - **Replace selection with the component** (on by default): the selected elements become a placed copy of the new component, a group instance (ARC-GRP-001). Copies stamped later are linked to them. Off, the selection is left as it was and only the file is written.
- **Edit Component.** On a placed copy or a library item, **Edit Component** opens the component's IFC file in its own tab, as a model. Every tool works there, and Save writes the file. Projects open in the session that use the component update their copies; others offer *Reload from library* when next opened (DM-LIB-001). Read-only libraries open the file as a copy, to be saved elsewhere.
- **Variants.** An item can hold several variants (like the types of a family), for example a bathroom in a left-hand and a right-hand version, or a chair in three sizes. Variants of a fragment are group types of one item; variants of an object are types of one family or custom object. **Add Variant** adds the current selection to an existing item as a new variant.
- **IFC files as fragments.** An IFC file copied into a library folder is a fragment at once (see Data). **Import to Library** (Manage › Library) writes a part of an external IFC file into a library folder as a new IFC file:
  - the part is chosen by storey, by IFC class, by system, or by picking in a preview;
  - elements keep their IFC classes, property sets, materials and geometry;
  - elements Reviera recognises become Reviera elements (DM-IMP-001 Recognise); the rest stay IFC-native (§2.11.1).
- **Stamping a fragment** (DM-LIB-002) creates the elements again at the clicked point, in one of two modes, chosen per stamp:
  - **As a group** (default): a group instance (ARC-GRP-001). Editing the group changes every stamped copy; Ungroup makes one independent.
  - **As elements**: independent elements with no group.

  In both modes:
  - **GUIDs**: every element gets new GlobalIds.
  - **Types**: the fragment's types are merged into the project. A type that already exists (same GUID, or same name and identical parameters) is reused. Otherwise there is a choice: *Use project's*, *Use library's*, or *Keep both* (renamed with a suffix).
  - **Materials**: matched by name, or created.
  - **Levels**: relative level 0 is the level clicked on. Higher relative levels map to the project's levels above it by order or by nearest elevation (a setting). When the project has too few levels, the member stays on the highest one with an offset, and a warning lists it.
  - **Hosts**: members whose host was left out of the fragment are rehosted where the copy lands (ARC-GRP-001 hosted members). An example is a door saved without its wall, stamped onto a wall.
- **Preview.** Selecting a fragment in the Library panel shows a 3D preview, its plan outline, its member counts by category, its variants, its levels and its size.

**Data (storage).**
- A fragment is an IFC file in a library folder.
  - **Written by Reviera** (Create Component, Import to Library): a standalone IFC4 model of the fragment, with:
    - a project, site and building;
    - one storey per relative level;
    - the elements with their types, materials, property sets, openings, hosting and other relationships.

    Its RXD carries the group template, the relative levels, the base point and the list of dropped outside references. For Import to Library, it also carries the source file's name and SHA-256. The RXD is optional to the file's meaning: with it stripped, Reviera still uses the file as an IFC fragment, as below.
  - **Any other IFC file** placed in a library folder is a fragment as it is. Stamping it brings its elements in as an IFC merge does (DM-IMP-001):
    - its storeys become relative levels by elevation;
    - its base point is the bottom-centre, unless its manifest entry names one;
    - its types become variants when it has several.
  - Either way, the file opens in other IFC tools as a small model.
- An item's variants are the types or group types in its file, or several files grouped as variants in the manifest.
- In a project, a group type stamped from the library records the item's GUID, variant and content hash in `families/index` (DM-LIB-001), so the Library panel can offer updates.

**Commands.**
`component.create(element_ids[], destination: folder_ref | path, name, kind?: "fragment"|"object", base_point?, include_hosts?: bool, include_rooms?: bool, replace_selection?: bool = true, tags?) -> item_ref` ·
`component.edit(item_ref | element_id) -> document_id` · `component.reload(item_ref)` ·
`library.add_variant(item_ref, element_ids[], variant_name) -> variant_ref` ·
`library.import_ifc(path, folder, filter?: {storeys?, classes?, systems?, element_guids?}, name?) -> item_ref` ·
`library.inspect(item_ref) -> {kind, variants, members_by_category, levels, size, outside_refs}` *(query)* ·
`component.place(..., mode?: "group"|"elements", type_conflict?: "project"|"library"|"both")` (DM-LIB-002, extended).


**Acceptance criteria.**
- [ ] Selecting a bathroom's four walls and choosing Create Component (hosts and rooms on) saves an IFC file with the walls, the door, the fixtures and the room, and replaces the selection with a placed copy of it. The saved file opens in another IFC viewer.
- [ ] Stamping that fragment three times, as groups, places three bathrooms, each with new GlobalIds. Adding a fixture to one bathroom's group adds it to all three.
- [ ] A fragment of a stair core spanning two levels, stamped on Level 2 of a five-level project, puts its upper part on Level 3.
- [ ] A fragment whose wall type `Exterior 300` differs from the project's type of the same name asks *Use project's / Use library's / Keep both*. *Keep both* adds `Exterior 300 (2)`.
- [ ] Import to Library of a manufacturer's IFC file, filtered to `IfcSanitaryTerminal`, adds a fragment of only those elements, with their property sets.
- [ ] A door saved alone as a fragment, without its wall, is stamped into a wall and cuts it.
- [ ] Tab-selecting two chairs inside a placed dining-set component and choosing Create Component writes a new IFC file holding only those two chairs.
- [ ] Edit Component on a placed bathroom opens its IFC file in a tab. Adding a towel rail and saving updates every placed bathroom in the open project.
- [ ] A component file written by Reviera, with its RXD removed by another tool, still opens as a model in other IFC viewers and still stamps in Reviera.

**Implementation note (2026-10-14, first build).**
- **Create Component** (`component.create`, quick menu, Modify tab, Modify | Components) collects:
  - the selection;
  - what it hosts: elements naming a member, repeatedly;
  - everything they name: hosts, types, levels and other referenced elements, all brought in rather than dropped.

  It writes them as a standalone IFC4 model through Reviera's own writer, with the base point (the selection's bottom centre) at the origin and the lowest level at 0. The file goes into the library folder shown, with a manifest entry, or to a chosen file. The model is unchanged; *Replace selection with the component* is not built yet.
- **Placing** (`component.place_fragment`; the panel's IFC thumbnails, rendered from the fragment's bodies):
  - elements are copied with new GlobalIds, every GlobalId inside their recipes rewritten;
  - levels are mapped by height above the lowest, and made when missing;
  - types are reused by GlobalId, then by class and name, and otherwise copied keeping their GlobalId;
  - elements are then turned and moved with the Modify tools' transform; openings, dormer parts and gates move with their owners.
- **Not built yet:**
  - placing as a group, so that editing changes every copy;
  - Edit Component;
  - variants;
  - Import to Library of parts of external IFC files;
  - IFC-native elements, which have no recipe to regenerate from;
  - the outside-references dialog and the type-conflict question.

### 2.8.18 Library folders and large libraries
**ID:** DM-LIB-004 · **Priority:** P1 · **Ref:** owner requirement (2026-10-14); DM-LIB-001 … 003; Reviera's own design

**Purpose.** Keep thousands of imported objects and model fragments in order. A library is a tree of nested folders of any depth. It can be browsed, searched, reorganised and shared like a well-kept file system. *(Owner requirement, 2026-10-14: "the library needs to support nested hierarchies to manage large sets of imported and model fragments".)*

**Behaviour & rules.**
- **A library is a folder that is opened.** *(Owner clarification, 2026-10-14.)*
  - **Library › Open Library** (`library.open`) opens any folder on a local disk, a network share or WebDAV as a library, the way a project file is opened.
  - Its root holds one JSON manifest, `reviera-library.json`; nothing else in the folder is Reviera's own.
  - Opening a folder that has no manifest offers to create one, or to browse it read-only with defaults.
  - Open libraries are the sources of the Library panel (DM-LIB-001), are remembered per user, and reopen at start-up.
  - **Library › New Library** creates a folder with an empty manifest.
- **Nested folders.** Within a library, items live in folders nested to any depth, for example `Furniture › Office › Chairs › Task chairs`. The tree in the Library panel shows each folder with the count of items in it and below it.
  - Folders are created, renamed, moved and deleted in the panel.
  - Items and folders are moved by drag and drop, or with Cut and Paste.
  - Deleting a folder that holds items asks for confirmation and moves them to the source's *Deleted items* folder, from which they can be restored for 30 days.
- **A library is a set of physical folders of 3D files.** *(Owner clarification, 2026-10-14.)*
  - The library's sub-directories are its folders.
  - Its items are ordinary 3D files, read where they are:
    - OBJ, with its MTL and texture files beside it;
    - STL, PLY, glTF/GLB, 3MF and OFF;
    - IFC files, whether whole models or fragments, written by Reviera or any other tool.
  - Reviera converts nothing and copies nothing into a private store. A file dropped into a library folder by any means is an item after the next refresh. The same folders can be kept in git, synced, or used by other programs.
- **The manifest** (`reviera-library.json`, in the library's root) is a JSON object:
  - `format`: `"reviera-library"`, and `version`: 1;
  - `id` (a UUID, so stamped types can find the library after it is moved or renamed), `name`, `description`, `author`, `licence` (SPDX) and `homepage`;
  - `defaults`: import options for mesh files (units, up axis, insertion point, clean-up, DM-IMP-015), the default category and the default stamp mode;
  - `folders`: settings per folder, keyed by the folder's path relative to the root. A folder inherits its parent's settings, and the entry overrides only what it names: category, import options, stamp mode, tags and thumbnail;
  - `items`: details per item, keyed by the file's path relative to the root:
    - name, tags, description and category;
    - import options, and the base point;
    - its variants (other files, or types within its file);
    - its SHA-256 and stable item GUID.
  - `smart_folders`: saved searches shared by everyone using the library.

  Every key is optional except `format` and `version`. Files with no entry use their folder's settings, then the format's defaults, so a manifest of only `format`, `version`, `id` and `name` makes any folder of 3D files a working library.
- **Writing the manifest.** Reviera updates the manifest when the user edits details, moves or renames items or folders, or adds files through the panel. Each update is an atomic replace, with keys in a stable sorted order, so the manifest diffs and merges cleanly in git. Files added or moved outside Reviera are reconciled on refresh:
  - new files get default details;
  - a moved file keeps its entry when its SHA-256 matches;
  - entries for missing files are listed and can be cleaned up.
- **Thumbnails** are rendered by Reviera and kept in the per-user cache, keyed by the file's hash, not written into library folders.
- **Folder settings** (inherited by sub-folders unless overridden):
  - default category;
  - default stamp mode (group or elements);
  - default tags;
  - a folder thumbnail, which is otherwise a mosaic of its first four items.
- **Smart folders.** A smart folder is a saved search: text plus filters over category, kind, tags, source, author, licence, size and date added. It shows matching items from anywhere, without moving them. Examples: *All plumbing fixtures*, *Added this month*, *Fragments over 2 levels*.
- **Search in a folder.** The search box searches the selected folder and everything below it, or every source; the result list shows each item's folder path.
- **Item preview and details.** *(Owner requirement, 2026-10-14: "the Library interface would have the ability to preview and edit metadata for a model that may not be possible in the format".)*
  - Selecting an item in the Library panel shows its **preview**:
    - an interactive 3D view (orbit, zoom, a plan and a front view);
    - its size in the model's units, with the item's import options applied;
    - its triangle or element count, materials, variants and levels.

    For an IFC fragment, the preview also lists its elements by category, and selecting one in the list highlights it in the preview.
  - The preview renders from the file in the library, without loading anything into the open project; the model's version is unchanged.
  - The **Details** form beside the preview edits the item's metadata. It is saved in the item's manifest entry, never in the file, so a file is never rewritten to hold what its format cannot. Examples: an STL has no units, name or materials; an OBJ has no units; a PLY has no category; and an IFC from a manufacturer may lack Reviera's tags. The fields are:
    - **Identity:** name, description, category (the IFC class it becomes, DM-IMP-015), tags, and a classification code (Uniclass, OmniClass or another system, with the code and its title).
    - **Placement:** units, up axis, insertion point and base point, default stamp mode, default rotation, and a uniform scale. Changing any of these updates the preview at once.
    - **Product:** manufacturer, model, model number or reference, URL, cost and its currency, and notes.
    - **Provenance:** author, source URL, licence (SPDX), and the date added.
    - **Materials:**
      - a name and a colour for each material slot, including the single slot of a file with no materials;
      - an optional mapping of a slot to a project material name, applied when the item is first stamped into a project.
    - **Properties:** any number of further properties (name, data type, value), grouped into property sets. They are written as `IfcPropertySet`s on the type when the item is stamped. Standard sets are offered by category, for example `Pset_ManufacturerTypeInformation` and the category's `Pset_*Common`.
    - **Thumbnail:** rendered from the preview's current view (*Use this view*) or chosen from an image file in the library. A chosen image is copied into the library folder and named in the manifest.
  - **Editing several items** at once edits the fields they share. A field whose values differ shows *(various)* and is left as it is unless typed over.
  - **Stamping uses the details.** When an item is first stamped into a project, its details become the type's name, IFC class, classification (`IfcClassificationReference`), property sets and material mapping, so the metadata reaches the model's IFC even though the source file never held it.
  - **IFC items:** values already in the IFC file are shown as read-only *from the file*. Details in the manifest add to them; a manifest value with the same name overrides the file's on stamping, and is marked as an override in the form. *Write into File* (for IFC items in a writable library) copies the details into the IFC file itself, as property sets on its types, when the user wants the file to carry them.
- **Import into Library.** *(Owner requirement, 2026-10-14: "the UI would include an import into a library: copy in a supported 3D format and adjust the manifest".)*
  - **Library › Import into Library**, or **Import…** on a folder's right-click menu, picks one or more files from anywhere: OBJ, STL, PLY, glTF/GLB, 3MF, OFF or IFC.
  - **What it does to each file:** copies it into the chosen library folder and adds its entry to the manifest. Nothing else in the library changes.
    - An OBJ brings its MTL and texture files along, keeping their relative paths.
    - A glTF brings its `.bin` and image files along.
  - **One dialog for the batch:**
    - the destination folder;
    - name, category and tags, set for all files or file by file;
    - for mesh files, the import options of DM-IMP-015: units, up axis, insertion point and clean-up. A 3D preview shows each file at its resulting size, so a wrong unit is seen before anything is copied.
  - The options are written into each file's manifest entry, so later stamps use them without asking.
  - **Dropping files from the system's file manager** onto a folder in the Library panel opens the same dialog with those files.
  - **Name clashes:** a file whose name is already used in the destination folder is renamed with a suffix. A file whose SHA-256 matches an item already in the library is reported, with the choice to skip it or to import it again.
  - **Its own undo:** Import into Library is undone from the panel (*Undo Import*), which removes the copied files and their manifest entries. It is not part of the model's undo history.
  - **Formats Reviera reads but a library does not hold**, such as STEP (DM-IMP-008), are converted on import into a supported format: IFC for solids, glTF for meshes. The original is copied beside it only when *Keep original* is ticked.
- **Existing folders.** **Add Folder as Source** adds any directory tree of 3D files as a source as it is. It is indexed in the background, with progress, and its folder structure is the library tree. **Copy Folder into Library** copies a directory tree into a folder of an existing source instead. Both end with a report:
  - files read;
  - files unreadable, with the reason;
  - duplicates, by SHA-256.

  Import options (units, up axis, category) can be set for a whole folder at once; they are saved in the manifest's `folders` entry.
- **Bulk edits.** Several selected items can be moved, tagged, re-categorised or deleted together.
- **Scale.** Loading is lazy, so the panel stays responsive with large libraries:
  - the tree loads folders as they are expanded;
  - thumbnails load as they scroll into view;
  - the index (DM-LIB-001) covers every folder.

  A source of 50,000 items in 2,000 folders opens its tree in under 1 s once indexed, and a search over it returns in under 200 ms.
- **Organisation libraries (P2).** A remote library is the same folder layout served over HTTPS or WebDAV. Its `reviera-library.json` doubles as the index of DM-LIB-001: each item's entry carries its SHA-256, so downloads are verified. The same tree appears for everyone. Remote libraries are read-only. Items are added through the organisation's own process: a git pull request, or a write-enabled WebDAV folder (DM-FILE-007).
- **Project Library.** The Project Library source lists the types, families and group types already in the open project, in the same tree form: by category, or by the folder they were stamped from.

**Data (storage).** A library is its directories and files, plus `reviera-library.json` in its root, Reviera's only file there. The search index and thumbnails are per-user caches (DM-LIB-001), rebuilt when missing. Smart folders, favourites and pinned stamps are per-user settings. No model data.

**Commands.**
`library.open(path) -> library_id` · `library.create(path, name) -> library_id` · `library.close(library_id)` ·
`library.folder.create(library_id, path) -> folder_ref` ·
`library.folder.rename(folder_ref, name)` ·
`library.folder.delete(folder_ref)` ·
`library.move(item_or_folder_refs[], to_folder_ref)` ·
`library.list(folder_ref, recursive?: bool, offset?, limit?) -> {folders[], items[]}` *(query)* ·
`library.smart_folder.save(name, query) -> smart_folder_id` ·
`library.import_files(paths[], to_folder_ref, options?: {name?, category?, tags?, units?, up_axis?, insertion?, cleanup?, per_file?, on_duplicate?: "skip"|"import", keep_original?}) -> {item_refs[], report}` ·
`library.undo_import(import_id)` ·
`library.source.add(path)` (DM-LIB-001) adds a folder as a source · `library.copy_folder(path, to_folder_ref, options?) -> job_id` ·
`library.get_meta(item_ref) -> {details, from_file, overrides}` *(query)* ·
`library.set_meta(item_or_folder_refs[], {name?, description?, category?, tags?, classification?, placement?, product?, provenance?, materials?, properties?, thumbnail?, settings?})` ·
`library.preview(item_ref, view?: "3d"|"plan"|"front", size?) -> image` *(query)* ·
`library.write_meta_to_file(item_ref)` (IFC items only) ·
`library.restore_deleted(item_refs[])`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- [ ] A directory of 3,000 OBJ, STL, glTF and IFC files in 120 nested folders, added with Add Folder as Source, appears as the same tree with item counts per folder, with no file in it changed or added. Duplicates are reported.
- [ ] An OBJ file copied into a library folder with a file manager can be stamped after Refresh, using its folder's import options.
- [ ] Import into Library of a chair OBJ, with its MTL and two textures, into `Furniture › Chairs` (units cm) copies all four files there. The manifest gains one entry, with `units: "cm"`. The chair then stamps at its real size without a dialog.
- [ ] An STL in a library is given, in its Details, the name "Planter", category Planting, units mm, manufacturer and model, and a `Pset_ManufacturerTypeInformation`. The STL file's bytes are unchanged, and the details are in the manifest. Stamped into a project, the type is an `IfcGeographicElementType` named "Planter" carrying that property set in the saved IFC.
- [ ] Changing an item's units from mm to cm in Details shows it ten times larger in the preview at once.
- [ ] Selecting a manufacturer's IFC item shows its own property values as read-only *from the file*; a manifest value of the same name is marked as an override and wins when stamped.
- [ ] Dropping three glTF files from the file manager onto a library folder opens the import dialog for the three. Undo Import afterwards removes the files and their manifest entries.
- [ ] Dragging the folder `Chairs` from `Furniture › Office` to `Furniture › Lounge` moves its items on disk, and stamps already placed in projects still find their item (by GUID).
- [ ] A search for "basin" in `Plumbing` returns only items under `Plumbing`, each shown with its folder path.
- [ ] A smart folder *Fragments over 2 levels* lists every matching fragment across all sources.
- [ ] A folder added to the library directory by a file manager appears in the panel after Refresh.
- [ ] A deleted folder's items can be restored from *Deleted items* the next day.
- [ ] Library › Open Library on a folder of 3D files with no manifest offers to create one; the created `reviera-library.json` holds only `format`, `version`, `id` and `name`, and every file in the folder is usable.
- [ ] Moving a library folder to another disk and opening it there keeps every item's details, and stamped types in projects still find the library by its `id`.

**Implementation note (2026-10-14, first build).**
- **Built:** the manifest, folders and settings, listing, Import into Library (with companions, duplicates by SHA-256 and free names), item details, delete and restore through `.deleted`, and the panel.
- **The panel:** docked on the right (Window › Component Library, CL), it lists the open libraries (kept per user in `libraries.json`; the sample library is offered at first), shows folders with counts, and shows items as thumbnails.
- **Thumbnails:** rendered offscreen and cached per user by file, date, size and import options.
- **The sample library:** `test-data/library` ships beside the samples in every package.
- **Not built yet:** smart folders, moving and renaming in the panel, drag and drop, search, bulk edits and organisation libraries.

### 2.8.19 A familiar workflow, in Reviera's own words
**ID:** DM-LIB-005 · **Priority:** P1 · **Ref:** owner requirement (2026-10-14); research/06 (the reference product's family UI and workflow); DM-LIB-001 … 004

**Purpose.** Users who know the reference product's families should find components familiar: the same gestures, places and sequence. Reviera keeps its own names and its own model of libraries as folders of ordinary files. *(Owner requirements, 2026-10-14: "not called Families; our term will be Component Libraries"; "differentiate, but be familiar to users with a Revit background"; "stamps just means a quick and easy mechanism to add library items, like a stamp in GIMP".)*

**Behaviour & rules.**
- **Names.** The feature is **Component Libraries** and its items **components**; the reference product's term is not used in Reviera's interface or help. A component's variants are its **types**.
- **The same gestures where they fit.** The reference product's patterns (research/06) map onto Reviera like this:

| What users know (research/06) | In Reviera |
|---|---|
| Architecture › Component › Place a Component, shortcut CM; places until Esc; Spacebar turns 90° | Architecture › Component › **Component**, shortcut **CM**; places until Esc; Spacebar turns 90° (DM-LIB-002) |
| Load Family (a file dialog with a preview), then place | The **Component Library** panel: folders and thumbnails; a click picks a component up and places it. Loading happens on the first copy, and the panel stays open. |
| Load Autodesk Family (a cloud content browser with a tree, search and preview) | The same panel, over folders on disk, a share or WebDAV, with organisation libraries later (DM-LIB-001, DM-LIB-004) |
| Library locations set in Options (Places) | Libraries opened in the panel (Open…, New…), remembered per user |
| Type catalogs and Specify Types | Variants in the manifest (DM-LIB-003) |
| Type Selector and Properties during placement | Properties during Place Component: the component, its details, rotation, mirror and offset |
| Edit Family, then Load into Project (and Close); Family Already Exists: overwrite, or overwrite with parameter values | **Edit Component**, then Save, which updates placed copies; a type conflict asks *Use project's*, *Use library's* or *Keep both* (DM-LIB-003) |
| Save As › Library › Family; Save Group and Load as Group for repeated layouts | **Create Component** from any selection, written as an IFC file (DM-LIB-003) |
| Thumbnails taken from the view saved last | Thumbnails rendered by Reviera from the file, cached per user (DM-LIB-004) |
| Project Browser › Families: category, family, type; drag a type into a view | The Model Tree and Project Browser list placed components and types; dragging a type from the browser is P2 |

- **Where Reviera differs, on purpose:**
  - libraries are plain folders of open 3D files and IFC, readable by other tools;
  - any selection becomes a component, as an IFC file;
  - placing is stamp-like, from a thumbnail palette, with no separate load step;
  - components can be arrayed along paths parametrically (ARC-MOD-033).

**Acceptance criteria.**
- [x] CM starts Place Component, which places copies until Esc; Spacebar turns the next copy 90°. *(Built 2026-10-14.)*
- [x] The Component Library panel shows a library's folders and thumbnails; clicking a component starts placing it. *(Built 2026-10-14.)*
- [ ] Neither the interface nor the help uses the word "family" for components.
- [ ] Edit Component on a placed copy opens its IFC file; saving updates the copies in the open model.

## 2.9 Parameters and units

### 2.9.1 Kinds of parameters
**ID:** DM-PARAM-001 · **Priority:** P0 (built-in, project) / P1 (family, shared, global) · **Ref:** research/05 §7.1, §7.6

**Purpose.** Parameters carry all element data. This section defines their kinds and how each kind is identified.

**Behaviour & rules.**

| Kind | Defined in | Identity | Schedulable / taggable | Typical use |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Built-in** | The application's parameter registry | Stable key (for example `wall.base_offset`) with a negative internal ID | Mostly yes | Mark, Comments, Level, Base Offset, Area, Volume, Fire Rating |
| **Family** | A family definition | Name, unique within the family | **No** | Driving geometry and formulas inside a family |
| **Shared** | A **parameter library** (§2.9.7) | **GUID** | Yes, including tags and title blocks | Firm-wide data fields used in families and projects |
| **Project** | The project, bound to categories | Name (if local) or GUID (if shared) | Schedules yes. Tags only if shared. | Project-specific data on many categories |
| **Global** | The project | GUID of the global parameter | Not directly (they can be shown through calculated values) | Driving dimensions and values project-wide |
| **Key schedule** | A key schedule (DOC) | Name | Yes | Pick-list values that set several parameters at once |
| **IFC-native** | A third-party IFC file | (`Pset name`, `property name`) | Yes | Properties Reviera found in imported files that do not match any definition |

- Every parameter value is either a **type** value (stored on the type) or an **instance** value (stored on the instance). The definition's binding decides which (§2.9.3). It is never both.
- **Read-only computed parameters** (Area, Volume, Length, Perimeter, Count, Host, Room) are produced by regeneration. They are shown greyed out, and commands that try to set them fail with a clear error.
- **IFC-native parameters.** When Reviera opens an IFC file, every property that does not match a built-in, shared or project definition becomes an *IFC-native parameter*. It is shown in Properties under its property-set name, can be edited and scheduled, and is written back to the same property set. The user can **promote** one to a project or shared parameter. Promotion keeps the values and adds a definition.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- [ ] A third-party IFC file with a custom property set `ACME_Asset` (property `AssetTag`) shows `AssetTag` in Properties and in the schedule field list. Edits are written back to `ACME_Asset.AssetTag`.

### 2.9.2 Parameter definitions
**ID:** DM-PARAM-002 · **Priority:** P0 · **Ref:** research/05 §7.1, §7.7, §16.3

**Purpose.** Parameter definitions are first-class objects with a fixed set of fields.

**Behaviour & rules.** A parameter definition shall have these fields:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `id` | Internal ID |
| `guid` | Required for shared, global and project parameters. Built-in parameters use their key. |
| `name` | Display name (unique among the definitions bound to a category) |
| `data_type` | A data-type key (§2.9.4), for example `length`, `yes_no`, `family_type:cat.doors` |
| `group` | A parameter group key (below) |
| `discipline` | `common`, `structural`, `hvac`, `electrical`, `piping`, `energy`, `infrastructure` |
| `tooltip` | Up to 500 characters |
| `visible` | Hidden parameters are kept but not shown (for add-in use) |
| `user_modifiable` | If false, only code can change values |
| `hide_when_no_value` | Hidden in Properties when empty |
| `min` / `max` | Optional range (numeric types) |
| `enum` | Optional allowed-values list (text and integer types). Written to IFC as `IfcPropertyEnumeration`. |
| `ifc_home` | Property-set name and property name (and, for built-in parameters, an IFC attribute) used to store the value (§2.3.3) |
| `formula` | Family and global parameters only |
| `reporting` | Family and global parameters only |

- **Parameter groups** (the "group under" list; keys are stable and display names are localisable): `analysis_results`, `analytical_model`, `constraints`, `construction`, `data`, `dimensions`, `division_geometry`, `electrical`, `electrical_circuiting`, `electrical_lighting`, `electrical_loads`, `electrical_analysis`, `energy_analysis`, `fire_protection`, `forces`, `general`, `graphics`, `green_building`, `identity_data`, `ifc_parameters`, `layers`, `materials_and_finishes`, `mechanical`, `mechanical_flow`, `mechanical_loads`, `model_properties`, `moments`, `other`, `phasing`, `photometrics`, `plumbing`, `primary_end`, `rebar_set`, `releases_member_forces`, `secondary_end`, `segments_and_fittings`, `set`, `slab_shape_edit`, `structural`, `structural_analysis`, `text`, `title_text`, `visibility`, `carbon` (Reviera addition).
- **Default IFC home** for user parameters: a property set named by the binding's configured *property-set name*. The default is `<Project or Library name> Parameters`, for example "ACME Parameters". Parameters may be given a specific property set name and property name, so that they map onto a buildingSMART property (for example a shared parameter "Acoustic Rating" mapped to `Pset_WallCommon.AcousticRating` for walls and `Pset_DoorCommon.AcousticRating` for doors). The IFC home can differ per bound category.
- **No collisions.** Built-in parameters keep their established names and their IFC homes (for example built-in Fire Rating owns `Pset_<Class>Common.FireRating`). A user parameter may not take a built-in's name for a bound category (§2.9.3), and may not be mapped onto an IFC home that a built-in or another parameter already uses for that category (`param.home_clash`). User parameters that map onto a standard property are named after that property, as above.
- **Built-in parameter registry.** The application ships a registry of built-in parameters: key, name, data type, group, the categories it applies to, type/instance, read-only flag and IFC home. Domain chapters add rows. Examples:

| Key | Name | Data type | Type/Instance | IFC home |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `elem.mark` | Mark | `text` | Instance | `IfcElement.Tag` |
| `elem.comments` | Comments | `text` | Instance | group-named set `Identity Data`.`Comments` (§2.3.3) |
| `type.type_mark` | Type Mark | `text` | Type | `IfcTypeProduct.Tag` |
| `type.description` | Description | `text` | Type | `IfcRoot.Description` (type) |
| `type.fire_rating` | Fire Rating | `text` | Type | `Pset_<Class>Common.FireRating` |
| `type.manufacturer` | Manufacturer | `text` | Type | `Pset_ManufacturerTypeInformation.Manufacturer` |
| `type.model` | Model | `text` | Type | `Pset_ManufacturerTypeInformation.ModelLabel` |
| `type.cost` | Cost | `currency` | Type | `Identity Data`.`Cost` (`IfcMonetaryMeasure`) |
| `type.classification_code` | Classification Code | `text` | Type | `IfcClassificationReference.Identification` |
| `type.keynote` | Keynote | `text` | Type | `Identity Data`.`Keynote` |
| `elem.level` | Level | `element:level` | Instance | Spatial containment |
| `elem.phase_created` | Phase Created | `element:phase` | Instance | RXD element data `phasing` |
| `wall.base_offset` | Base Offset | `length` | Instance | RXD element data `constraints` (and the evaluated geometry) |
| `wall.unconnected_height` | Unconnected Height | `length` | Instance | `Qto_WallBaseQuantities.Height` (as a derived value) + RXD |
| `door.width` | Width | `length` | Type | `IfcDoor.OverallWidth` (instance attribute, written from the type) + `IfcDoorType` property |

**Commands.** `param.definition(param_ref) -> definition` · `param.list(category?, element_id?) -> definition[]` · `param.set_ifc_home(param_ref, category?, pset_name, property_name)`

**Acceptance criteria.**
- [ ] Mapping a shared parameter "Acoustic Rating" to `Pset_WallCommon.AcousticRating` for walls and to `Pset_DoorCommon.AcousticRating` for doors writes each value to the right standard property set.
- [ ] Mapping a project parameter onto `Pset_WallCommon.FireRating` for walls is refused with `param.home_clash`, naming built-in Fire Rating.
- [ ] `param.list("cat.walls")` returns every built-in, project and shared parameter bound to walls, with its data type and IFC home.

### 2.9.3 Project parameters and category bindings
**ID:** DM-PARAM-003 · **Priority:** P0 · **Ref:** research/05 §7.3, §7.6; screenshots/platform/parameter_properties_shared_project_parameter.png, screenshots/platform/manage_tab_settings_panel.png

**Purpose.** To add data fields to project elements by category.

**Workflow.**
1. Manage › Settings › **Project Parameters**. The list is sorted A–Z and has a search field.
2. **Add**: choose *Project parameter* (enter name, data type, group) or *Shared parameter* (pick from the parameter library). Choose **Type** or **Instance**. For instance parameters, choose **Values aligned per group type** or **Values can vary by group instance**. Choose the categories on the right (a filterable tree with *Check all* / *Check none*, and *Hide unchecked*). Optionally set the IFC property-set name.
3. **OK**. Every existing element in the chosen categories gets the parameter, with no value.
4. **Modify** changes the binding (categories, group, IFC home). **Remove** deletes the definition and all its values, after a confirmation that shows how many values will be lost.

**Behaviour & rules.**
- A binding is (definition, categories, type or instance, group behaviour). A definition can have only one binding in a project.
- Changing a binding from instance to type (or back) is allowed. Reviera asks how to resolve values that differ between instances of the same type (take the most common value, take the first value, or clear). The resolution is reported.
- Parameters can also be created from the schedule-field dialog (DOC) and from the Family Types dialog (as family parameters). Those are the same definitions.
- A project or shared parameter with the same name as a built-in parameter of a bound category is refused; built-in names follow established convention and take precedence (§2.9.2, *No collisions*).
- **Project Parameters dialog** (`param.project.manage()`). The list shows every project and shared parameter binding with Name, Data type, Type/Instance, Group, Categories (count, with the list in a tooltip), Source (Project, or the library name for shared ones) and IFC property set. Buttons: **Add**, **Modify**, **Remove** and **Duplicate** (copies a project parameter's definition and binding under a new name and GUID, without values; it is `param.project.add` with the copied definition). A search field filters by name, and a drop-down filters by category.
  - The **Parameter Properties** sub-dialog validates before OK is enabled: a name is required, at most 255 characters, unique among definitions bound to any of the chosen categories, and free of `[ ] { } | ; < >` (characters reserved by formulas and naming rules); a data type is required; at least one category must be ticked; a property-set name, if given, must not start with `Pset_` or `Qto_` unless it maps onto that standard set's existing property (§2.9.2), and must not start with `Reviera_`.
  - Changes made in the dialog (several adds, modifies and removes) are applied together on **OK** as one transaction named "Project Parameters"; **Cancel** discards them.
  - Removing a binding used by schedules, filters, tags, view templates or formulas lists those uses first.

**Data (storage).** Definitions and bindings: RXD document `standards/parameters`. Values: IFC property sets (§2.3.3).

**Commands.**
`param.project.add(def, categories[], is_instance, group_behavior: "aligned"|"vary", pset_name?) -> param_id` ·
`param.project.modify(param_id, changes)` ·
`param.project.remove(param_id)` ·
`param.get(element_id, param_ref) -> value` ·
`param.set(element_ids[], param_ref, value)` ·
`param.set_many(changes: [{element_id, param_ref, value}])` ·
`param.clear(element_ids[], param_ref)` ·
`param.project.manage()` (opens the Project Parameters dialog)

**Acceptance criteria.**
- [ ] In the Project Parameters dialog, adding "Fire Rating" bound to Doors (where a built-in Fire Rating exists) is refused with the clash named, and OK stays disabled until the name is changed.
- [ ] Adding an instance text parameter "Room Finish Code" to Rooms and Areas makes it appear in both categories' Properties and schedules, and in IFC under the configured property set.
- [ ] Changing a parameter from instance to type, when instances of the same type disagree, shows the resolution dialog and applies the choice.
- [ ] `param.set` on a read-only computed parameter fails with error `param.read_only`.

### 2.9.4 Data types and IFC measure types
**ID:** DM-PARAM-004 · **Priority:** P0 (common) / P1 (discipline types) · **Ref:** research/05 §7.7, §8

**Purpose.** A fixed, versioned catalogue of data types. Each type maps to an IFC measure type and an SI internal unit.

**Behaviour & rules.**
- Each data type has a **key** (for example `length`) and a **versioned ID** (`reviera:spec/length@1`). Keys are used in formulas, tables and APIs. Versioned IDs are stored in RXD, so that a future change in meaning can be migrated.
- The catalogue (normative baseline; domain chapters may add types, but not change existing ones):

| Key | Discipline | Storage | IFC value type | SI internal unit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | common | string | `IfcLabel` (≤ 255 chars) or `IfcText` | — |
| `multiline_text` | common | string | `IfcText` | — |
| `integer` | common | i64 | `IfcInteger` | — |
| `number` | common | f64 | `IfcReal` | — |
| `yes_no` | common | bool | `IfcBoolean` | — |
| `url` | common | string | `IfcURIReference` | — |
| `date` / `datetime` | common | ISO 8601 | `IfcDate` / `IfcDateTime` | — |
| `length` | common | f64 | `IfcLengthMeasure` (`IfcPositiveLengthMeasure` when `min > 0`) | m |
| `distance` | common | f64 | `IfcLengthMeasure` | m |
| `area` | common | f64 | `IfcAreaMeasure` | m² |
| `volume` | common | f64 | `IfcVolumeMeasure` | m³ |
| `angle` | common | f64 | `IfcPlaneAngleMeasure` | rad |
| `rotation_angle` | common | f64 | `IfcPlaneAngleMeasure` | rad |
| `slope` | common | f64 | `IfcRatioMeasure` (rise/run) | — |
| `ratio` / `percentage` | common | f64 | `IfcRatioMeasure` / `IfcPositiveRatioMeasure` | — |
| `currency` | common | f64 | `IfcMonetaryMeasure` (with `IfcMonetaryUnit` from project currency) | currency unit |
| `mass` | common | f64 | `IfcMassMeasure` | kg |
| `mass_density` | common | f64 | `IfcMassDensityMeasure` | kg/m³ |
| `mass_per_length` | common | f64 | `IfcMassPerLengthMeasure` | kg/m |
| `time` | common | f64 | `IfcTimeMeasure` | s |
| `duration` | common | ISO 8601 | `IfcDuration` | — |
| `speed` | common | f64 | `IfcLinearVelocityMeasure` | m/s |
| `cost_per_area` | common | f64 | `IfcReal` + unit in the template (no IFC measure) | currency/m² |
| `material` | common | element ref | `IfcPropertyReferenceValue` → `IfcMaterial` | — |
| `image` | common | asset ref | `IfcPropertyReferenceValue` → `IfcImageTexture` / `IfcURIReference` | — |
| `fill_pattern` | common | element ref | `IfcLabel` (pattern name) | — |

| `element:<kind>` | common | element ref | `IfcPropertyReferenceValue` → `IfcObjectDefinition` / `IfcLabel` GUID | — |
| `load_classification` | electrical | element ref | `IfcLabel` | — |
| `force` | structural | f64 | `IfcForceMeasure` | N |
| `linear_force` | structural | f64 | `IfcLinearForceMeasure` | N/m |
| `area_force` | structural | f64 | `IfcPlanarForceMeasure` | N/m² |
| `moment` | structural | f64 | `IfcTorqueMeasure` | N·m |
| `linear_moment` | structural | f64 | `IfcLinearMomentMeasure` | N·m/m |

| `unit_weight` | structural | f64 | `IfcReal` (no IFC measure) | N/m³ |
| `thermal_expansion` | structural | f64 | `IfcThermalExpansionCoefficientMeasure` | 1/K |
| `section_area` / `section_modulus` / `moment_of_inertia` / `warping_constant` | structural | f64 | `IfcAreaMeasure` / `IfcSectionModulusMeasure` / `IfcMomentOfInertiaMeasure` / `IfcWarpingConstantMeasure` | m² / m³ / m⁴ / m⁶ |
| `point_spring` / `line_spring` / `area_spring` / `rotational_spring` | structural | f64 | `IfcLinearStiffnessMeasure` / `IfcModulusOfLinearSubgradeReactionMeasure` / `IfcModulusOfSubgradeReactionMeasure` / `IfcRotationalStiffnessMeasure` | N/m, N/m², N/m³, N·m/rad |
| `acceleration` | structural | f64 | `IfcAccelerationMeasure` | m/s² |
| `frequency` | structural/electrical | f64 | `IfcFrequencyMeasure` | Hz |
| `temperature` | hvac/piping | f64 | `IfcThermodynamicTemperatureMeasure` | K |
