Stored on the project as `rxd:structural_settings`. Keys: brace and kicker symbols (parallel line or none) and the brace offset, the coarse cutback, point-to-point steel (steel members are not shortened at joins, STR-BEAM-003's switch), the three analytical checks and the consistency criteria (C1–C8, C1–C7 on by default; circular support references on by default), the four tolerances, boundary condition spacing, the four load display scales and load labels. Structure › Structural Settings opens one dialog of all pages; OK applies them in one step (`structural_settings.show` is the window's action). In Coarse plans (DOC-GFX-010) beams, braces and truss members are drawn as single lines along their location lines, less the coarse cutback at joined ends, braces with their symbol; their bodies are not drawn. Not yet: the connection and boundary condition symbol families, vertical brace symbols above and below the cut, the load case summaries, Reset page and the template-default markers, and Coarse section views. The checks themselves are built (STR-AM-007, 2026-10-16).

### 4.1.14 Section catalogues, materials and regional standards
**ID:** STR-SEC-001 · **Priority:** P1 · **Ref:** research/08 (S0720–S0822)

**Purpose.** Structural types start from the standard sections, materials and design standards that apply where the building is, so users pick a W10X49 in Chicago, an HEB 300 in Munich or a 254 x 254 x 73 UC in Leeds without typing dimensions.

**Behaviour & rules.**
- Reviera ships open **section catalogues** as data files, one per family and standard: AISC W, C, L, WT, rectangular and round HSS and standard pipe (ASTM A6, A500, A53); Euronorm IPE, HEA and HEB (EN 10365); UK UB and UC (BS 4-1). Each lists nominal dimensions only (depth, flange width, web and flange thickness; or height, width and wall; or outside diameter and wall), with its standard, units, shape, default material and sources. Reviera computes area, second moments and radii of gyration from the outline (root fillets are left out, so values are slightly below published ones). Catalogues are small factual subsets; publishers' property tables are not copied.
- The **region** follows the model's building code (§1.x code settings): United States (IBC/IRC), Canada (NBC), Europe (DIN and custom codes), United Kingdom (Approved Documents) or Australia (NCC). It sets the preferred catalogues (listed first), the default steel grade and concrete class (for example ASTM A992 and f'c 4000 psi; S355 and C30/37; CSA 350W and 30 MPa; 300PLUS and 32 MPa), and the design standards named for loads, steel, concrete and timber (ASCE/SEI 7, AISC 360, ACI 318, NDS; NBC, CSA S16, A23.3, O86; EN 1990–1995; AS/NZS 1170, AS 4100, AS 3600, AS 1720.1).
- *Load Section* makes a structural column type from a catalogue designation, named for it, with the catalogue's default material unless another is given. Loading the same designation and material again reuses the type.
- **Advisory checks** (`column.check`) report slenderness against simple code limits: steel KL/r above 200 (AISC 360 user note), concrete k·lu/r above 22 for unbraced columns in the US and Canada (ACI 318), and the slenderness λ for Eurocode regions (EN 1992-1-1 §5.8.3.1, whose limit needs the design load). They are prompts for the engineer, not design checks; design checks belong to analysis providers (§4.0.2a).

**Data.** Catalogues are compiled into Reviera (`crates/reviera-core/data/sections/*.json`, with a provenance README). Types record their catalogue designation and material on the `recipe.column_type`; IFC carries the material name.

**Commands.**
- `structural.catalogs(catalog?) -> [{id, family, standard, units, shape, default_material, preferred, designations[]}]`
- `structural.standards() -> {region, catalogs[], steel, concrete, loads, steel_standard, concrete_standard, timber_standard}`
- `column.load_section(catalog, designation, material?) -> type_id`
- `column.check(column_ids?) -> [{column_id, length, slenderness, limit?, note}]`

**Acceptance criteria.**
- [x] Every catalogue section makes a valid type; HEB 300 and W8X24 have their published dimensions, and HEB 300's computed Ix is within 5 % of the published value.
- [x] A US model lists the AISC catalogues first and loads W shapes in ASTM A992; a DIN model lists HEB, HEA and IPE first with S355 and C30/37.
- [x] In a US model a Pipe 2 STD column 12 m tall exceeds KL/r 200 and a W10X49 4 m tall does not; a 400 × 400 concrete column 12 m tall exceeds k·lu/r 22. In a DIN model the same column reports λ with no limit, citing EN 1992-1-1.
- [x] Timber sections (NIST PS 20 dressed sizes, EN 336 sizes) in the region's timber grade, and a materials library with strengths (steel grades, concrete classes, NDS, EN 338 and EN 14080 timber).

*Built (2026-10-16), timber and materials:* sawn lumber (`na_lumber`, PS 20 dry dressed sizes, 26) and EN 336 timber (`eu_timber`, 42) catalogues of rectangular wood sections; a timber section takes the region's timber grade (Douglas Fir-Larch No.2 in the US, Spruce-Pine-Fir No.1/No.2 in Canada, C24 in Europe, the UK and Australia). `structural.materials` lists the library (`data/materials.json`: 35 steel grades, concrete classes and timber grades with their key values in MPa and kg/m³ and their sources), the region's first; every region's default steel, concrete and timber is in it. Properties show a section type's material strength and modulus. `column.check` applies le/d not over 50 to timber in US and Canadian models (NDS 3.7.1.4; CSA O86) and reports λ elsewhere.

---

## 4.2 Reinforcement (rebar)

Every reinforcement feature in this section is **P2**, as the priority tiers require, unless stated otherwise. Rebar tools live on the **Concrete** tab. They also appear on the contextual tab of any selected valid host.

### 4.2.1 Rebar hosts
**ID:** STR-RBR-001 · **Priority:** P2 · **Ref:** research/03 §3.1

**Purpose.** Decide which elements can contain reinforcement.

**Behaviour & rules.**
- **Valid hosts:** structural framing, structural columns, foundations, structural connections, floors, walls, foundation slabs, wall foundations, slab edges and parts cut from concrete walls or floors.
- Generic-model families become valid hosts when their family flag *Can Host Rebar* is set.
- **Material condition:** the host material's *model behaviour* must be Concrete or Precast Concrete. Walls and floors must also be structural and contain a concrete layer.
- If a host stops qualifying, its rebar is kept but flagged as **orphaned**, with a warning. A host can stop qualifying through a material change or through becoming non-structural. The user can re-host the rebar or delete it.
- Rebar shall never be silently deleted, except when its host is deleted. In that case the delete cascades and the count is shown in the confirmation.

**Data (IFC mapping).** Rebar elements are related to their host with `IfcRelAggregates`, where the host is the whole and the reinforcement is a part. The IFC4 reference-view convention also accepts `IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure`. Reviera writes `IfcRelAggregates` and also records the host GlobalId in RXD element data (`rebar`), so that the link survives round trips through tools that drop aggregates. Host eligibility is computed and is not stored.

**Commands.** `rebar.can_host(element_id) -> bool`, `rebar.rehost(rebar_ids[], host_id)`

**Acceptance criteria.**
- [ ] A floor whose concrete layer is changed to timber flags its rebar as orphaned and keeps it in place.
- [x] Deleting a host column with 3 rebar sets shows "3 reinforcement elements will be deleted" and removes them in the same transaction.

*Built (2026-10-19), first milestone:* `rebar.can_host` (with the host kind, the reason it cannot, and each face's cover type) and `rebar.rehost`. Hosts are structural concrete columns (material kind concrete or precast concrete) and concrete beams, structural floors and structural (bearing, shear or combined) walls whose type has a concrete layer; a generic type's structure layer with no material named counts as concrete. A set whose host stops qualifying is kept, and `rebar.info` reports it orphaned with the reason; deleting the host deletes its sets in the same step, and the delete confirmation counts them under *Structural Rebar*. IFC: each host aggregates its sets (`IfcRelAggregates`, `rxd:rebar`), and the set's recipe keeps the host's GlobalId. Not yet: foundations, connections, slab edges, parts, Component Library components with *Can Host Rebar*, braces, the orphan warning in the warnings list.

### 4.2.2 Reinforcement settings, rounding and cover
**ID:** STR-RBR-002 · **Priority:** P2 · **Ref:** research/03 §3.1

**Purpose.** Project-level rules for reinforcement.

**Behaviour & rules.**
- **Area and path reinforcement produce real rebar** (one mode per project).
  - When the mode is on, area and path systems generate individual rebar sets. These can be scheduled and edited, and they survive removal of the system.
  - When it is off, the bars are internal to the system.
  - The mode is **locked** once any area or path system exists.
- **Hooks in shape definition** (on or off). This must be decided before the first rebar is placed and is then locked.
- **Presentation defaults** for new sets, and abbreviations for area and path tags.
- **Rounding:** on or off. Method is Nearest, Up or Down. Separate increments apply to bar length, segment length and fabric-sheet dimensions. Bar types can override the project rounding.
- The Properties palette shows rounded values as "exact [rounded]".
- **Cover:** *Cover* tool. Pick elements or faces, then choose a named **cover setting**. The *Cover Settings* dialog creates, duplicates and deletes named cover types with offsets. Each host face stores its cover type, so cover can differ per face.

**UI: Reinforcement Settings dialog** (*Concrete › Settings › Reinforcement Settings*, `reinforcement_settings.show()`). A tree dialog with four pages; *OK* commits all pages as one transaction.
- **General:** *Area and path reinforcement produce rebar* and *Include hooks in shape definition*. Each is greyed out, with the reason in a tooltip, once it is locked (an area or path system exists; any rebar exists).
- **Presentation:** default set presentation for new sets in plan, section and 3D views (Show All, First/Last, Middle), and the default for spliced sets.
- **Abbreviations:** tag abbreviations for area and path reinforcement layers (for example "T1", "B2", "EF") and for the direction labels. Each abbreviation 1–8 characters, unique per layer.
- **Rounding:** on or off; method (Nearest, Up, Down); increments for bar length, segment length and fabric-sheet dimensions (default 1 mm, 5 mm and 5 mm). Increments must be > 0 and ≤ 100 mm. Bar types with their own rounding are listed read-only with a link to the type.

**UI: Rebar Cover Settings dialog** (*Concrete › Settings › Cover Settings*, `rebar_cover_type.manage()`). A grid with one row per cover type: name, offset and a usage count (how many host faces use it).
- *Add* creates a row named "New cover N" with offset 25 mm; *Duplicate* copies the selected row; *Delete* is allowed only for unused types, or after picking a replacement type that all its faces are moved to.
- Names must be unique and non-empty. Offsets must be ≥ 0 and ≤ 500 mm. Changing an offset regenerates every rebar constrained to faces using that type, and the dialog states how many hosts will update before *OK*.
- New projects get the template's cover types; a project always has at least one.

**Data (IFC mapping).**
No IFC equivalent.
- **RXD document** `rebar`: settings (HostRebarInAreaPath, HooksInShape, Rounding.*, Presentation.*) and the cover-type table (name, offset).
- **RXD element data** (`rebar`) on each host: per-face cover assignments (Top, Bottom, Exterior, Interior, Other as cover-type references, with per-face overrides keyed by stable face IDs).

**Commands.**
- `reinforcement_settings.set(key, value)`
- `reinforcement_settings.show()`
- `rebar_cover_type.create(name, offset) -> id`
- `rebar_cover_type.manage()`
- `rebar_cover.assign(host_id, face_ref? , cover_type_id)`

**Acceptance criteria.**
- [x] With Nearest/10 mm rounding, a computed bar length of 2 437 mm displays as "2437 [2440]", and schedules use 2 440 mm.
- [x] Trying to change the area/path mode after an area system exists is refused, with an explanation.
- [x] Deleting a cover type used by 12 faces asks for a replacement type; after *OK* the 12 faces use the replacement and their rebar regenerates in the same transaction.
- [x] Changing the offset of cover type "Interior 25" to 30 mm moves every bar constrained to faces of that type by 5 mm.

*Built (2026-10-19):* `reinforcement_settings.get` (with each cover type's uses and the locked settings) and `reinforcement_settings.set` (rounding on, method, bar and segment increments above 0 and at most 100 mm; hooks in shape definitions, locked once rebar is placed; the area and path mode). `rebar_cover_type.create`, `.set` (name, offset 0–500 mm) and `.delete` (refused with the use count unless a replacement is given; returns the faces moved; a project keeps at least one), and `rebar_cover.assign` (one face or all). The settings and cover types are kept on the project (`rxd:rebar`); each host's face assignments in `rxd:rebar_cover`, defaulting by the host's kind (columns and beams *Beams and columns*, floors *Interior*, walls *Exterior* outside and *Interior* elsewhere; 35/25/40/75 mm, or 1 1/2"/3/4"/2"/3" in US models). `rebar.info` gives each bar's exact and rounded length and the first as "exact [rounded]". Concrete › Settings › **Reinforcement Settings** (rounding, hooks, and the cover types as editable `name = mm` lines with their uses) and Concrete › **Cover** (faces, then a cover type). Not yet: presentation defaults, abbreviations, fabric-sheet rounding, per-bar-type rounding, per-face overrides by face id, the grid-style Cover Settings dialog with Duplicate.

### 4.2.3 Standard (shape-driven) rebar placement
**ID:** STR-RBR-003 · **Priority:** P2 · **Ref:** research/03 §3.2

**Purpose.** Place planar or multi-planar bars from a library of shape families into a host.

**Workflow.**
1. Choose *Concrete › Rebar*, or pick it from a selected host's contextual tab.
2. Pick a shape on the contextual tab or in the **Shape Browser** palette (thumbnails of the loaded shapes).
3. Choose a **placement method**:
   - **Expand to Host:** the shape stretches to fill the host's cover box in the placement plane.
   - **By Two Points:** draw a rectangle, aligned to the view or to a picked reference, that the shape fills. This method also places cranked bars.
   - **Sketch:** draw the bar's centreline (STR-RBR-007).
   - **Free Form:** see STR-RBR-013.
4. Choose a **placement plane**: current work plane, near cover reference or far cover reference.
5. Choose an **orientation**: parallel to work plane, parallel to cover or perpendicular to cover. By Two Points adds Horizontal, Vertical and Perpendicular Segment. The `[` and `]` keys cycle orientations.
6. Choose the **set layout** (STR-RBR-004) and the set type, standard or **varying**. Click to place.

**UI.** Contextual tab "Modify | Place Rebar" with panels Placement Method, Placement Plane, Placement Orientation, Rebar Set, Set Type, Family (Load Shapes) and Show Tooltip. The optional cursor tooltip lists the keys for rotate, flip and align. *Multi-planar shapes* such as stirrups with legs in two planes are placed in section views and offer extra orientations.

**Behaviour & rules.**
- Placement respects host cover. If a bar cannot fit, Reviera refuses it and explains which dimension failed.
- New bars are visible in the placement view and in all section views, and hidden in other views by default (STR-RBR-017).

**Data (IFC mapping).**
- `IfcReinforcingBar`. PredefinedType comes from the shape style and role: `MAIN` for main bars, `LIGATURE` for stirrups and ties, `SHEAR`, `EDGE`, `RING`, `ANCHORING`, `SPACEBAR` or `PUNCHING`.
- The type is `IfcReinforcingBarType`, with NominalDiameter, CrossSectionArea, BarLength, BarSurface (`PLAIN` or `TEXTURED`), **BendingShapeCode** and **BendingParameters** (the A, B, C… values, in order).
- Body geometry: an `IfcSweptDiskSolid` along the bar centreline, one item per bar in the set, using `IfcMappedItem` for identical bars.
- **RXD element data** (`rebar`) holds the layout recipe and identity: HostId, ShapeFamilyId, PlacementMethod, LayoutRule, Quantity, Spacing, ArrayLength, Partition, RebarNumber, Style (Standard or StirrupTie), StirrupTieAttachment, HookStart, HookEnd, HookRotation, EndTreatment, WorkshopInstructions (Bent or Straight) and OverrideHookLengths.
- Mass and total length: a standard quantity set where the schema defines one. Otherwise they are computed on load and not stored.

**Commands.**
- `rebar.place(host_id, shape_id, bar_type_id, method: "expand"|"two_points"|"sketch", plane, orientation, points?, layout?) -> rebar_id`
- `rebar_shape_browser.show()`

**Acceptance criteria.**
- [x] Expand-to-Host of a closed stirrup shape in a 300 × 600 column section with 40 mm cover produces a stirrup whose outer dimensions equal the host dimensions minus twice the cover.
- [x] A placed bar exports as `IfcReinforcingBar` with its type's `BendingShapeCode` equal to the shape code of the shape family.

*Built (2026-10-19), Expand to Host:* `rebar.place` with `placement` *section* (closed links, shape 51, with 135° hooks into the core, spread along a rectangular column or beam), *face* (straight, L or U bars along a member at its top, bottom, left or right face, their legs turned into the section) or *layer* (straight bars in a floor's top or bottom layer in a plan direction, or a wall's exterior or interior face, vertical or horizontal, each bar clipped to the outline and its openings less the edge cover; `offset` sets a second layer further in). Bars keep inside each face's cover; a shape that cannot fit is refused (`rebar.no_fit`), naming the width, depth or length. `rebar.set` changes the bar type, shape or placement, and `rebar.info` reports the set. Bends are drawn at the bar type's bend diameters. IFC: `IfcReinforcingBar` (`MAIN` or `LIGATURE`) with NominalDiameter, CrossSectionArea, BarLength and BarSurface `TEXTURED`, a faceted tube body per bar, and a synthesized `IfcReinforcingBarType` per set (marked `rxd:rebar_type`, rewritten on each save) with the shape code as `BendingShapeCode` and the A, B, C… dimensions as `BendingParameters`. Rebar in its host is not a clash. Concrete › **Rebar** places a set in each selected host from a dialog of the placements that host takes, the shapes, the bar types and the layout. Not yet: By Two Points, Sketch and Free Form, placement planes and orientations, varying sets, the Shape Browser, view visibility (STR-RBR-017), `IfcSweptDiskSolid` bodies with mapped items, round columns (spirals).

### 4.2.4 Rebar set layouts
**ID:** STR-RBR-004 · **Priority:** P2 · **Ref:** research/03 §3.2 ("Rebar set layout rules")

**Purpose.** Distribute identical bars along a direction.

**Behaviour & rules.**

| Rule | Input | Behaviour |
|------|-------|-----------|
| Single | — | One bar |
| Fixed Number | n | n bars spread evenly over the array length |
| Maximum Spacing | s | Smallest count that keeps centre spacing at or below s |
| Number with Spacing | n, s | n bars at spacing s; the array length follows |
| Minimum Clear Spacing | c | Clear gap at least c; stays valid when bar size changes |
| Custom Spacing | formula | Segment list such as `3x100; ?x200; 5x100`. `?` marks the one variable segment that absorbs the remaining length. A second syntax, `1400@100; 900@300`, gives distance at spacing. |

- Sets are tagged and scheduled as **one object** with quantity and spacing.
- Formula errors are reported inline: a non-numeric value, more than one `?`, or a total longer than the array length.
- Individual bars can be hidden or removed and later reset (STR-RBR-006).

**Data (IFC mapping).** The IFC body carries one swept solid per bar, so other tools see the true count. **RXD element data** (`rebar`) holds the layout recipe: LayoutRule, Quantity, Spacing, ArrayLength and CustomSpacingFormula.

**Commands.** `rebar.set_layout(rebar_id, rule, n?, spacing?, clear?, formula?)`

**Acceptance criteria.**
- [x] `3x100; ?x200; 5x100` over 2 000 mm yields 3 spaces of 100 mm, then 6 of 200 mm, then 5 of 100 mm. That is 14 spaces filling 300 + 1 200 + 500 = 2 000 mm, so 15 bars, with the first bar at 0.
- [x] With Minimum Clear Spacing 50 mm, changing the bar diameter from 12 to 20 mm reduces the count where needed so the clear gap stays at least 50 mm.

*Built (2026-10-19):* every rule of the table, in `rebar.place` and `rebar.set_layout` (several sets at once). Maximum spacing spreads the fewest bars evenly; number with spacing that runs past the array is refused; custom formulas take both syntaxes, and a formula with two `?`, a non-number or a total past the array is refused with the reason (`rebar.formula`). The array runs between the covers less a bar, so the outer bars' surfaces sit at the cover. A set is one element with its quantity; its body has a tube per bar. A set's Properties show the shape, bar type, quantity, length ("exact [rounded]"), total length, mass and dimensions, and edit its Rule, Number, Spacing and Formula. Not yet: hiding and resetting individual bars (STR-RBR-006), the inline formula error in the Properties row.

*Built (2026-10-26), bars as swept disks in IFC:* a set's bars, varying sets' length groups, area, path and fabric reinforcement's bars and fabric sheets' wires are written as `IfcSweptDiskSolid`s along their centrelines (`IfcPolyline`s through the bends' arc points; `AdvancedSweptSolid` representations), one per bar, instead of faceted tubes; a save that changes nothing keeps them. The concrete sample went from 16.4 MB to 1.1 MB. Bar types' `BendingParameters` are now `IfcLengthMeasure`s (the select does not take positive lengths), so the sample passes IfcOpenShell's schema validation without issues. *(Owner, 2026-10-26: "Fix the precast IFC size with IfcSweptDiskSolid bars.")* Not yet: bends as true arcs (`IfcSweptDiskSolidPolygonal` with a fillet radius, or an `IfcIndexedPolyCurve` with arc segments); couplers are still faceted.

### 4.2.5 Varying rebar sets
**ID:** STR-RBR-005 · **Priority:** P2 · **Ref:** research/03 §3.2 ("Varying rebar set")

**Purpose.** Sets whose bar lengths change across inclined or skewed straight host faces.

**Workflow.**
1. Start *Rebar* (STR-RBR-003) and choose **Varying** in the *Set Type* panel before placing; or select an existing standard set and choose *Convert to Varying* on its contextual tab.
2. Each bar in the set is re-fitted to the host cover faces at its own position along the array, so bar segments lengthen or shorten with the taper.

**Behaviour & rules.**
- Only straight inclined faces are supported, not arcs. Reviera explains the refusal when a face is curved.
- An existing standard set can be converted to a varying set, and back where the geometry allows. *Convert to Standard* is refused, naming the bars that differ, when the bars no longer share one length within the rounding increment (STR-RBR-002).
- Every layout rule of STR-RBR-004 works on varying sets. Spacing is measured along the array direction, not along the inclined face.
- Bar handles constrained to the inclined faces stay constrained per bar; handles on parallel faces keep one shared constraint.
- **Numbering.** Each distinct length (after rounding) is a separate identity for numbering (STR-RBR-016), so a varying set can carry several rebar numbers; tags show the range ("12–17").
- Schedules list each distinct length, or one row per set with minimum and maximum length when the schedule groups by set.
- A varying set that regenerates to only one distinct length stays varying until converted.

**Data (IFC mapping).** One `IfcReinforcingBar` per distinct length group, aggregated under one `IfcElementAssembly` (`REINFORCEMENT_UNIT`), with the varying flag in RXD element data (`rebar`). Each group's `BarLength` is its own length; the set-level layout recipe (STR-RBR-004) is stored once on the assembly.

**Commands.** `rebar.convert_to_varying(rebar_ids)`, `rebar.convert_to_standard(rebar_ids)`

**Acceptance criteria.**
- [x] A set in a tapered wall produces bars whose lengths follow the taper, and the schedule shows a length range.
- [x] Converting a varying set in a tapered wall back to standard is refused and the message names the number of differing lengths.
- [x] A varying set with five distinct rounded lengths exports one `IfcElementAssembly` (`REINFORCEMENT_UNIT`) aggregating five `IfcReinforcingBar` groups.
- [x] Placing a varying set against a curved wall face is refused with an explanation.

*Built (2026-10-19):* a new placement, `{kind: through, along}`: straight bars across a wall's thickness between its exterior and interior covers, `along` metres from its start, spread up the wall by any layout rule (spacing measured up the wall). `rebar.place` takes `varying`; a varying set fits each bar to the wall's faces at its own height (slanted and tapered cross-sections, ARC-WALL-005; the cover measured square to a leaning face), a standard set's bars all take the first bar's length, centred in their section. `rebar.convert_to_varying` and `rebar.convert_to_standard` take `rebar_ids`; Convert to Standard is refused while the bars have more than one rounded length (`rebar.lengths_differ`, naming how many and which); a set that regenerates to one length stays varying until converted. Curved walls are refused (`rebar.curved`, saying why). Placements other than Through are refused (`rebar.not_varying`): layers in floors and walls already fit each bar to the outline. Each distinct rounded length is its own numbering identity (the same as a standard straight bar of that length), so a varying set carries several numbers; `rebar.info` gives `varying`, `length_groups` (length, count, number) and a length range in `length_text`; the Rebar Tag, Properties and the schedule's Rebar Number show the number range ("8–18"); Bar Length and segment A show the length range, with *Minimum Bar Length* and *Maximum Bar Length* fields. IFC: the set's own `IfcReinforcingBar` is the first length group; the other groups are derived `IfcReinforcingBar`s, all aggregated under a derived `IfcElementAssembly` (`REINFORCEMENT_UNIT`) that the host aggregates, rewritten on every save and skipped on load (the recipe stays on the set). The Rebar dialog has *Through the wall* with *Along the wall* and *Set type*; the set's tab has a Set Type panel (Convert to Varying, Convert to Standard); Properties show Set type. Not yet: varying for other placements (sloped floor edges, beams of varying depth), shape handles, a schedule row per length.

### 4.2.6 Rebar editing, propagation and splitting
**ID:** STR-RBR-006 · **Priority:** P2 · **Ref:** research/03 §3.2 ("Editing")

**Behaviour & rules.**
- **Shape handles:** circles at bar ends, triangles on edges, a handle for the bar plane and a handle for the set extent.
- **In-canvas segment length controls:** editable, and rounded according to STR-RBR-002. Hook lengths are read-only unless *Override Hook Lengths* is on.
- **Pick New Host** and **Select Host**.
- **Move Rebar in Set**, **Remove Bar**, **Reset Bars** and **Split Set** at a chosen bar.
- **Propagate:** copy and adapt selected bars to other hosts of the same category. *Align by Host* matches the host's local frame; *Align by Face* matches a picked face. Constraints are re-solved per target, and targets where they cannot be solved are reported.

**Commands.**
- `rebar.set_segment_length(rebar_id, segment, length)`
- `rebar.move_bar_in_set(rebar_id, bar_index, delta)`
- `rebar.remove_bar(rebar_id, index)`
- `rebar.reset_bars(rebar_id)`
- `rebar.split_set(rebar_id, at_index) -> rebar_id`
- `rebar.propagate(rebar_ids[], target_host_ids[], mode: "host"|"face", face_ref?) -> rebar_ids[]`
- `rebar.pick_new_host(rebar_ids[], host_id)`

**Acceptance criteria.**
- [x] Propagating a stirrup set from one beam to 10 beams of different lengths produces 10 sets, each spanning its own beam between covers.
- [x] Splitting a 20-bar set at bar 8 yields two sets of 8 and 12 bars with identical type and shape.

*Built (2026-10-19):* edits stay parametric in the set's recipe (`edits`, by each bar's index before edits, reported by `rebar.info` as `bar_indices`): `rebar.set_segment_length` (A, B, …; rounded to the segment increment; refused past the room inside the cover; `null` resets: a link's A and B, a face bar's run and legs, a layer bar's A capping each bar from its start), `rebar.move_bar_in_set`, `rebar.remove_bar` (the quantity drops), `rebar.reset_bars`, `rebar.split_set` (the set keeps bars before the one given, a new set of the same type, shape and partition takes the rest), `rebar.propagate` (copies to other hosts of the same kind, each worked out in its own host since sets are placed relative to their host; `face` mode moves bars at a face to the face given; returns the new sets and the hosts where they do not fit, with why) and `rebar.pick_new_host`. Rebar sits under its host in the model tree. The set's contextual tab has Remove Bar, Move Bar and Split Set (click the bar), Reset Bars, Propagate (click hosts, Enter) and Pick New Host; Properties edit each segment. Not yet: shape handles and in-canvas segment controls, Select Host, hook length overrides, Align by Face with a picked face (faces are named).

### 4.2.7 Sketched rebar and rebar constraints
**ID:** STR-RBR-007 · **Priority:** P2 · **Ref:** research/03 §3.2 ("Rebar constraints"), §3.2 "Shape matching"

**Purpose.** Draw bar centrelines directly, and keep bars constrained to their host.

**Behaviour & rules.**
- **Sketch Rebar:** sketch lines and arcs in a plane inside the host. Reviera matches the result to a loaded shape (STR-RBR-008) or creates a new one.
- **Constraints:** each handle can be constrained to a planar reference:
  - **host cover**
  - **another bar**
  - **host surface** (with an offset)

  The reference plane must be parallel to the handle, within 6° for end handles. Straight bars can attach to stirrup bend points at 45° increments.
- **Edit Constraints mode:**
  - The bar being edited is highlighted in one colour and its constraint target in a second colour (theme tokens, not fixed colours).
  - The offset is shown as an editable dimension.
  - Constraints can be disabled, kept or reset to default.
  - Several sets, including cranked and spliced sets, can be edited together.
- When the host changes, constrained handles follow and unconstrained handles keep their absolute positions.

**Data (IFC mapping).** No IFC equivalent. **RXD element data** (`constraints`) holds one entry per handle: handle ID, target kind (Cover, Bar, Surface), target GlobalId or face reference, and offset.

**Commands.**
- `rebar.sketch(host_id, plane, curves[], bar_type_id, style, hooks?) -> rebar_id`
- `rebar.constrain(rebar_id, handle_id, target_kind, target_ref, offset)`
- `rebar.reset_constraints(rebar_id)`
- `rebar.constraints(rebar_id) -> {handles[], faces[]}`

**Acceptance criteria.**
- [x] A longitudinal bar constrained to the top cover moves when the cover type changes from 40 to 50 mm.
- [x] A constraint to a face 10° away from parallel is refused, with an explanation.

*Built (2026-10-19):* `rebar.sketch` draws a bar's centreline as lines and arcs (`{line: {start, end}}`, `{arc: {start, end, through}}`, end to end) in a plane inside any concrete host, in the plane's coordinates; `plane` `{origin, x, normal}` defaults to the host's own (a floor's mid-depth, a wall's location line, a beam's or column's long section through its axis). The result is matched to a loaded shape (00 straight, 11 one 90° bend, 21 two 90° bends to one side, 51 a closed rectangle); anything else, and anything with an arc (tessellated into eight segments), becomes **99**, the special-shape code, added to the catalogue. Corners are bent at the bar type's standard or stirrup bend; segment dimensions are the corners' runs plus half a bar at each bend. `style` standard or stirrup_tie (role ligature); `hook_start`, `hook_end` turn square to the bar toward the host's middle. The set spreads along the plane's normal to the far face's cover by `layout` (a single bar by default). The corners are kept in world coordinates in the recipe (`placement: {kind: sketch, points, normal, style, hooks, constraints}`; the RXD `constraints` entries live there). Handles are `start`, `segment:N` and `end`. `rebar.constrain` keeps one to a host face's **cover** (the plane at the cover plus half a bar), a host **surface**, or another set's **bar** (its nearest segment), with an offset further in (default 0 from a cover, otherwise where the handle is, so it does not move); `target_kind: none` frees a handle. The faces are `top`, `bottom`, `left`, `right`, `start`, `end` for beams and columns, `exterior`, `interior`, `top`, `bottom`, `start`, `end` for straight walls, `top`, `bottom` and `edge:N` for floors; each takes its host's cover by kind. A reference more than 6° from parallel to a segment (or from square to an end, or another bar's direction) is refused (`rebar.not_parallel`, naming the angle). Constraints are solved each time the bars are worked out, by projecting each handle onto its plane in turn until they agree (a segment moves square to its plane, an end along its bar), so constrained handles follow host and cover changes and unconstrained ones keep their absolute positions; a bar-to-bar reference is followed one level deep, so two bars referencing each other settle. Changing or removing constraints keeps the handles where the old ones put them. `rebar.constraints` lists the handles (where, direction, constraint, reference plane) and the host's faces. Sketched sets are not propagated, and their segments are not set by hand (refused, naming why). Concrete › **Sketch Rebar** (bar type, style, hooks, layout; then click the corners in the host's plane, the first corner closing a link, or type them in Coordinates, XY); the set's tab › Constraints › **Edit Constraints** (each handle: Free, a face's cover, a face, or a bar of another set in the host, with its offset; while open the bar is drawn in the CONSTRAINT_BAR colour over the host and each reference as a line to its plane and a cross on it in CONSTRAINT_TARGET) and **Reset Constraints**. Not yet: stirrup-bend attachment at 45° increments, the in-view editable offset dimension and handle dragging, editing several sets together, cranked bars, theme-switchable colours (the two are named view colours), sketching in section views.

### 4.2.8 Rebar shapes, shape codes and shape matching
**ID:** STR-RBR-008 · **Priority:** P2 · **Ref:** research/03 §3.2 ("Rebar shapes and shape codes")

**Purpose.** Reviera shall support a parametric family kind, the **rebar shape family**. It defines a bar's centreline and its dimensions, and a **shape code** that is used in tags, schedules and bending details.

**Behaviour & rules.**
- **Shape family content:**
  - a sketched centreline of rebar lines
  - dimension parameters named A, B, C… that become the shape-code segments
  - major segments
  - bend and hook definitions
  - a multi-planar flag
  - **allowable bar types**
  - a **status checker** that validates the sketch, its dimensions and its constraints, so the family can be used
- **Shape parameters:** style, stirrup/tie attachment, start and end hook settings, shape image, spiral settings, **shape code**, and whether hooks are included in the shape.
- **Shape matching:** a sketched or free-form bar maps to an existing shape when all of these match:
  - segment count
  - joined geometry
  - hook count and direction
  - hook bend dimensions
  - style

  Otherwise Reviera creates a new shape family. It is named with the next free number, which the user can rename.
- **National shape-code standards:** Reviera ships open **shape-code catalogues** as data files that map a code to a segment pattern. Candidates are ISO 4066 and BS 8666 / ACI 315-style numbering. Each catalogue is authored from the published code structure and not copied from vendor templates. Users can add catalogues.
- Shape families can be built in 3D by rotating hooks and cranks out of plane.

**Data (IFC mapping).**
- The shape code goes to `IfcReinforcingBarType.BendingShapeCode`, and the ordered A, B, C… values go to `BendingParameters` (`IfcLengthMeasure` and `IfcPlaneAngleMeasure`).
- Where a standard pset exists, values are also written to it: `Pset_ReinforcingBarBendingsBS8666Common`, `Pset_ReinforcingBarBendingsISOCD3766Common`, `Pset_ReinforcingBarBendingsDIN135610Common` and `Pset_ReinforcingBarBendingsBECCommon`.
- The shape family itself is an `IfcReinforcingBarType`. Its **RXD family recipe** holds the centreline sketch, parameter list and status.

**Commands.**
- `rebar_shape.create_from_sketch(curves[], params, code?) -> shape_id`
- `rebar_shape.match(rebar_id) -> shape_id | null`
- `rebar_shape.check(shape_id) -> issues[]`
- `rebar_shape_catalogue.load(path)`

**Acceptance criteria.**
- [ ] Sketching an L-bar that matches an existing L shape reuses that shape and does not create a new family.
- [ ] Adding a 135° hook to the same sketch creates a new shape, because the hook count differs.
- [ ] An exported bar carries the shape code and parameters in both `IfcReinforcingBarType` and the matching standard pset.

*Built (2026-10-19), the catalogue:* an open BS 8666 shape-code catalogue (`data/rebar/shapes_bs8666.json`: 00 straight, 11 L, 21 U, 51 closed link with 135° hooks, authored from the code structure), listed by `rebar_shape.list` with each shape's dimensions, style and bends; the code and dimensions go to `BendingShapeCode` and `BendingParameters`. Not yet: shape families with sketched centrelines, shape matching, the status checker, more catalogues and `rebar_shape_catalogue.load`, the standard bending psets.

### 4.2.9 Bar types, hooks and cranks
**ID:** STR-RBR-009 · **Priority:** P2 · **Ref:** research/03 §3.2 ("Rebar instance and type data", "Hooks", "Cranks")

**Behaviour & rules.**
- **Bar type:**
  - deformation (deformed or plain)
  - material
  - **bar diameter** and **model diameter**
  - standard bend diameter, standard hook bend diameter and stirrup/tie bend diameter
  - a **hook length table** (one row per hook type)
  - maximum bend radius
  - rounding overrides
  - a graphics subcategory
- **Hook type:** angle, extension multiplier and style.
- **Cranks:** a crank is an offset inside a segment. It is defined by crank length, offset and angle, and is kept inside the cover.
  - *Add Crank* acts on an existing bar. *Place with Crank* uses By Two Points.
  - Adding a crank re-matches the bar to a shape, or creates one.
  - Constraints stay editable on cranked bars.
- **Spiral bars:** height, pitch, and base and top finishing turns.

**Data (IFC mapping).** `IfcReinforcingBarType` attributes The RXD family recipe of the bar type holds what IFC cannot: ModelDiameter, BendDiameters, HookLengthTable and MaxBendRadius. Hook types are kept in **RXD document** `rebar`. Cranks are **RXD element data** (`rebar`): SegmentIndex, Position, Length, Offset and Angle.

**Commands.**
- `rebar_bar_type.create(name, diameter, material_id, ...) -> type_id`
- `rebar_hook_type.create(name, angle, extension_multiplier) -> id`
- `rebar.add_crank(rebar_id, segment, position, length, offset, angle)`

**Acceptance criteria.**
- [ ] Adding a 75 mm crank to segment A of a straight bar produces a bar whose crank stays inside cover, and a matching cranked shape is used or created.

*Built (2026-10-19), bar and hook types:* the region's bar catalogue (`data/rebar/bar_sizes.json`: ASTM A615 #3–#18 in US models, 6–50 mm B500B bars elsewhere) with bar and model diameters, deformation, material and inside bend diameters for standard bends, hooks and stirrups (ACI 318-19 Tables 25.3.1 and 25.3.2; EN 1992-1-1 Table 8.1N); the region's hook types (90°, 180°, 135° stirrup/tie, with extension multipliers and minimum lengths); `rebar_bar_type.list` / `.create` and `rebar_hook_type.list` / `.create` (project types kept in `rxd:rebar`). Not yet: hook length tables per bar type, maximum bend radius, rounding overrides, cranks, spirals.

### 4.2.10 Area reinforcement
**ID:** STR-RBR-010 · **Priority:** P2 · **Ref:** research/03 §3.3

**Purpose.** Lay out orthogonal bar layers over a region of a floor, wall or foundation slab.

**Workflow.**
1. Choose *Concrete › Area* and select the host.
2. Sketch a closed boundary. The parallel-line symbol marks the **major direction** edge, which can be changed.
3. Click *Finish*. A reinforcement symbol and tag are placed.

The *Whole Host* option uses the host outline as the boundary.

**Behaviour & rules.**
- **Layout rule:** Maximum Spacing or Fixed Number.
- Additional top/exterior and bottom/interior cover offsets allow layers to be stacked.
- **Layers:** Top/Bottom for floors, Exterior/Interior for walls, each × Major/Minor. Each layer has an on/off toggle, bar type, hook type, hook orientation and spacing.
- Host openings cut the bars.
- In "real rebar" mode (STR-RBR-002) the bars are rebar sets that can be seen in section. *Remove Area System* keeps them.

**Data (IFC mapping).**
- The system is an `IfcElementAssembly` with `REINFORCEMENT_UNIT`, with its recipe (Boundary, MajorDirection, LayoutRule, Layers[]) in RXD element data (`rebar`).
- The bars are `IfcReinforcingBar` elements aggregated into the system.
- The symbol is view-specific annotation (chapter 5).

**Commands.**
- `area_reinforcement.create(host_id, boundary | "whole_host", major_edge, layers[], layout_rule) -> system_id`
- `area_reinforcement.remove_system(system_id) -> rebar_ids[]`

**Acceptance criteria.**
- [x] A 6 × 4 m slab region with top and bottom × major and minor at 200 mm produces four layers, cut around a 1 × 1 m opening.
- [x] *Remove Area System* in real-rebar mode leaves four rebar sets that can be scheduled.

*Built (2026-10-19):* `area_reinforcement.create` lays layers over a closed `boundary` (points in the host's plane: plan for floors, along the wall and up from its base for walls) or the whole host, the major bars along the chosen edge of the boundary or outline and the minor ones square to it. Layers are top and bottom (exterior and interior for walls) × major and minor, each with on/off, bar type, hook type (turned into the host, or out with `hook_flip`) and spacing or number under maximum spacing or fixed number; each face's minor layer sits inside its major one, and `additional_top` and `additional_bottom` stack them further in. Bars are clipped to the boundary, the host's outline and its openings (sketch holes, vertical openings and shafts) less the edge cover. `area_reinforcement.set` changes it; `area_reinforcement.remove_system` (only with real rebar on) keeps the layers as ordinary rebar sets, returned. The system is an `IfcElementAssembly` `REINFORCEMENT_UNIT` with its recipe; on export one `IfcReinforcingBar` per layer (marked `rxd:rebar_part`, rewritten on each save, not read back as elements) is aggregated under it, and the host aggregates the system. `reinforcement_system.info` reports the layers with counts, lengths and mass, and the steel's volume. The real-rebar setting is locked once an area or path system exists. Concrete › **Area** sets the layers, then the boundary is sketched on the host's plane (a floor's top in a plan or 3D view, a wall's face in 3D), snapping to its corners and edges, closed by the first corner or Enter, or drawn as a rectangle (R), with the major-direction edge drawn doubled and moved with M; or the whole host. Coordinates (UI-A11Y-001) types or corrects the corners, and edits a placed system's boundary. **Remove Area System**; Properties show the layers and edit the spacing. Not yet: the reinforcement symbol and tag, wall openings cutting wall layers, hook orientation per layer by name.

### 4.2.11 Path reinforcement
**ID:** STR-RBR-011 · **Priority:** P2 · **Ref:** research/03 §3.4

**Purpose.** Bars laid perpendicular to an **open** path along a slab or wall edge, for example edge U-bars and top bars over supports.

**Workflow.** Choose *Concrete › Path* and sketch an open path. A flip control chooses the side. Finish.

**Behaviour & rules.**
- **Parameters:** layout rule, additional offset, face (top or bottom), bar spacing or number of bars.
- **Primary bar:** type, length, shape (single segment or with perpendicular segments), and start and end hooks.
- Optional **alternating bars** with their own type, length, shape and offset.
- The reinforcement volume is calculated.
- Path boundary visibility can be controlled through visibility/graphics overrides.

**Data (IFC mapping).** `IfcElementAssembly` `REINFORCEMENT_UNIT` with its recipe in RXD element data (`rebar`). The bars are `IfcReinforcingBar`.

**Commands.** `path_reinforcement.create(host_id, path_curves[], side, primary, alternating?, spacing | count, face) -> system_id`

**Acceptance criteria.**
- [x] A 5 m path at 150 mm spacing with alternating bars offset by 300 mm produces primary and alternating bars in the correct pattern.

*Built (2026-10-19):* `path_reinforcement.create` lays bars square to an open polyline in the host's plane, on its left (or right with `flip`), at a face, spaced along the path between its end covers by `spacing` or `count` (both: number with spacing). The primary bar has a type, length, legs turned into the host at both ends (a U, 0 for straight), start and end hooks and an offset from the path; optional alternating bars take every second place with their own type, length, legs, hooks and offset. Bars are clipped to the host less its cover. `path_reinforcement.set` changes the side, layout or bars; `reinforcement_system.info` gives the primary and alternating counts, lengths, mass and the reinforcement volume. IFC as area reinforcement (an `IfcReinforcingBar` each for the primary and alternating bars). Concrete › **Path** sets the bars, then the path is sketched on the host (Enter finishes), ticks showing the bars' side and F flipping it; Coordinates types or corrects its points, and edits a placed path (`path_reinforcement.set` takes `path`). Properties edit the side and spacing. Not yet: curved paths, path boundary visibility overrides.

### 4.2.12 Fabric (welded wire) reinforcement
**ID:** STR-RBR-012 · **Priority:** P2 · **Ref:** research/03 §3.5 · screenshots/structure_mep/fabric_area_sheet_layout.png

**Purpose.** Mesh sheets placed by area or one at a time.

**Behaviour & rules.**
- **Fabric area:**
  - Select a floor, wall or slab and sketch a closed boundary. The **major direction** sets sheet rotation.
  - Edge controls on the bounding rectangle set the start and end edges, sheet alignment and **lap splices**. Lap position is *Aligned* or *Staggered*.
  - Sheets are cut by the boundary and by host openings.
- **Single fabric sheet:** sheets snap to cover, sheet edges, lap positions and midpoints. *Cut by Host Cover* clips them.
- **Bent fabric sheet:** sketched from a cross-section profile.
- **Custom fabric sheets:** user-edited wire layouts, or rule-generated sheets in precast (STR-PRE-004).
- **Fabric wire type:** diameter and material.
- **Fabric sheet type:** major and minor wire type, spacing, overhangs, layout pattern, unit weight, and sheet length and width.

**Data (IFC mapping).**
- `IfcReinforcingMesh` (PredefinedType `USERDEFINED` or `NOTDEFINED`), typed by `IfcReinforcingMeshType` with MeshLength, MeshWidth, Longitudinal/TransverseBarNominalDiameter, Longitudinal/TransverseBarCrossSectionArea, Longitudinal/TransverseBarSpacing, BendingShapeCode and BendingParameters (for bent sheets).
- The fabric area is an `IfcElementAssembly` `REINFORCEMENT_UNIT` with its recipe (Boundary, MajorDirection, LapSplicePosition, LapLengths) in RXD element data (`rebar`).

**Commands.**
- `fabric_area.create(host_id, boundary, major_edge, sheet_type_id, lap_position, start_edge?) -> system_id`
- `fabric_sheet.place(host_id, sheet_type_id, point, rotation, cut_by_cover?) -> id`
- `fabric_sheet.create_bent(host_id, profile_curves[], sheet_type_id, extent) -> id`

**Acceptance criteria.**
- [x] A fabric area over a slab with one opening produces sheets clipped by both the boundary and the opening, with the configured lap lengths.
- [x] Switching from Aligned to Staggered moves every second row of lap splices by half a sheet length.

*Built (2026-10-19):* fabric wire and sheet types from the region's catalogue (`data/rebar/fabric.json`: BS 4483 A142, A193, A252, A393, B385, B503 in 4.8 × 2.4 m sheets; WRI 6x6-W1.4xW1.4 … W4.0xW4.0 in 8 × 20 ft sheets, wire diameters from the W area) or the project's own (`fabric_wire_type.list` / `.create`, `fabric_sheet_type.list` / `.create`, with mass per square metre; overhangs default to half the crossing wires' spacing). `fabric_area.create` lays sheets over a boundary or the whole host from its major edge, their length along it, stepping by the sheet less the end lap (`major_lap`) and side lap (`minor_lap`; by default a crossing spacing plus 50 mm); *Staggered* starts every second row half a sheet back. Each sheet's wires are cut by the boundary, the host's openings and its cover, and the sheet reports whether it was cut; major wires lie at the cover, minor ones on them. `fabric_area.set` changes the sheet type, laps, lap position or major edge. `fabric_sheet.place` places one sheet (`IfcReinforcingMesh`) at a corner point and rotation, cut by the host's cover when asked. IFC: a fabric area is an `IfcElementAssembly` `REINFORCEMENT_UNIT` aggregating an `IfcReinforcingMesh` per sheet; sheets carry MeshLength, MeshWidth, the longitudinal and transverse diameters, areas and spacings, typed by an `IfcReinforcingMeshType` (IFC4). Concrete › **Fabric Area** (the boundary sketched as for area reinforcement, or the whole host; `fabric_area.set` takes a new `boundary`) and **Fabric Sheet** (click the first corner, then a point along its length, the sheet's outline following the cursor); Properties show the sheet count (and how many are cut) and edit the lap position and laps. Not yet: edge controls in the view, the start-edge choice, snapping single sheets to cover, sheet edges and laps, bent sheets (`fabric_sheet.create_bent`), custom sheets, `BendingShapeCode` for bent sheets.

### 4.2.13 Free-form rebar
**ID:** STR-RBR-013 · **Priority:** P2 · **Ref:** research/03 §3.6

**Purpose.** Bars in hosts with complex or curved geometry, placed by picking host faces in 3D views.

**Behaviour & rules.**
- **Surface distribution:**
  - Non-planar bars are interpolated between a first bar and a last bar. Each of those is defined by where a start or end surface meets the host surface.
  - The bars follow the host surface and respect cover. Where faces have different covers, the largest cover is used.
- **Aligned distribution:**
  - Planar bars. Each bar plane cuts the host surfaces, and the planes are aligned along a **distribution path** built from host edges.
  - Path constraints are edited as *Path Surface 1/2* in Edit Constraints.
  - Each face's own cover is used.
  - This suits stirrups in members with varying sections.
- Shape matching for free-form bars uses *Workshop Instructions = Bent*. If no shape can describe the geometry, the bar reports only its total length.
- Free-form sets accept cranks and couplers.

**Data (IFC mapping).** `IfcReinforcingBar`. Bars use per-bar `IfcSweptDiskSolid` geometry along `IfcIndexedPolyCurve` or B-spline centrelines. RXD element data (`rebar`) records Distribution = "Surface" or "Aligned", with the constraint surfaces referenced by stable face IDs.

**Commands.** `rebar.place_free_form(host_id, kind: "surface"|"aligned", start_face, end_face, path_edges?, bar_type_id, layout) -> rebar_id`

**Acceptance criteria.**
- [x] A surface distribution on a doubly curved shell keeps every bar at the specified cover within 1 mm at sampled points.
- [ ] An aligned distribution in a tapered beam produces stirrups whose sizes follow the taper.

*Built (2026-10-19):* `rebar.place_free_form` with `kind` surface or aligned; the recipe's placement is `{kind: free_form, distribution: surface|aligned, …}` and its sets are always varying (STR-RBR-005: each rounded length its own number; Convert to Standard and Convert to Varying are refused). Concrete roofs are now rebar hosts (a roof type named for concrete or with a concrete `material`; covers top Exposed, bottom and edges Interior), taking only free-form distributions; Rebar and Sketch Rebar point to Free Form for them. **Surface:** the roof's underside (its faces, the facets of a dome or vault) is welded, its normals smoothed, and offset into the shell by the bottom cover plus half a bar (or to the top cover); planes interpolated from `start_plane` to `end_plane` (`{origin, normal}`; or `direction` x or y: planes square to it across the roof, inside the edge cover) are spaced by the layout over the distance between them, and each cut's longest polyline, trimmed by the edge cover at both ends, is a bar. On a 5 m hemisphere every sampled point of every bar is within 1 mm of 25 + 6 mm from the modelled underside (the faceted surface, not the true sphere). Different covers on one shell are not yet taken as their largest. **Aligned:** planes square to a path (points, or `path_ref` axis for beams and columns, `along` or `up` for walls) at the layout's spacing, inside the end covers, cut the host's body (all bodies but reinforcement, so a set never depends on itself); the section's outline around the path is cleaned of nearly straight corners and each side is moved in by the cover of the host face it faces most (`top`, `bottom`, `left`, `right`, `exterior`, `interior`, …) plus half a bar, giving a closed link from its first corner round and back with 135° hooks into the core, a bar apart along the path. A rectangular link is shape 51 (A, B and hooks C, D, the same values as the section placement gives along a rectangular beam), otherwise 99 with its sides as segments; a surface set of straight bars is 00, otherwise 99 (its total length). Reviera has no tapered beams yet, so the second criterion is open; the same mechanism is tested up a wall tapering 1° per face, whose links narrow by 2 tan 1° per metre up. Concrete › Reinforcement › **Free Form** (for a roof: layer, direction, bar type, layout; for a beam, column or wall: the path, bar type, layout). Not yet: picking start and end faces and path edges in the view (stable face IDs), Path Surface constraints in Edit Constraints, cranks and couplers on free-form sets, B-spline centrelines in IFC (bars are written as meshes like other sets), and speed: an aligned set rebuilds every body when its bars are worked out.

### 4.2.14 Path shape distribution and morphed distribution
**ID:** STR-RBR-014 · **Priority:** P2 · **Ref:** research/03 §3.6 ("[2027] Path Free Form Rebar", "Morphed") · screenshots/structure_mep/rebar_3d_path_shape_distribution_2027.png · screenshots/structure_mep/rebar_morphed_longitudinal_distribution_2027.png

**Purpose.** Two advanced distributions for infrastructure-type geometry such as bridges and tunnels.

**Behaviour & rules.**
- **Path shape distribution:**
  1. Place a *main bar* in a section view by Two Points, Expand to Host or Sketch.
  2. Click **Path** and select one or more continuous host edges.
  3. Finish.

  Identical planar bars are then distributed along the double-curved edge path. Bar segments can be constrained to edges so that the set follows changes to the host. The distribution range and the main bar can be edited later, and bar lengths may vary.
- **Morphed distribution:** select a transverse stirrup set (circular, spiral or multi-segment). Longitudinal bars are generated that follow the stirrup shape, and they update when the stirrups change.

**Data (IFC mapping).** `IfcReinforcingBar`. RXD element data (`rebar`) records Distribution = "Path" or "Morphed", with the driver set's GlobalId (morphed) or PathEdgeRefs (path).

**Commands.**
- `rebar.distribute_along_path(main_rebar_id, path | path_ref, range?, layout?) -> rebar_id`
- `rebar.distribute_morphed(driver_stirrup_set_id, bar_type_id, count | spacing) -> rebar_id`

**Acceptance criteria.**
- [x] Changing a driver stirrup set's diameter regenerates the morphed longitudinal bars inside the new stirrup outline.
- [x] A path distribution along a 3D-curved edge keeps each bar plane perpendicular to the path tangent.

*Built (2026-10-19):* the recipe's placement `{kind: distributed, distribution: path|morphed, …}` keeps its source set's GlobalId and is worked out from it every time, so the set follows the source and is deleted with it. `rebar.distribute_along_path` takes the main set's first bar (any placement; its shape code and bar type) and a path: `path` points, or `path_ref` a named path of the main set's host (`axis`, `along`, `up`, kept by name so it follows the host), with `range` [from, to] metres along it and a `layout`. The main bar must lie square to the path where it starts (refused, `rebar.path`, saying how far it reaches along it). A frame is carried along the path, each segment's turned onto it by the rotation between their directions, so the bars twist no more than the path does; every bar's plane is square to the tangent of the path segment it lies on (checked along a polyline curving in plan and rising). `rebar.distribute_morphed` takes a driver set of at least two closed stirrups or ties (section links, aligned free-form links, sketched links), a bar type and a `count` round the stirrups (or a `spacing` along the first): the stirrups' loops (without their hooks) are walked by equal shares of their length from their first corner, each point moved square to the stirrup, in its plane and toward its inside, by half the stirrup's bar plus half its own, and joined from the first stirrup to the last. Changing the links from Ø10 to Ø16 moves the bars in with the new outline and the thicker link. Morphed sets are varying (each length its own number), shape 00 when straight, else 99. Neither is propagated, split by segment or converted. The set's tab › **Distribute** › *Path Distribution* (its host's path, or typed x, y, z points in mm; range; layout) and *Morphed* (bar type; count or spacing). Not yet: picking path edges in the view and sketching a 3D path, constraining bar segments to edges, putting morphed bars at the stirrups' corners first, a main bar that changes its bar type carrying it to the path set.

### 4.2.15 Splices and couplers
**ID:** STR-RBR-015 · **Priority:** P2 · **Ref:** research/03 §3.7 · screenshots/structure_mep/rebar_couplers.png

**Behaviour & rules.**
- **Splice:**
  - *Splice* on a selected set, by **Pick Line** or **By Length**.
  - Lap and stagger lengths come from the splice type or from the bar type.
  - Spliced sets are constrained to each other and move together.
  - Splicing is supported only on straight segments of shape-driven rebar. It is refused for spiral, arc, multi-planar, area, path and free-form bars. Free-form longitudinal splicing is an open question (§4.17).
- **Coupler:**
  - *Concrete › Coupler*: **On Bar End** or **Between Two Bars**.
  - The coupler type is sized to the bar automatically, and a type is created when none fits.
  - **Tolerances:** the bar ends must be no more than 10 bar diameters apart and offset by no more than 3 diameters. Arc bars must share a centre.
  - Couplers apply **end treatments** that shorten the bars.
  - Couplers can be scheduled, grouped, numbered per partition, tagged, and propagated across sets.
  - The coupler family option *Align to View* hides a coupler when the view direction is more than 75° from the bar axis.
  - Couplers always display as solids in 3D.

**Data (IFC mapping).**
- Couplers are `IfcMechanicalFastener`. In IFC4, PredefinedType is `USERDEFINED` with ObjectType "COUPLER"; in IFC4X3 it is `COUPLER` where available. The type is `IfcMechanicalFastenerType`.
- The coupler is connected to both bars through `IfcRelConnectsWithRealizingElements`, with the bars as relating and related elements and the coupler as the realizing element.
- Splices are stored in RXD element data (`rebar`): SpliceTypeId, LapLength, Stagger and partner GlobalIds.

**Commands.**
- `rebar.splice(rebar_id, mode: "line"|"length", line? , length?, splice_type_id?) -> rebar_ids[]`
- `rebar_coupler.place(bar_end_refs[1..2], type_id?) -> coupler_id`

**Acceptance criteria.**
- [x] Placing a coupler between two Ø25 bar ends 300 mm apart is refused, because the gap is more than 10 diameters (250 mm).
- [x] A spliced set exports two bars per splice location, connected by the configured lap length.

*Built (2026-10-19):* `rebar.splice` cuts a set of straight bars (shape 00, not hooked or already spliced; links, bent, area, path and free-form bars are refused) by a distance from their start or where a plan line crosses them into two sets overlapping by the lap (default 50 bar diameters, provisional pending expert review, Q14), every second bar's splice moved by the stagger; each keeps the other's GlobalId (`splice` in its recipe) and a change of layout, bar type, placement or host to one is made to both. `rebar_coupler.place` puts a coupler (`IfcMechanicalFastener` USERDEFINED, ObjectType COUPLER) on one bar end or between two of the same size no more than 10 diameters apart and 3 off line (refused naming the distance and limit); it is a sleeve 1.6 bar diameters across and 6 long, sits in the *Structural Rebar Couplers* category, is not a clash with its bars or their host, is deleted with its bars, and exports with `IfcRelConnectsWithRealizingElements` between the two sets; `rebar_coupler.info`. Splice (position, lap, stagger) and Coupler (click one or two bar ends) are on the set's contextual tab. Not yet: splice and coupler types, end treatments shortening bars, arc bars, coupler numbering, schedules, tags, propagation and Align to View.

### 4.2.16 Reinforcement numbering and partitions
**ID:** STR-RBR-016 · **Priority:** P2 · **Ref:** research/03 §3.1 ("Reinforcement numbering and partitions") · screenshots/structure_mep/rebar_partitions_by_level.png

**Purpose.** Give identical reinforcement elements identical numbers within a partition.

**Behaviour & rules.**
- Each rebar set, fabric sheet and coupler gets a **Rebar Number**.
- Elements that are identical in type, size, material and shape, including segment values after rounding, share a number within the same **Partition**.
- **Partition** is a free-text instance value, used for phase, host type, location, top or bottom, and so on.
- Rebar, fabric and couplers each have their own number sequence.
- *Reinforcement Numbers* dialog: list the sequences per partition, change a start number, **remove gaps** and renumber.
- Numbers update on regeneration when an element's identity changes. Locked numbers (an option) do not.

**UI: Reinforcement Numbers dialog** (*Concrete › Settings › Reinforcement Numbers*, `reinforcement_numbering.show(partition?)`).
- A partition list on the left (every partition name in use, plus "(none)"), with a filter box. `partition` preselects one.
- For the selected partition, three tabs (Rebar, Fabric, Couplers), each a grid with: number, element count, a short identity summary (bar type, shape code, main dimensions), locked flag, and a *Select* button that selects those elements in the model.
- Per sequence: **Start number** (integer ≥ 1); **Remove gaps**; **Renumber** (reassigns numbers in creation order, keeping locked numbers fixed and skipping them).
- Per row: change a number to a free value (refused, with the conflicting row highlighted, if the value is used by a different identity in the same sequence), lock or unlock.
- All edits apply on *OK* as one transaction; *Cancel* discards them.

**Data (IFC mapping).** The rebar number is written to `IfcReinforcingBar.Tag`, and to `Pset_PrecastConcreteElementFabrication.PieceMark` where an exchange requires it. Partition and lock flag: RXD element data (`rebar`). Sequences: RXD document `model/rebar`.

**Commands.**
- `reinforcement_numbering.renumber(partition?, kind: "rebar"|"fabric"|"coupler", start?, remove_gaps?)`
- `reinforcement_numbering.show(partition?)`
- `rebar.set_partition(ids[], name)`

**Acceptance criteria.**
- [x] Two identical stirrup sets in partition "L1" share number 5. Moving one to partition "L2" gives it a number in L2's sequence.
- [x] *Remove gaps* turns the sequence 1, 2, 4, 7 into 1, 2, 3, 4 without changing which elements share numbers.
- [x] In the dialog, typing number 3 for a row when 3 belongs to another identity in the same partition and kind is refused and the other row is highlighted.
- [x] Renumbering a sequence with number 4 locked keeps 4 on its elements and numbers the others 1, 2, 3, 5, ….

*Built (2026-10-19):* every rebar set and fabric sheet (placed alone or laid by a fabric area) has a number, shared by identical ones in the same partition: rebar by bar type, shape code and segment values after segment rounding; fabric by sheet type and, for a cut sheet, its wires' lengths. `rebar.set_partition` puts sets, sheets and fabric areas in a partition (`rxd:rebar_partition`; a fabric area's sheets take its partition). Sequences per partition and kind (rebar, fabric) are kept on the project (`rxd:rebar_numbers`: start, each identity's number, locks). An identity met first takes the next free number in creation order and keeps it, so numbers do not move when other elements go and gaps can appear; numbers are kept on every rebar and fabric change. `reinforcement_numbering.list`, `.renumber` (creation order, or `remove_gaps` in number order; locked numbers stay and are skipped; `start`), `.set` (a number another identity in use has is refused, naming it; lock) and `.apply` (the dialog's edits as one step). `rebar.info` reports the number and partition; the number is the set's or sheet's IFC `Tag`. Concrete › Settings › **Reinforcement Numbers** (choose a partition and sequence; a grid of numbers with count, elements and lock; start, Remove gaps, Renumber; a clashing number marks the other row; Select Elements); Properties show Rebar Number and edit Partition. Not yet: couplers, `Pset_PrecastConcreteElementFabrication.PieceMark`, the filter box, the varying-set ranges (STR-RBR-005).

### 4.2.17 Rebar visibility and presentation
**ID:** STR-RBR-017 · **Priority:** P2 · **Ref:** research/03 §3.2 ("Rebar presentation", "View visibility"), §3.8

**Purpose.** Control, per view, which bars of a set are drawn and whether they show through or as solids, so that drawings stay readable.

**Workflow.**
1. Select one or more rebar sets (or area, path or fabric systems).
2. On the contextual tab, choose *View Visibility States* (a grid of the project's views with *Unobscured* and *Solid* check boxes per view; *Solid* is enabled only for 3D views), or choose a presentation mode in the *Presentation* panel, which applies to the active view.
3. For *Select*, click the bars to show; **Enter** finishes. The picks are journaled as micro-operations so an unfinished pick session is recovered after a crash (§2.1 of the conventions).

**Behaviour & rules.**
- **Per-instance, per-view visibility states:**
  - *View unobscured*: the bars show through the host.
  - *View as solid*: applies in 3D views at Fine detail. At Coarse and Medium detail bars are drawn as centrelines.
- Default visibility: the placement view and all section views. Rebar cut by a section is always shown.
- **Set presentation per view:** Show All, Show First/Last, Show Middle, or Select (pick the bars to show).
  - First/Last and Middle draw a **set extent line** with end ticks spanning the whole set, so the distribution is still shown.
  - The default for new sets comes from Reinforcement Settings (STR-RBR-002).
  - Select keeps bar indices; if the bar count later drops below a picked index, that pick is dropped and the view falls back to Show All when no picks remain.
- **Spliced set presentation:** show representative bars per lap zone.
- Presentation changes only what is drawn. Tags, schedules and IFC export always count every bar.
- View templates (chapter 5) can carry a rebar presentation default that overrides the per-set mode in views using the template.
- Visibility and presentation edits are view data and are undoable.

**Data (IFC mapping).** View-dependent settings are stored with the view's own RXD data (chapter 5), as a map from rebar GlobalId to Unobscured, Solid and Presentation (mode plus selected indices). Nothing is written to the rebar's IFC entity.

**Commands.**
- `rebar.set_view_visibility(rebar_ids[], view_id, unobscured?, solid?)`
- `rebar.set_presentation(rebar_ids[], view_id, mode, selected_indices?)`

**Acceptance criteria.**
- [x] *Show Middle* in a plan view draws one representative bar and the set extent line, and other views are not affected.
- [x] A set set to *Unobscured* in a 3D view is visible through its concrete host there, and stays hidden by the host in a second 3D view.
- [ ] A set of 15 bars shown with *Show First/Last* still tags as quantity 15 and exports 15 bar bodies.
- [x] *Solid* cannot be ticked for a plan view in the View Visibility States grid.

*Built (2026-10-19):* per view and per rebar set or area, path or fabric system, `rebar.set_view_visibility` (unobscured; solid, refused for views that are not 3D) and `rebar.set_presentation` (all, first_last, middle, select with indices) store view data (`rxd:rebar_view` on the view, by GlobalId; nothing on the rebar), and `rebar.view_states` lists a set's states in every view. Each view draws its rebar accordingly: tubes for solid sets in 3D views at Fine detail, centrelines otherwise; unobscured rebar through its host (a renderer x-ray layer for geometry and lines); First/Last and Middle with the set's extent line and end ticks; Select's picks past the bar count dropped, falling back to all. Clicking a drawn bar selects its set. The default presentation for sets without their own comes from Reinforcement Settings (`presentation`). Counts, numbers and the export keep every bar. The contextual tab of a set has **Show All**, **First/Last**, **Middle**, **Select Bars** (click bars, Enter finishes) and **View Visibility States** (a grid of the views, Solid only for 3D views); an unsaved `{3D}` view is saved first. Not yet: the default of showing rebar only in its placement and section views, spliced-set presentation, view template defaults, journaling of Select picks, and the tag quantity check (tags are STR-RBR-018).

### 4.2.18 Rebar documentation
**ID:** STR-RBR-018 · **Priority:** P2 · **Ref:** research/03 §3.8

**Purpose.** Annotate and schedule reinforcement for placing drawings and bar bending schedules.

**Workflow.**
- **Tag:** *Annotate › Tag by Category*, click a set; the tag attaches to the set (or to the representative bar shown by STR-RBR-017).
- **Multi-rebar annotation:** choose *Aligned* or *Linear*, pick one or more sets, place the dimension line, then the tag. Picks are journaled as micro-operations (§2.1 of the conventions).
- **Bending detail:** select a set, choose *Bending Detail*, click to place in the view; the scale and rotation can be set before the click.

**Behaviour & rules.**
- **Rebar tags** read number, shape code, bar size, spacing and quantity.
- **Multi-rebar annotation:** an aligned or linear dimension plus a tag that spans a set or several sets.
  - The dimension measures the set extent and the tag reads quantity, size and spacing (for example "15 Ø12 @ 150").
  - Several sets are accepted only if they are parallel; otherwise the pick is refused with a message.
  - The annotation follows the sets when they move and is deleted with the last set it references.
- **Bending detail:** a view-specific annotation that draws a bar's shape with its segment dimensions. It updates when the bar changes.
  - Segment labels and dimension values use the shape's A–R parameters after rounding (STR-RBR-002). Hooks are drawn with their angle.
  - Varying sets (STR-RBR-005) show the range of each varying segment ("1 200–1 650").
- **Rebar schedule** (chapter 5 schedule engine): bar number, shape code, segments A–R, quantity, total length and mass. It can be filtered by partition.
  - Mass is length × nominal mass per metre of the bar type. Totals use rounded lengths when rounding is on.
  - A bending-schedule template that groups by partition and bar number is shipped.

**Data (IFC mapping).** Annotation entities as defined in chapter 5. Schedule fields read `IfcReinforcingBar`, `IfcReinforcingBarType` and RXD element data (`rebar`). Multi-rebar annotations and bending details store the GlobalIds of their referenced sets in their own view-specific RXD data.

**Commands.**
- `rebar_tag.place(rebar_id, view_id, point, tag_type_id) -> id`
- `multi_rebar_annotation.place(rebar_ids[], view_id, kind: "aligned"|"linear", line) -> id`
- `bending_detail.place(rebar_id, view_id, point, scale?) -> id`

**Acceptance criteria.**
- [x] Changing segment B of a bar updates its bending detail and the schedule's B column in the same regeneration.
- [x] A multi-rebar annotation on a set of 15 Ø12 bars at 150 mm reads "15 Ø12 @ 150" and its dimension equals the set extent (2 100 mm).
- [x] Picking two non-parallel sets for one multi-rebar annotation is refused with a message.
- [x] The schedule's mass column for 10 bars of 6 m Ø16 (1.578 kg/m) shows 94.7 kg.

*Built (2026-10-19):* rebar sets schedule with the fields `rebar.number`, `rebar.partition`, `rebar.shape`, `rebar.bar_type`, `rebar.quantity`, `rebar.spacing`, `rebar.bar_length`, `rebar.total_length`, `rebar.mass` (rounded total length × the bar's nominal mass per metre, π d²/4 × 7 850 kg/m³), `rebar.A` … `rebar.R` (after segment rounding) and `rebar.description` ("15 Ø12 @ 150"); `rebar_schedule.create` makes the shipped Bar Bending Schedule (partition, number, shape, bar type, A–E, quantity, lengths, mass), grouped by partition and number. The **Rebar Tag** reads the number and description; `rebar_tag.place` tags a set in a plan, hanging from its middle bar. `multi_rebar_annotation.place` (aligned square to the bars, or linear along x or y) is a dimension from the first bar to the last of one or more parallel sets (others refused) reading quantity, size and spacing; `bending_detail.place` draws the middle bar flattened in its own plane at a point, scale and rotation, with the number, bar type, shape code and segment values. Both are plan annotations (`anno.multi_rebar`, `anno.bending_detail`) that read their sets when drawn, so a set's change shows at once; a multi-rebar annotation goes with the last set it references and a bending detail with its set; `rebar_annotation.list` reports them as drawn. The stroke font gains Ø, @ and :. Concrete › Documentation (Rebar Tag, Multi-Rebar Aligned and Linear, Bending Detail, Bar Bending Schedule) and the set's contextual tab; click where each goes. Not yet: tags in sections and 3D views, multi-rebar annotations with a separate tag placement, hook angles drawn on bending details, varying-set ranges, schedule filters by partition (sort and group work), fabric and coupler schedules.
