*Built (2026-10-18):* `structural_connection.automate` finds the joins in the framing (each column's foot where no column stands below; each beam end on the column or girder it rests on, from the beams' supports; each brace end at the column, else the beam, its axis meets within 500 mm), limited to the given members' joins, and gives each the type of the first matching rule. Rules match the join kind (`column_base`, `beam_column`, `beam_beam`, `brace`), the main and connected members' sections and the connected member's depth range; a rule without a range uses its type's range of applicability (shear plate 150–920 mm, end plate 200–920 mm deep). The built-in *Default* rule set gives base plates, shear plates (beam–column and beam–beam) and gussets; projects keep their own in `rxd:connection_rules` (`structural_connection.set_rule_set`, `rule_sets`), or `rules` are passed with the call (a Lua or JSON table). Only steel members are connected; joins with a connection on the same members are skipped (*Skip*) or a generic one gets the type (*Replace generic only*); where a generator fails a generic connection marked Failed holds the join. A preview changes nothing (not even the undo history); `apply_automation` takes the preview's report itself rather than an id. Runs (time, rule set, counts) are kept in `rxd:connection_runs`. Steel › Connections › **Automate Connections**: the rule set, the existing-joins choice and Preview; the preview marks each join in 3D views by type (grey where skipped), with the log (status, join, type, members, reason), Apply and Save CSV. Gussets now stop at the bottom of a beam framing into the column at a brace's top (or the top of one at its foot), and their bolts with them. Not yet: background jobs, angle and grade conditions in rules, a rule set editor dialog, and classifying joins by section family beyond sections.

### 4.4.5 Plates
**ID:** STR-STL-005 · **Priority:** P2 · **Ref:** research/03 §5.3

**Workflow.**
1. Choose *Steel › Plate*. Pick the placement plane: the current work plane, or a planar face of a steel element.
2. Sketch a single closed contour with lines and arcs (rectangle, polygon and circle tools are offered). Each sketch operation is journaled as a micro-operation, so an unfinished sketch is recovered after a crash (§2.1 of the conventions).
3. Finish. Reviera validates the contour and creates the plate.

**Behaviour & rules.**
- Parameters: thickness (default 10 mm, 1–200 mm), material (steel grade), coating and justification (*Top*, *Centre* or *Bottom* relative to the sketch plane), plus a free *Part role* (for example stiffener, gusset, cap plate) used by numbering and schedules.
- The contour must be one closed, non-self-intersecting loop. Several loops or gaps are refused and the offending segment is highlighted. Holes in plates are made with hole patterns or contour cuts (STR-STL-006, STR-STL-008), not inner loops.
- Arcs in the contour are approximated by corner cuts.
- A plate sketched on a face is hosted by that face: it moves with the element and its sketch plane updates when the face moves. If the face disappears the plate stays in place, becomes unhosted and a warning names it.
- *Edit Contour* reopens the sketch. Corner cuts (STR-STL-008) can be applied afterwards.
- Folded plates are produced only by connections. After *Break* they become independent, and their sketch can no longer be edited.
- Plates are drawn only at Fine detail (STR-STL-001), and are valid targets for bolts, welds and cuts.

**Data (IFC mapping).** `IfcPlate` (PredefinedType `SHEET`, or `USERDEFINED` "FOLDED"), typed by `IfcPlateType`. `Pset_PlateCommon`. Geometry: an extruded area solid from the contour. Material: `IfcMaterialLayerSetUsage` with one layer of the plate thickness. The editable contour, justification and host face reference are RXD element data (`constraints`).

**Commands.** `plate.create(work_plane | face_ref, contour_curves[], thickness, material_id, justification) -> id`

**Acceptance criteria.**
- [x] A plate sketched on a column flange face exports as `IfcPlate` with the correct thickness.
- [ ] A contour with a gap of 2 mm is refused at *Finish* and the open segment end is highlighted.
- [x] A 15 mm plate with *Bottom* justification on a flange face sits fully outside the flange, with its bottom face on the flange face.
- [x] Moving the hosting column moves the plate with it.

*Built (2026-10-18):* `plate.create` on any work plane or on a named **face** of a column, beam, brace or plate (`face.list`: flange_1, flange_2, web_1, web_2, start, end; top, bottom), the face plane following its element. The contour is corners or line and arc segments (arcs flattened); it must close within 0.1 mm (`plate.open_contour` names the segment), not cross itself and have an area; thickness 1–200 mm (default 10 mm); justification bottom (outside a face), centre or top; material, coating and role (`Pset_PlateCommon.Reference`). `plate.set` (Edit Contour and the rest) and `plate.info`. A plate on a face moves with its element; when the element is deleted the plate stays where it was, unhosted. Plates move, rotate and mirror with Modify (their plane is then fixed in space). IfcPlate (SHEET) with a B-rep body, drawn at Fine detail, category Structural Connections. Steel › **Plate**: with one element selected, pick its face; otherwise the view's work plane; click the corners, Enter finishes. Properties: thickness, justification, role, material, the plane and whether hosted. The gap check refuses the contour but the window cannot yet highlight the open end (sketches are closed by clicks). Not yet: arcs kept as arcs, corner cuts, `IfcMaterialLayerSetUsage`, extruded-solid bodies, folded plates, the sketch journal.

### 4.4.6 Bolts, anchors, holes and shear studs
**ID:** STR-STL-006 · **Priority:** P2 · **Ref:** research/03 §5.3 · screenshots/structure_mep/steel_fabrication_elements_plate_anchors.png

**Workflow.**
1. Select the steel elements to join with Ctrl+click, then press Enter.
2. Pick the face the pattern is perpendicular to.
3. Sketch a **rectangular** or **circular** pattern. Finish.

**Behaviour & rules.**
- **Bolts:**
  - standard, grade, diameter and assembly (for example bolt + nut + 2 washers)
  - bolt length and **grip length**, both calculated
  - grip length increase
  - **hole definition** per connected element (type, tolerance, slotted)
  - inverted
  - finish calculation at gap
  - location (site or shop) and coating
  - count and spacing per direction, and edge distances
- **Anchors:** the same flow, between concrete and steel. Parameters: standard, length and grade.
- **Holes:** a pattern without fasteners.
- **Shear studs:** a pattern on a steel element. Parameters: standard, diameter and length.
- Bolt standards are open data tables (dimensions per standard). Reviera ships tables only where their content is not copyrighted, and users can add their own.
- The shape of a pattern can be edited after placement.

**Data (IFC mapping).**

| Element | IFC |
|---------|-----|
| Bolt | `IfcMechanicalFastener` `BOLT`, NominalDiameter, NominalLength; `Pset_MechanicalFastenerBolt` (ThreadDiameter, ThreadLength, NutsCount, WashersCount, …) |
| Anchor | `IfcMechanicalFastener` `ANCHORBOLT` |
| Shear stud | `IfcMechanicalFastener` `STUDSHEARCONNECTOR` |
| Hole | `IfcOpeningElement` `OPENING` with `IfcRelVoidsElement` in each pierced element |

A pattern is an `IfcElementAssembly` `USERDEFINED` "FASTENER_GROUP" that aggregates its fasteners, or a single fastener with `IfcMappedItem` copies. The joined elements are related with `IfcRelConnectsWithRealizingElements`. Pattern parameters (kind, counts, spacings, grip, location, hole definitions) are RXD element data (`constraints`).

**Commands.**
- `bolt_pattern.create(element_ids[], face_ref, pattern: "rect"|"circle", params) -> id`
- `anchor_pattern.create(...)`
- `hole_pattern.create(...)`
- `shear_stud_pattern.create(...)`

**Acceptance criteria.**
- [x] A 2 × 3 M20 bolt pattern through a 15 mm plate and a 10 mm web reports a grip length of 25 mm and creates 6 holes in each element.
- [x] An exported bolt is an `IfcMechanicalFastener` with `NominalDiameter` = 20 mm.

*Built (2026-10-18):* `bolt_pattern.create`, `anchor_pattern.create`, `hole_pattern.create` and `shear_stud_pattern.create`: the elements, the plane the fasteners are square to (a work plane or a face) and a layout (`rect`: rows, columns, spacings, centre; `circle`: count, radius, centre, start angle). Each fastener runs along the plane's normal; the grip (from the first element's entry to the last one's exit, taking each element's first solid run, so an I-section's far flange is not counted, plus a grip increase), the bolt length under the head (grip, two washers, a nut and thread beyond, rounded up to 5 mm or 1/4"), and the holes made in each element are found from the elements' bodies when the pattern is made or edited and kept with it. Bolt proportions come from generic metric and inch tables (not a standard's copyrighted table); hole tolerance 2 mm or 1/16"; slots, inverted bolts, shop or site, coating, anchors' and studs' lengths. The pattern is an IfcElementAssembly (USERDEFINED, FASTENER_GROUP) aggregating IfcMechanicalFastener elements (BOLT, ANCHORBOLT, STUDSHEARCONNECTOR) with NominalDiameter and NominalLength; each hole is an IfcOpeningElement (OPENING, marked `rxd:hole`) voiding its element, rewritten on save, and is cut in the element's body by the solid kernel (so views and the overlap finder show it). `fastener_pattern.set` edits a pattern and finds its grip again; `fastener_pattern.info` reports it. A pattern goes when one of its elements is deleted. Steel › **Bolts**: kind, face and layout in a dialog, then a click for the centre; Properties show diameter, grip, length, hole size, holes per element and location. Not yet: user bolt tables, the hole definition per element, finishing the grip at a gap, editing the pattern's shape by grips, `IfcRelConnectsWithRealizingElements`.

### 4.4.7 Welds
**ID:** STR-STL-007 · **Priority:** P2 · **Ref:** research/03 §5.3

**Purpose.** Record shop and site welds between steel elements, with the data a fabricator needs.

**Workflow.** Choose *Steel › Welds*. Select the elements to weld (two or more steel elements, Ctrl+click), press Enter, then pick an available **edge**. Only edges where the selected elements touch within 1 mm are offered and highlighted. A cross symbol represents the weld. Picks are journaled as micro-operations (§2.1 of the conventions).

**Behaviour & rules.**
- Parameters: main and double weld type, thickness, location (site or shop), surface shape and preparation. Values come from data tables, not free text.
  - Weld types include fillet, butt (square, single-V, single-bevel, double-V), plug and spot; surface shapes flat, convex and concave. The tables are open data files that users can extend.
  - Thickness is the throat (a) or leg size, > 0 mm; length defaults to the picked edge and can be shortened; an *Intermittent* option takes segment length and pitch.
- Welds **do not move** with their elements. When geometry changes they are flagged for review.
  - Review means: the weld keeps its position, a *needs review* status appears in Properties and in the warnings list, and *Accept* clears it once the user has checked or re-picked the edge.
  - If one of the welded elements is deleted, the weld is deleted with it (STR-GEN-002).
- Welds cannot be placed on sub-elements of custom connections (STR-STL-003).
- Shop welds join elements into one **assembly** for assembly marks (STR-STL-010); site welds do not.
- Welds are drawn only at Fine detail. Weld symbols in drawings are annotations of chapter 5 that read the weld parameters.

**Data (IFC mapping).** `IfcFastener` with PredefinedType `WELD`, and `Pset_FastenerWeld` (Type1, Type2, Surface1, Surface2, Process, a, l, Intermittent, …). Related with `IfcRelConnectsWithRealizingElements`. The picked edge reference, location (site or shop) and review status are RXD element data (`structural`).

**Commands.** `weld.create(element_ids[], edge_ref, params) -> id`

**Acceptance criteria.**
- [x] Moving a plate with a weld marks the weld "needs review" and leaves its position unchanged.
- [x] Picking an edge where the selected elements do not touch is not possible: the edge is not highlighted.
- [x] A 6 mm fillet weld exports as `IfcFastener` (`WELD`) with `Pset_FastenerWeld.a` = 6 mm.
- [x] A plate shop-welded to a beam gets the beam's assembly mark; the same plate site-welded does not.

*Built (2026-10-18):* `weld.edges` lists the edges of the selected elements (where their faces fold) that touch every other element within 1 mm along their length; `weld.create` refuses any other edge (`weld.not_touching`). The weld fills the corner between the faces at the edge (its legs along them, leaving out the faces where the elements bear on each other), with type and second type, throat `a` (default 6 mm), length (from the edge's start), surface, preparation, shop or site and intermittent segments, values checked against the open weld table (`data/steel/weld_types.json`, `weld.tables`). Welds keep their place: each element's shape is recorded, and `weld.info` and `weld.review` report *needs review* once one changes until `weld.set` with `accept`. A weld goes when one of its elements is deleted. IfcFastener (WELD) with `Pset_FastenerWeld` (Type1, Type2, Surface1, a, l, Intermittent, Process). Steel › **Weld**: in a 3D view the touching edges are drawn, the one under the cursor highlighted; click it, then type, throat and location. Properties: type, throat, length, location, review status and Accept. Not yet: assembly marks from shop welds (STR-STL-010), weld symbols in drawings, project additions to the weld table, the pick journal.

### 4.4.8 Modifiers and parametric cuts
**ID:** STR-STL-008 · **Priority:** P2 · **Ref:** research/03 §5.4

| Tool | Behaviour | Command |
|------|-----------|---------|
| **Corner Cut** (plates) | Convex or concave, straight or radius | `steel_modifier.corner_cut(plate_id, corner_ref, kind, size)` |
| **Cope Skewed** (framing) | Skewed cope at a member end | `steel_modifier.cope_skewed(member_id, end, params)` |
| **Shorten** | A cut at the nearest end; positive shortens, negative extends; angles across height and width give diagonal cuts | `steel_modifier.shorten(member_id, end, length, angle_h?, angle_w?)` |
| **Contour Cut** | A sketched hole or notch through framing or plates, with gap width, radius, boring and boundary distances | `steel_modifier.contour_cut(element_id, face_ref, curves[], params)` |
| **Cope** (parametric) | Select intersecting members, then Enter. A swap control chooses which member is cut. | `steel_cut.cope(member_ids[], cut_member_id?)` |
| **Miter**, **Saw Cut – Flange**, **Saw Cut – Web** | End cuts between two members | `steel_cut.miter(a, b)`, `steel_cut.saw(a, b, part: "flange"|"web")` |
| **Cut Through** | Cuts one element by the shape of another, plus a gap | `steel_cut.cut_through(cut_id, cutter_id, gap)` |
| **Cut By** | Cuts by the intersecting geometry | `steel_cut.cut_by(cut_id, cutter_id)` |

**Behaviour & rules.**
- Parametric cuts form a **sub-connection** (shown as a dashed box) that cannot be retyped.
- Modifiers and cuts regenerate when their members move. Void cuts and connections can be combined.
- Shape handles extend a member beyond its shorten modifier.
- **Uncope** (*Parametric Cuts › Uncope*, `steel_cut.uncope(member_ids[])`): select one or more members that carry copes, then press Enter. Every parametric cope on those members is removed and their ends return to the uncut shape. A sub-connection left with no cuts is deleted; one that still holds other cuts (for example a miter) is kept. Copes that belong to a detailed connection (STR-CONN-001) are not removed; they are listed as skipped, because editing them belongs to the connection's parameters. Selecting members with no copes is reported as "nothing to remove" and makes no transaction.
- Deleting a cut opening directly (selecting its dashed box contents) has the same effect for that single cut.

**Data (IFC mapping).** Cuts are `IfcOpeningElement` (PredefinedType `OPENING`, or `USERDEFINED` "COPE", "MITER", …) with `IfcRelVoidsElement`. Their parameters are RXD element data (`constraints`). A sub-connection is an `IfcElementAssembly` `USERDEFINED` "SUB_CONNECTION".

**Commands.** The commands are listed in the table above, plus `steel_cut.uncope(member_ids[])`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- [x] A cope between a secondary beam and a girder removes the girder's flange zone from the secondary beam's end and updates when the girder depth changes.
- [x] *Uncope* on that secondary beam restores its full end profile, deletes the now-empty sub-connection and is undone in one step.
- [ ] *Uncope* on a beam whose cope belongs to a shear-plate connection leaves the cope and reports it as skipped.

*Built (2026-10-18):* every cut is an element of its own (IfcOpeningElement, USERDEFINED with ObjectType COPE, COPE_SKEWED, MITER, SAW_CUT, SHORTEN, CONTOUR_CUT, CUT_THROUGH or CUT_BY) whose cutter solid is worked out from the members whenever bodies are built, and subtracted from the target's body by the solid kernel (so the 3D view, plans and the overlap finder see it); IFC gets the opening's B-rep voiding the target. The cuts one command makes form a sub-connection (IfcElementAssembly SUB_CONNECTION). `steel_cut.cope` cuts the member whose end is at the joint (or the one named) by the other's flange zones (flange thickness plus a clearance, 13 mm or 1/2", across the flange width plus the clearance), following its depth; `steel_modifier.cope_skewed` notches a member end's top and/or bottom by depth, length and angle; `steel_cut.miter` cuts two members on the plane halving their corner; `steel_cut.saw` cuts a member flush with another's nearer flange or web face; `steel_modifier.shorten` moves a beam or brace end back (forward when negative) through its end extension, with angles across the height and width for a diagonal end; `steel_modifier.contour_cut` cuts a sketched contour on a work plane or face, through or to a depth; `steel_cut.cut_through` (with a gap) and `steel_cut.cut_by` subtract another element's body; `steel_modifier.corner_cut` cuts a plate's corner straight, convex or concave. `steel_cut.uncope` removes copes and empty sub-connections in one step, skipping copes owned by a connection (none of the built-in library types make copes yet, so this path is untested) and failing with `uncope.nothing` when there is nothing to remove; `steel_cut.list` reports the cuts. Cuts go when their elements go. the Steel tab has Cope, Miter, Saw Cut, Cut Through, Cut By, Uncope, Shorten, Corner Cut and Contour Cut (sketched like a plate). Not yet: the dashed sub-connection box in views, shape handles past a shorten, boring and boundary distances on contour cuts, and copes made by connection types.

### 4.4.9 Connection code checking (provider)
**ID:** STR-STL-009 · **Priority:** P2 · **Ref:** research/03 §2.9 ("Code checking"), §5.2

**Purpose.** Check detailed connections against a design code, and size them, through a pluggable provider rather than a built-in proprietary checker.

**Workflow.**
1. Select one or more detailed connections whose instance has *Override by Instance* on (STR-CONN-001), so that the code-check tab is available.
2. In Modify Parameters, open the code-check tab: choose the provider, the design code the provider offers (for example a Eurocode 3 or AISC 360 module) and the design forces. Forces come from the connection's *Design Forces* property per load case or combination, or from the member end forces of a result package (STR-RES-001).
3. Choose *Check*, *Presize* or *Report*. Checks run in the background (ANA-GEN-001).

**Behaviour & rules.**
- *Check*, *Presize* and *Report* on connections go through a **connection design provider** (ANA-PLUG-001 kind `structural`, capability `connection_check`).
- **Provider input:** member sections and materials, connection type and parameters (plates, bolts, welds), geometry of the join, and the design forces per load group. **Output:** per check item (for example bolt shear, bearing, block tearing, weld resistance) the resistance, the action, the utilisation ratio and pass or fail, plus an overall status and a report file (HTML or PDF).
- Presize grows bolt diameter and plate and weld thickness step by step until the check passes.
  - Steps follow the bolt and plate tables (STR-STL-006). Presize stops with *Failed* after the largest size, or after 20 iterations, and reports which item still fails.
  - Presize changes connection parameters, so it is an undoable model edit; the provider never edits the model directly.
- Status (NotCalculated, Failed or OK) and the report path are written to RXD element data (`structural`).
- Any later change to the connection, its members or its design forces resets the status to *NotCalculated* (stale).
- Connections without design forces are refused with a message naming them.
- Reviera does not bundle a code checker in the first release. The provider interface and a sample Lua provider for simple bolt shear and bearing checks are supplied.

**Data (IFC mapping).** No IFC equivalent for check results. Status, utilisation (the maximum ratio), code, provider, date and report path are RXD element data (`structural`) on the connection. The report file is referenced from the model with `IfcDocumentReference` through `IfcRelAssociatesDocument`.

**Commands.**
- `structural_connection.check(connection_ids[], provider_id, code) -> report`
- `structural_connection.presize(connection_ids[], provider_id, code)`

**Acceptance criteria.**
- [x] With the sample provider, a bolt group whose design shear exceeds its capacity gets status Failed and a report that shows the utilisation ratio.
- [x] Presize on that connection increases the bolt diameter until the utilisation is ≤ 1.0, sets status OK, and is undone in one step.
- [x] Changing the beam size after a successful check resets the status to *NotCalculated*.
- [x] Checking a connection with no design forces is refused with a message naming it.

*Built (2026-10-19):* connections keep design forces per load case or combination (`structural_connection.set_design_forces`: N tension positive, V in the connected member's depth direction, Vh across, M; N and N·m), edited in Properties as `group: N, V, Vh, M` in kN. A provider is a Lua plugin with `capability = "connection_check"`, its `codes` and a `check(input)` function, run against a read-only host (it cannot run commands); `connection_check.providers` lists them. Its input (`reviera_core::connection_check::CheckInput`, SI units) carries the code, the connection's type and parameters, the bolt group (count, diameter, area, grade with fub and the AISC nominal shear stress, hole size, pitch, edge), the plies the bolts bear on (plate, the beam's web, the column's flange, a tube's wall, with fy and fu from the materials library), the weld lines (size, length, electrode strength), the members' sections and materials, and the forces; its answer is a list of items (name, load group, action, resistance, ratio, ok, and the parameter that would strengthen it). `structural_connection.check` records the answer (`record_check`): status OK when every item passes, utilisation the largest ratio, provider, code and date, and a hash of the input answered, so any later change to the connection, its members or its forces shows *not calculated* (`check_status`); the connection's code-check flag (STR-CONN-001) follows. `structural_connection.presize` asks again with the failing items' parameters one step larger (bolt, plate and weld tables by region; bolt counts by one), at most 20 rounds, then sets the sizes and records the answer, all one undo step; one that cannot pass is recorded as failed with the items still failing. `structural_connection.check_report` writes an HTML report. The built-in sample provider (MIT, `connection_check_sample`) checks bolt shear, bearing and tear-out on each ply, bolt tension and fillet welds to AISC 360-16 LRFD or EN 1993-1-8 (simplified: no eccentricity, prying or block shear); bearing on a member's web grows the bolt count, as bigger bolts only shorten the tear-out edge. Steel › Connections › Check, Presize and Check Report (asking for the provider and code); Properties show the status and each item's ratio. Not yet: forces taken from analysis results, background jobs, the provider kinds of ANA-PLUG-001 (only Lua plugins), anchor rod checks, and the report as an `IfcDocumentReference`.

### 4.4.10 Steel interoperability and fabrication output
**ID:** STR-STL-010 · **Priority:** P2 · **Ref:** research/03 §5.5

**Behaviour & rules.**
- **IFC is the primary exchange format** with detailing software. Members, plates, fasteners, welds, openings and connection assemblies all round-trip as described above.
- **Part and assembly marks:**
  - *Steel › Numbering* assigns part marks to identical parts and assembly marks to identical assemblies (main member plus everything welded to it in the shop).
  - The part mark is written to `IfcElement.Tag`. The assembly mark is written to the assembly's `Tag`. A copy of both is kept in RXD element data (`structural`) with the numbering options.
  - An assembly is an `IfcElementAssembly` `USERDEFINED` "STEEL_ASSEMBLY".
- **[Suggestion] NC export** as a plugin: per-part CNC files in the openly documented DSTV NC1 format, generated from member profiles, holes, cuts and plates.
- Proprietary exchange formats used by the reference product's detailing integration are **not** supported (§4.17).

**Commands.**
- `steel_numbering.run(scope, options) -> report`
- `steel_nc.export(scope, folder, format="dstv")` (plugin)

**Acceptance criteria.**
- [x] Two identical beams with identical holes get the same part mark. Adding one hole to one beam gives it a new mark.

*Built (2026-10-19):* `steel_numbering.run` (and `steel_numbering.preview`, which changes nothing). Parts are steel columns, beams and braces, plates placed by hand and connection plates. A member's mark compares its section, length, holes (fastener patterns' and connection bolts', in standard holes 2 mm or 1/16" over) and cut solids in its own frame, either way round (and mirrored for symmetric sections); a plate's compares its thickness, outline, holes and cuts in every start corner, direction and mirror of its outline, so a plate turned or moved keeps its mark. Marks are a prefix and a number by kind (`c`, `b`, `br`, `p`; options for prefixes and the first number). An assembly is a main member (the longest; else the biggest plate) and everything shop-welded to it: shop welds, and connection plates welded to their member (shear plate and gusset to the main member, end plate to the beam, base plate to the column); site welds and bolts do not join. Identical assemblies (the main mark and the other parts' marks and places in its frame) share a mark in capitals. The part mark goes to `Tag` and `rxd:steel_marks` (with the assembly mark and options); each assembly is an IfcElementAssembly (USERDEFINED STEEL_ASSEMBLY) tagged with its mark, aggregating its members and hand-placed plates in IFC (connection plates stay aggregated by their connections, beam system and truss members by theirs), made again on every run. NC export (`steel_nc.export`, built in rather than a plugin) writes one DSTV NC1 file per part mark with its quantity through the MIT `reviera-dstv` crate (`clients/dstv`; writer and reader of the 7th edition's ST header, BO, AK, IK and EN blocks): members with profile code, dimensions, weight and painting surface per metre and holes on the web (`v`, `h`) and flanges (`o`, `u`); plates (`B`) in their smallest rectangle with their outline (`AK`, anticlockwise) and holes. Steel › Fabrication › **Numbering** (with the marks listed) and **NC Export**; Properties show an element's part and assembly marks. Not yet: member copes and cuts as NC contours, skew cut angles, keeping marks stable across model changes, and marks in schedules and tags on drawings.

---

## 4.5 Concrete detailing and precast

All features in this section are **P2**. Precast tools are on *Concrete › Precast Detailing* and *Precast Settings*. Precast is a **rule-driven pipeline**:
1. split walls and slabs into pieces
2. reinforce the pieces and add mounting parts
3. generate shop drawings
4. export CAM data

Ref: research/03 §6.1

### 4.5.1 Precast configuration
**ID:** STR-PRE-001 · **Priority:** P2 · **Ref:** research/03 §6.1

**Purpose.** One tree-structured dialog holds all precast rules.

**UI.** *Concrete › Precast Settings › Configuration* (`precast_config.show()`). Tree:
- Concrete
  - Wall: Solid Wall, Double Wall
  - Slab: Solid, Hollow-core, Lattice-girder slab

  Each with Segmentation, Reinforcement, Connections (mounting parts) and Shop Drawing nodes.
- Built-in parts: Annotations, Dimensioning
- CAM Export
- Data folder path for templates and families

**What each node edits:**

| Node | Contents | Validation |
|------|----------|------------|
| Segmentation | The rules of STR-PRE-002: minimum and maximum length or width and height, maximum weight, joint gaps, minimum distance to openings, profile overlap; for hollow-core, the slab family, division profile, minimum width and strand diameter | Minimum ≤ maximum; gaps 0–100 mm; maximum weight > 0 t; families must be loaded |
| Reinforcement | Reinforcement types per thickness range (area, edge, lattice girder), as used by STR-PRE-003; custom fabric sheet rules (STR-PRE-004) | Thickness ranges must not overlap; bar and mesh types must exist |
| Connections | Mounting-part rules (STR-PRE-005): part family, count by weight bands, edge distances, symmetry | Weight bands must be contiguous and ascending |
| Shop Drawing | Sheet template, centre-of-gravity symbol, dimension type and distances, descriptions (STR-PRE-006) | Template must contain the required viewports |
| Annotations / Dimensioning | Tag family per category, dimension rules per category | Tag families must be loaded |
| CAM Export | Writer per format, output folder and filename rule (STR-PRE-007) | Filename rule must parse |
| Data folder | Path to templates and families | Path must exist and be readable |

- Invalid values are marked in the tree node and in the cell, and *OK* is disabled until they are fixed.
- *OK* commits as one transaction. The dialog shows how many existing assemblies were made with an older configuration version; Reviera does not re-split or re-reinforce them automatically, but offers *Re-run on affected assemblies* (STR-PRE-002 `precast.resplit`, STR-PRE-003).
- *Export…* and *Import…* buttons call the commands below. Import replaces the whole configuration after a confirmation; references to families not loaded in the project are listed so they can be loaded.
- A new project's configuration comes from its template; Reviera ships an open default configuration.

**Data (IFC mapping).** No IFC equivalent. **RXD document** `fabrication` (precast configuration section), versioned. It can be exported and imported as a standalone file to share between projects. Each version increments on commit; the version used is recorded on each precast assembly (RXD element data `structural`, rule snapshot hash, STR-PRE-002). The standalone file is JSON with a schema version.

**Commands.**
- `precast_config.get(path) -> value`
- `precast_config.set(path, value)`
- `precast_config.export(file)`
- `precast_config.import(file) -> {version, missing[]}`
- `precast_config.apply(config) -> version`
- `precast_config.affected() -> {version, older[]}`
- `precast_config.show()`

`path` addresses a node and key, for example `wall.solid.segmentation.max_length`. `set` applies the dialog's validation and returns an error naming the rule.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- [x] A configuration exported from one project and imported into another produces identical segmentation results on an identical wall.
- [x] Entering a minimum wall length of 9 m with a maximum of 8 m marks the Segmentation node invalid and disables *OK*.
- [x] After changing the maximum weight, the dialog reports how many existing assemblies used the previous version and offers to re-run on them.
- [x] `precast_config.set("wall.solid.segmentation.max_length", -1)` fails with a message naming the rule.

*Built (2026-10-19):* the configuration is the RXD document `rxd:fabrication` on the project (JSON: `version`, `density` in t/m³, `auto_update`, `wall.{solid,double}` and `slab.{solid,hollow_core,lattice_girder}` each with `segmentation`, `reinforcement`, `connections`, `shop_drawing`; `annotations`, `dimensioning`, `cam.{format,folder,filename}`, `data_folder`; lengths in metres, weights in tonnes). Starting values, Reviera's own, provisional pending subject-matter expert review (Q14, `EXPERT_REVIEW.md`): walls 0.6–8 m long, 0.3–4 m high, 12 t, 20 mm joints, 200 mm from openings; slabs 0.6–2.5 m wide (hollow-core 0.3–1.2 m, 12.5 mm strands), 12 t, 20 mm joints; density 2.5 t/m³. `precast_config.get` and `.set` address values by dotted path; `.set` keeps a value's type, refuses an unknown path, and checks every rule (positive lengths, minimum ≤ maximum, gaps 0–100 mm, weights and density above 0, the CAM filename's placeholders, an existing data folder), refusing with `precast_config.invalid` and the path and rule; every change raises the version. `.apply` replaces the whole document as one step (the dialog's OK). `.export` writes `{schema: 1, kind: "reviera.precast_configuration", configuration}`; `.import` checks it and the rules, replaces the document and lists the slab components and division profiles it names that the project lacks. `.affected` gives the version and the assemblies made with an older one. Concrete › Precast Settings › **Configuration**: a tree (General; Solid Wall, Double Wall, Solid Slab, Hollow-core Slab, Lattice-girder Slab each with Segmentation, Reinforcement, Connections, Shop Drawing; Annotations; Dimensioning; CAM Export) checked as you type: a field that breaks a rule turns red, its page is marked "(!)", the rule shows under the tree and OK is disabled. A check box re-splits the assemblies an older version made after OK. Export… and Import… buttons. Not yet: the reinforcement, connections, shop-drawing, annotation and dimensioning nodes' contents (their steps are not built), families checked as loaded, the template's own configuration.

### 4.5.2 Segmentation (split)
**ID:** STR-PRE-002 · **Priority:** P2 · **Ref:** research/03 §6.2

**Workflow.**
1. Choose *Split*, optionally with *Multiple*.
2. Select walls, floors or foundation slabs, then Finish.
3. For floors, choose the slab kind: **Hollow-core**, **Solid** or **Lattice-girder**.

**Behaviour & rules.**
- **What Split does:** creates parts (chapter 3 parts engine), divides them by the rules, places mounting parts and reinforcement (when automatic updates are on), and creates one **assembly per piece**.
- **Wall rules:** minimum and maximum length, minimum and maximum height, **maximum weight**, horizontal and vertical joint gap, minimum distance to openings, and profile overlap height.
- **Slab rules:** minimum and maximum width, maximum weight and joint gap. Hollow-core slabs add the hollow-core family, a **division profile**, minimum width, segmentation gap and strand diameter.
- **Re-splitting:** after the source boundary changes, Split is re-run on the **assembly**. If it is run on the source element instead, Reviera detects the existing split and offers to redirect.
- **Automatic updates** (a toggle) controls whether mounting parts and reinforcement are re-created when pieces change.
- **Double walls:** a wall type with three layers (concrete, thermal or air, concrete) is split and reinforced as one double-wall piece.
- **Independent lattice girders** can be sketched on lattice-girder slab assemblies.

**Data (IFC mapping).**
- **Initial version (owner decision, 2026-10-12; open question Q13).** The IFC relationship between the source wall or slab and its pieces is **not written**. IFC allows a piece only one decomposition parent, and that parent is its piece assembly (below). The source-to-piece link is kept in RXD element data only. Which IFC relationship, if any, carries it is decided later on expert advice.
- Each piece is an `IfcWall` or `IfcSlab` (or an `IfcBuildingElementPart` with `PRECASTPANEL`) inside an `IfcElementAssembly` (`USERDEFINED` "PRECAST_ASSEMBLY") together with its reinforcement and mounting parts.
- `Pset_PrecastConcreteElementGeneral` and `Pset_PrecastConcreteElementFabrication` (TypeDesignator, PieceMark, ProductionLotId, SerialNumber).
- **RXD element data** (`structural`) holds the source element GlobalId, slab kind and rule snapshot hash.

**Commands.**
- `precast.split(element_ids[], slab_kind?) -> assembly_ids[]`
- `precast.resplit(assembly_ids[])`
- `precast.set_auto_update(bool)`
- `precast.info(assembly_ids[]?) -> assemblies[]`

**Acceptance criteria.**
- [x] A 30 m × 3 m wall with maximum length 8 m and maximum weight 12 t is split into the fewest pieces that satisfy both limits, with the configured gaps.
- [x] No joint lies closer to an opening than the minimum distance.
- [x] Each piece exports as an `IfcElementAssembly` that contains the concrete element and its reinforcement.

*Built (2026-10-19):* `precast.split` on straight walls (solid or double) and floors (solid, hollow-core or lattice-girder). A wall gets rows of equal height when taller than the maximum height, then joints along it: the fewest pieces with every piece within the minimum and maximum length and the maximum weight (its concrete volume, less openings, × density; the heaviest row counts), and no joint within the minimum distance of an opening; the pieces are made even where that keeps every rule, otherwise each joint goes as far along as the rules allow (stepping back off an opening). A 30 m × 3 m × 250 mm wall at 8 m and 12 t gives five 6 m pieces (four would weigh 14 t). A floor is cut into strips side by side along its longest outline edge: hollow-core in standard (maximum) widths with the rest last (the last two shared if the rest is under the minimum), others like walls. Its parts are divided (made first if it has none: one per layer) with the configured gaps, and each piece's parts go in an `IfcElementAssembly` (USERDEFINED, ObjectType `PRECAST_ASSEMBLY`) with a piece mark (W1-1, W1-2, … or S1-…; a row letter when there are rows) and `Pset_PrecastConcreteElementFabrication` PieceMark and TypeDesignator on it and its parts. The assembly's recipe (`recipe.precast_assembly`) keeps the source, kind, parts, mark, place, configuration version, a hash of the kind's rules, and the divisions it made. In IFC the parts are aggregated by their assembly, not by the source (the source-to-piece link stays in RXD, per the owner decision above), and the assembly is contained in the source's storey. Splitting an element already split is refused naming its assemblies (the window offers to re-split); `precast.resplit` removes the split's pieces and assemblies and splits again with the current rules; `precast.set_auto_update` sets the configuration's flag (nothing is regenerated yet: STR-PRE-003, 005); `precast.info` gives each assembly's mark, kind, source, parts, volume, weight, version and place. Deleting the source deletes its assemblies. Concrete › Precast Detailing › **Split** (the wall or slab kind) and **Re-split**; the Model Tree shows the assemblies under the element split and their parts under them. Since STR-PRE-003, the assembly also holds the reinforcement generated for its piece. Pieces are put in rows by the row cut, not by height (an opening moves a piece's middle). Not yet: curved walls, double walls as one three-layer piece, profile overlap between rows, joints kept off openings in floors, hollow-core division profiles, independent lattice girders, the *Multiple* option.

### 4.5.3 Automatic precast reinforcement
**ID:** STR-PRE-003 · **Priority:** P2 · **Ref:** research/03 §6.3 · screenshots/structure_mep/precast_wall_auto_reinforcement.png

**Workflow.** Choose *Auto Reinforce*. Select an assembly, or several assemblies of the same kind. Choose the **area reinforcement type** and, for walls, the **edge reinforcement type**. Click OK.

**Behaviour & rules.**
- Reinforcement types are defined per wall or slab thickness. Each covers:
  - area bars or mesh
  - edge bars around openings and edges (for example U-bars)
  - lattice girders for double walls and girder slabs
- Editing a reinforcement type changes every default that refers to it. Reviera offers to re-run on the affected assemblies.
- The dialog offers only the reinforcement types whose thickness range contains the piece thickness. Selecting assemblies of different kinds (for example a wall and a slab) is refused.
- **Re-running** on an assembly that is already reinforced replaces only the reinforcement that the previous run generated (marked as generated, with the run's rule snapshot). Bars the user added by hand are kept; generated bars the user edited are kept and reported, so manual work is never lost silently.
- With automatic updates on (STR-PRE-002), reinforcement is regenerated whenever a piece's geometry changes; with them off, the assembly is flagged as out of date.
- Area reinforcement respects the host cover (STR-RBR-002) and is cut around openings with the configured clearance; edge bars wrap openings and free edges with the configured lap; lattice girders are laid parallel to the span at the configured spacing and edge distance.
- Generated reinforcement gets partition = the assembly's piece mark, so numbering (STR-RBR-016) is per piece.
- The report lists, per assembly, the bars, sheets and girders created, kept or skipped, and why.

**Data (IFC mapping).** Generated rebar and mesh as in §4.2, aggregated into the piece assembly. Lattice girders are `IfcReinforcingElement` subtypes: `IfcReinforcingBar` chords and diagonals grouped in an `IfcElementAssembly` `USERDEFINED` "LATTICE_GIRDER". The generated flag, the reinforcement type used and the rule snapshot hash are RXD element data (`rebar`) on each generated element.

**Commands.** `precast.reinforce(assembly_ids[], area_type_id, edge_type_id?) -> report`, `precast.reinforcement_types(assembly_ids[]) -> {thickness, area_types[], edge_types[]}`

**Acceptance criteria.**
- [x] Reinforcing a wall piece with a 1.2 × 2.1 m door opening places U-bars around the opening edges and mesh cut around it.
- [x] Re-running on that piece after the user added one extra bar keeps the extra bar and replaces only generated reinforcement.
- [x] A 200 mm wall piece is offered only reinforcement types whose thickness range contains 200 mm.
- [x] Generated bars carry the piece mark as their partition.

*Built (2026-10-19):* reinforcement types are in the configuration per kind (`<kind>.reinforcement.area_types` and, for walls, `edge_types`): id, name, thickness range, bar type, spacing and, for edge types, the leg; thickness ranges may not overlap within a list (refused naming both types). Provisional starting types (expert review E-12): walls `A10-150` (120–250 mm, Ø10 @ 150 each face), `A12-150` (250–400 mm, Ø12 @ 150) and `U10-200` (120–400 mm, Ø10 U-bars @ 200, 500 mm legs); solid and lattice-girder slabs `S10-150` (100–350 mm, Ø10 @ 150 both ways, top and bottom); hollow-core none. `precast.reinforcement_types` gives the types whose range holds every selected piece; `precast.reinforce(assembly_ids, area_type_id, edge_type_id?)` refuses pieces of different kinds (`precast.mixed`) and a type whose range does not hold a piece (`precast.thickness`, naming the range and the piece). Wall pieces get vertical bars (outside) and horizontal bars (inside them) at both faces as layer sets of the element split, bounded by the piece (its parts' extent along and up the wall) less the edge cover; layer bars are now cut round a wall's openings and keep the edge cover beside an opening's sides too (a bar is kept only where lines a cover either side of it are inside the concrete). Edge types add U-bar sets (sketched, shape 21) round each free edge of the piece (less where an opening meets it) and each side, head and sill of an opening in it: the web across the thickness at the edge cover, both legs the type's leg into the piece, spaced along the edge (expert review E-13). Slab pieces get bars both ways at the top and the bottom, bounded by the piece's strip. Every generated set's partition is the piece mark, and it carries `rxd:precast_generated` (assembly, type, a hash of its recipe as made); the assembly lists them (`reinforcement`) and holds them in IFC instead of the host. Running again removes generated sets as made and keeps, and reports, those edited since and sets added by hand in the piece's partition; re-splitting removes them with their pieces; deleting the assembly deletes them. The report gives per assembly the sets made, replaced and kept (with why) and what was skipped. Concrete › Precast Detailing › **Auto Reinforce** (the types the pieces allow; a report after); the configuration's Reinforcement pages edit the types, one per line. Not yet: lattice girders (`LATTICE_GIRDER` assemblies) and double walls' girders, meshes (fabric) as area reinforcement, an opening clearance other than the cover, laps between area bars and U-bars checked, regeneration on piece changes with automatic updates on (the assembly is not yet flagged out of date), editing a type offering to re-run.

### 4.5.4 Custom fabric sheets
**ID:** STR-PRE-004 · **Priority:** P2 · **Ref:** research/03 §3.5, §6.3

**Purpose.** Generate a fabric sheet shaped to each precast piece, instead of cutting standard sheets, so that the plant can produce one welded mesh per piece.

**Workflow.** Select one or more precast assemblies and choose *Concrete › Precast Detailing › Custom Fabric Sheets*, optionally choosing a rule set other than the default. Rules are edited in *Precast Settings › Custom Fabric Sheet Rules* (part of the precast configuration, STR-PRE-001).

**Behaviour & rules.**
- Rule-generated custom sheets are cut around openings. The rules are wire spacing, edge distances, opening clearances and maximum sheet size, set in *Custom Fabric Sheet Rules*. The output is `IfcReinforcingMesh` with per-sheet wire geometry.
- **Rule set contents:** wire diameter and spacing per direction, edge distance per edge kind (outer edge, joint edge), clearance around openings, minimum wire length (shorter wires are dropped), maximum sheet length and width (default 6.0 × 2.5 m), and which layer (near or far face) to fill.
- A piece larger than the maximum sheet size gets several sheets, split along a line perpendicular to the main wires, with the configured lap.
- Wires stop at the clearance line around each opening; wires that would be shorter than the minimum length are omitted, and the omitted count is reported.
- Sheets are regenerated when the piece changes if automatic updates are on (STR-PRE-002); otherwise the piece is flagged as out of date.
- Each sheet is numbered like any fabric sheet (STR-RBR-016); two pieces with identical sheets share a number.

**Data (IFC mapping).** One `IfcReinforcingMesh` per sheet, aggregated into the piece assembly, with MeshLength, MeshWidth, the longitudinal and transverse bar diameters and spacings, and one swept body per wire. The rule set id and the generated flag are RXD element data (`rebar`); rule sets are part of the precast configuration in RXD document `fabrication`.

**Commands.** `precast.generate_custom_fabric(assembly_ids[], rule_id?)`

**Acceptance criteria.**
- [x] A slab piece with two openings receives one custom sheet whose wires stop at the configured clearance from each opening.
- [x] A 9 m × 2.4 m wall piece with a 6 m maximum sheet length receives two sheets lapped by the configured lap length.
- [x] Two identical pieces get sheets with the same rebar number.

*Built (2026-10-19):* rules are the configuration's `fabric_rules` (id, name, main and cross wire types, their spacings, edge distance at outer edges and at joints, opening clearance, shortest wire, largest sheet length and width, lap, layer `outer`/`inner`/`both`), checked like the rest (values above 0, lap shorter than the largest sheet, unique ids). The provisional starting rule `C8-150` (expert review E-14): Ø8 wires @ 150 both ways, 50 mm from edges, joints and openings, 300 mm shortest wire, 6.0 × 2.5 m largest sheet, 300 mm lap, both faces. `precast.generate_custom_fabric(assembly_ids, rule_id?)` gives each piece (hollow-core refused: prestressed) sheets at the rule's face(s): main wires along the piece's longer side; one sheet when the piece fits, else equal sheets split square to the main wires (and across them when the piece is wider than the largest sheet), lapped by the lap. A sheet (`IfcReinforcingMesh`, `recipe.custom_fabric_sheet`) keeps the rule as used, its corner, direction and size in its host's plane, and the piece's region, and its wires are worked out from the host each time: the piece less its openings grown by the clearance; a wire end stops at the clearance line at an opening, at the joint distance where the host goes on past the piece, at the outer distance at the host's own edge, and not at all at a side where another sheet laps on; the outermost wires sit at the edge distance from piece edges. Wires shorter than the shortest are left out and counted in the report. Sheets are numbered as fabric by their wires and lengths, so identical pieces' sheets share a number; their partition is the piece mark; they carry `rxd:precast_generated` and the assembly holds them (in IFC too, with MeshLength, MeshWidth, wire diameters and spacings, a mesh type, a body per wire and the number as Tag). Running again replaces sheets as made and keeps edited ones. Concrete › Precast Detailing › **Custom Fabric** (choose a rule; a report after) and the configuration's **Custom Fabric Sheet Rules** page (one rule per line). Not yet: regeneration when a piece changes with automatic updates on, an opening clearance per wire end kind, sheets on non-rectangular piece outlines beyond the piece's bounding rectangle (the host outline still clips them), bent wires, swept-disk bodies.

### 4.5.5 Mounting parts
**ID:** STR-PRE-005 · **Priority:** P2 · **Ref:** research/03 §6.1–6.2

**Purpose.** Place the embedded parts that a precast piece needs for lifting, fixing and connecting, from rules rather than by hand.

**Workflow.** Select precast assemblies and choose *Concrete › Precast Detailing › Mounting Parts*. Parts are also placed automatically by *Split* when automatic updates are on (STR-PRE-002). Individual parts can afterwards be moved, deleted or added by hand like any family occurrence.

**Behaviour & rules.**
- Rule-driven placement of lifting anchors, loops, bushings, connectors and lattice girders, per configuration.
- Placement rules include count by weight, edge distances and centre-of-gravity symmetry.
  - **Weight bands** decide the count and family (for example up to 10 t: 2 anchors; up to 16 t: 4 anchors). A piece heavier than the last band is not given parts and is reported.
  - Weight is computed from the piece volume (openings removed) and the concrete density of the material (default 2 500 kg/m³).
  - Lifting anchors go on the top edge for walls and the top face for slabs, symmetric about the centre of gravity, at least the configured edge distance from ends and openings. If no symmetric position satisfies the distances, the closest valid positions are used and a warning is issued.
- Mounting-part families can carry dimensioning references for shop drawings.
- Re-running replaces only parts the rules generated; parts added or moved by hand are kept and reported.
- Mounting parts host on the piece and move with it; deleting the piece deletes them (STR-GEN-002).

**Data (IFC mapping).** `IfcMechanicalFastener` (`USERDEFINED` "LIFTING_ANCHOR", "BUSHING", …) or `IfcDiscreteAccessory` (`USERDEFINED` "CONNECTOR", or `ANCHORPLATE`), aggregated into the piece assembly. The generated flag and the rule that placed each part are RXD element data (`structural`). The piece weight is written as NetWeight in `Qto_WallBaseQuantities` or `Qto_SlabBaseQuantities` of the piece.

**Commands.** `precast.place_mounting_parts(assembly_ids[]) -> report`, `mounting_part.place(assembly_id, point) -> part_id`

**Acceptance criteria.**
- [x] A 9 t wall piece configured for "2 anchors up to 10 t" receives 2 lifting anchors placed symmetrically about the centre of gravity.
- [x] A 20 t piece with bands only up to 16 t receives no anchors and is listed in the report.
- [x] Re-running after the user moved one anchor keeps the moved anchor and reports it.

*Built (2026-10-19):* each kind's `connections` node holds the mounting rules: the part's name, weight bands (`max_weight` in tonnes and `count`, ascending, checked to be contiguous), the distance from the piece's ends (and a slab's edges) and from openings, and the anchor's diameter and depth; provisional starting rules (expert review E-15): 2 anchors up to 10 t, 4 up to 16 t, 300 mm from ends and openings, Ø30 × 200 mm. `precast.place_mounting_parts` weighs each piece by its parts' bodies (openings removed) × density and finds its centre of gravity from their volume; the first band holding the weight gives the count, and a heavier piece gets none and a warning in the report. Wall anchors go on the piece's top edge on the location line, slab anchors on its top face (one row along the long side for two, two rows for more), spread symmetrically about the centre of gravity and drawn in until every one keeps the distances (openings that reach within the anchor's depth and the opening distance of the top edge count for walls); when none does, each goes to the nearest valid place and the report warns. An anchor is an `IfcMechanicalFastener` (USERDEFINED `LIFTING_ANCHOR`, `recipe.mounting_part`: assembly, head point, size) with a rod body; it moves, rotates and mirrors with element.move etc. and goes with its assembly; the assembly lists its parts (`mounting`) and holds them in IFC, and gets the piece weight as `Qto_WallBaseQuantities` / `Qto_SlabBaseQuantities` NetWeight (kg). Running again replaces parts as placed and keeps, and reports, those moved since and those placed by hand (`mounting_part.place`). Concrete › Precast Detailing › **Mounting Parts** (a report after) and the configuration's Connections pages (bands one per line). Not yet: loops, bushings, connectors and lattice girders as parts, Component Library families with dimension references, placement by Split with automatic updates, the NetWeight on the pieces themselves, anchors turned to a sloping or curved top.

### 4.5.6 Shop drawings
**ID:** STR-PRE-006 · **Priority:** P2 · **Ref:** research/03 §6.4 · screenshots/structure_mep/precast_shop_drawing.png

**Workflow.** Select assemblies and choose *Shop Drawings*. Reviera creates one sheet per assembly, or per group of identical assemblies, from the shop-drawing template configured for that element kind.

**Behaviour & rules.**
- **Templates** are Reviera assembly-sheet templates (chapter 5 sheets and assembly views). They define:
  - viewports: front, sections, 3D and reinforcement
  - a centre-of-gravity symbol
  - dimension type and dimension line distances
  - descriptions
  - schedules: bill of materials for concrete, rebar, mesh and mounting parts
  - per-category tags (*Annotations*) and per-category dimension rules (*Dimensioning*)
- Similar pieces share dimension layouts.
- Only title blocks that contain the required template viewports are accepted. Reviera ships open template title blocks.
- Shop-drawing generation is a command, so Lua scripts and the MCP server can drive and customise it. This replaces the reference product's separate precast API.

**Commands.** `precast.shop_drawings(assembly_ids[], template_id?, group_identical?: bool) -> sheet_ids[]`

**Acceptance criteria.**
- [x] Generating shop drawings for 10 pieces, of which 4 are identical, with grouping on produces 7 sheets. Each has dimensioned views, a centre-of-gravity symbol and a BOM schedule.

*Built (2026-10-20):* `precast.shop_drawings(assembly_ids, template_id?, group_identical = true)` makes an A3 sheet (number `PS-<mark>`) per piece, or per group of identical pieces (same kind, outline, openings, reinforcement numbers and sizes, fabric sheets and anchor places, to the millimetre in the piece's frame; reinforcement numbered per piece-mark partition, so identical pieces carry the same numbers). Each sheet carries a **shop drawing item** (`shopDrawings` in the sheet data: the assemblies and the top-left corner) that the sheet draws from the model whenever it is shown or printed, so it follows the pieces; it goes when none of its pieces is left. It draws, in the piece's frame (along and up a wall; along and across a slab) at the largest of 1:5, 10, 20, 25, 50, 100 that fits 240 × 130 mm: the front view (outline, openings crossed with their sizes, lifting anchors), chain dimensions of the ends and openings and the overall length below, the anchors above and the height and openings at the left; the centre-of-gravity symbol with its distances from the piece's start and bottom; Section A-A through the thickness with its dimension; a bill of materials (concrete thickness, volume and weight; rebar by number with shape, bar, quantity, length and mass; fabric sheets by number with wires and size; mounting parts and count); and the marks the sheet stands for. Making them again replaces sheets made for the same pieces. Only the built-in template (`default`, A3) exists. Concrete › Precast Detailing › **Shop Drawings** (grouping on or off; the first sheet opens). Not yet: templates and title blocks with required viewports, model views on the sheet (sections have no crop regions or scale setting yet, 3D views cannot be placed, annotation is plan-only), so the views and the bill of materials are drawn on the sheet rather than placed as viewports and a schedule element; per-category tags and dimension rules, reinforcement views, similar pieces sharing dimension layouts.

### 4.5.7 CAM export
**ID:** STR-PRE-007 · **Priority:** P2 (framework) / P3 (specific proprietary formats) · **Ref:** research/03 §6.4

**Purpose.** Hand precast pieces to plant production systems as machine-readable files.

**Workflow.** Select precast assemblies (or none, for all assemblies in the project) and choose *Concrete › Precast Detailing › CAM Export*. Choose the writer and the output folder; the filename rule comes from the configuration (STR-PRE-001) and can be overridden for this run. The export runs in the background and ends with a summary.

**Behaviour & rules.**
- A **CAM export framework** with per-format writer plugins.
  - A writer is a provider (ANA-PLUG-001 style manifest with name, version, SPDX licence and file extension), implemented in Lua or as an external process. It receives the neutral piece model below and returns files.
  - `cam_writer.list` lists installed writers with their format and version.
- Each writer node has an output **filename rule** built from variables: name with length, minimum length, padding and alignment; date; time; production number.
  - Syntax: `{Var:Length:MinLength:Pad:Align}`, where any trailing field may be omitted; variables are `Name`, `ProdNo`, `Date` (YYYYMMDD), `Time` (HHMMSS) and `Mark`. Unknown variables and malformed fields are rejected before export with the position of the error.
  - Names that would collide in the folder get a numeric suffix, and the summary lists them.
- **[Suggestion]** writers: Unitechnik (versions 5.2/6.0/7.0) and PXML, as plugins. Implementations must be based on openly available format documentation. If such documentation is not available under acceptable terms, the format stays P3.
- Reviera always provides a neutral **JSON/CSV piece export** (geometry outline, openings, embeds, reinforcement and piece marks) for custom CAM pipelines.
  - Coordinates are in millimetres in the piece's local production system (origin at the lower-left corner of the piece's front face, X along the length).
- Pieces without a piece mark, or whose reinforcement or mounting parts are out of date (STR-PRE-003, STR-PRE-005), are exported only after a confirmation that lists them; scripted calls report them as warnings.
- The export does not change the model.

**Data (IFC mapping).** Reads the precast assemblies, pieces, reinforcement and mounting parts of STR-PRE-002 to 005 and `Pset_PrecastConcreteElementFabrication` (PieceMark, ProductionLotId, SerialNumber). Writer settings and filename rules are stored in the precast configuration (RXD document `fabrication`). Nothing is written back.

**Commands.**
- `precast.cam_export(assembly_ids[], writer_id, folder, filename_rule?) -> {files[], renamed[], warnings[]}`
- `cam_writer.list() -> writers[]`

**Acceptance criteria.**
- [x] The rule `{Name:12:4:0:left}_{ProdNo}` names files with zero-padded, left-aligned piece names and the production number.
- [x] The rule `{Nme}_{ProdNo}` is rejected before any file is written, with the position of the unknown variable.
- [x] The neutral JSON export of a wall piece with one opening lists the outline, the opening, every bar with its shape and the lifting anchors, with coordinates in the piece's local system.
- [x] Exporting leaves the undo stack unchanged.

*Built (2026-10-20):* the neutral piece model, its JSON and CSV writers and the filename rules are the MIT crate `reviera-precast-cam` (`clients/precast-cam`, schema 1): mark, name, production number, kind, length, height, thickness, volume and weight; the outline and openings; embeds (kind, name, head, direction, diameter, length); bar sets (number, shape code, bar, diameter, each bar's centreline); fabric sheets (number, wires); millimetres with the origin at the lower-left of the piece's front face (a wall's exterior, a slab's underside), X along, Y up or across, Z in. Filename rules parse `{Var:Length:MinLength:Pad:Align}` (variables Name, ProdNo, Date, Time, Mark; length truncates, the minimum pads with the pad character on the side away from the alignment) and reject an unknown variable, a malformed field, an unclosed brace or a character no file system takes with its character position (`cam.filename_rule`, `position` in the details); the configuration's `cam.filename` (`{Mark}` by default) is checked the same way. `cam_writer.list` gives the built-in `neutral_json` and `neutral_csv` writers and external writers from manifests in the configuration's data folder (`cam_writers/*.json`: id, name, version, SPDX licence, extension, command); an external writer is run with the piece's neutral JSON on its input and its output saved as the file. `precast.cam_export(assembly_ids (all when empty), writer_id, folder, filename_rule?)` builds every piece and every name before writing anything, numbers colliding names (`_2` …, reported), writes one file per piece and reports pieces without reinforcement or mounting parts as warnings; it is a read command, so the model and the undo stack are untouched. Production numbers run in export order (pieces sorted by mark when all are exported). Concrete › Precast Detailing › **CAM Export** (writer, folder, filename rule for this run; a summary after). Not yet: Lua writers, Unitechnik and PXML plugins (P3; openly documented formats only), running in the background, a confirmation listing out-of-date pieces (there is no out-of-date flag yet), ProductionLotId and SerialNumber from `Pset_PrecastConcreteElementFabrication`.
