### 4.12.10 Solar analysis
**ID:** ANA-SOLAR-001 · **Priority:** P2 · **Ref:** research/03 §13.4 ("Solar")

**Behaviour & rules.**
- *Daylight & Solar › Solar*:
  - **study type**: cumulative insolation over a date range, or PV potential
  - **settings**: PV panel efficiency, coverage and payback inputs
  - **surfaces**: all roof exterior surfaces, all mass faces, or a selection
  - *Update*

  Results are managed per view.
- **[Suggestion] Providers:** a Radiance-based irradiance provider, or a built-in sky-patch cumulative method. An open PV-modelling library such as pvlib (BSD-3) could be used for PV yield.
- **Sun studies** (still, single-day, multi-day and lighting) and the **sun path** display are view features in chapter 5. The solar analysis uses the same sun model.
- **Inputs.** Site location and weather file (ANA-EM-001); the date range (default a full year) and hours (default sunrise to sunset); a grid spacing on each analysed face (default 1 m, range 0.1–10 m); and shading context, which is every model element and visible linked element in the 3D view the study is run from, unless a category is excluded.
- **Cumulative insolation.** Results are kWh/m² per grid point over the period, plus per-face totals (kWh) and averages. The built-in provider splits the sky into patches, takes direct and diffuse irradiance from the weather file, and tests visibility from each grid point to each patch and to the sun positions by ray casting against the shading context.
- **PV potential.** Per face: usable area (face area × coverage, default 80%), annual energy = insolation × usable area × panel efficiency (default 18%) × system derate (default 0.86), installed cost (cost per kW peak) and simple payback (cost ÷ (annual energy × energy price)). All defaults are editable in the settings and stored with the study.
- **Studies are per view.** Each 3D view keeps a list of studies; *Update* re-runs the active one. Results draw with an analysis display style (ANA-ADS-001), with a legend. Results become stale when the model, the site or the weather file changes.
- A face with no sun hours in the period (for example a north face in winter at high latitude) reports 0, not an error. Faces of elements in a link are analysed only if the link is visible.
- **Export:** per-face results to CSV, and the grid values to the result package.

**Data (IFC mapping).** The result package (grid points, values, per-face totals, inputs) is stored as a file referenced by `IfcDocumentReference` and indexed in **RXD document** `analysis`. Per-face totals are also schedulable result parameters (ANA-GEN-002) on the analysed elements.

**Commands.**
- `solar.run(study_type, date_range, surfaces: "roofs"|"masses"|face_refs[], pv_settings?) -> job_id`
- `solar.export(job_id, path)` (CSV of per-face results)

**Acceptance criteria.**
- [x] Cumulative insolation on a south-facing roof face is higher than on a north-facing face of the same pitch for a northern-hemisphere site.
- [x] A roof face fully shaded by a taller neighbouring mass has at least 50% lower insolation than the same face with the mass hidden.
- [x] For a 100 m² face with 1 200 kWh/m² per year, 80% coverage, 18% efficiency and derate 0.86, PV potential reports 14 861 kWh per year (within 0.5%).
- [x] Moving the shading mass marks the study stale until *Update* completes.

*Built (2026-10-25, with ANA-ENV-002):* Analyze › **Daylight & Solar** › *Solar Study* (study type, period, surfaces: every roof, every mass, or the selection; grid spacing; PV coverage, efficiency, derate, cost per kWp and energy price) and *Solar Results* (per face: element, area, mean kWh/m², total kWh, PV kWh a year and payback; the stale notice; *Show on Model*, *Hide*, *Export…*). `solar.run` distils the analysed faces (roof faces' top surfaces, mass faces not facing down; keyed `<GlobalId>/<face>`), the shading context (every model element's body, except excluded categories), the site (latitude, longitude, time zone, true north) and the weather file's hourly direct normal and diffuse horizontal irradiance (EPW fields 15 and 16) into `solar.input` and submits an `analysis.solar` job to the built-in runner; `solar.collect` records it (`solar.record`, the last ten studies); `solar.results`, `solar.status` (stale when the faces, shading, site, period or weather changed: a hash of the inputs) and `solar.export` (CSV). Method (Reviera's, E-36): hourly sun positions at the half hour; direct = DNI × cos(incidence) where a ray to the sun misses the context; diffuse = DHI × the visible share of an isotropic sky of 8 altitude rings of near-square patches; ray casting by Möller–Trumbore; grid squares of the spacing clipped to each face (its centroid when none fit); PV per the formula above, scaled to a year when the period is shorter, cost = usable area × efficiency × cost per kWp. *Show on Model* draws each grid point's square on its face in 3D views, blue (least) to red (most), the range in the status bar. Not yet: per-view study lists and analysis display styles with a placed legend (ANA-ADS-001), sun studies and the sun path, linked models, the Perez sky and pvlib/SSC models, schedulable per-face result parameters, the result package as an IFC document.

### 4.12.11 Analysis display styles (visualisation framework)
**ID:** ANA-ADS-001 · **Priority:** P2 · **Ref:** research/03 §13.4 ("Analysis Display Styles"), §4.6 · web: Settings Tab for Analysis Display Styles

**UI: the Analysis Display Styles dialog** (*Manage › Additional Settings › Analysis Display Styles*, `analysis_style.manage`). Left: the list of styles grouped by display kind, with *New*, *Duplicate*, *Rename* and *Delete*. Right: three tabs and a live preview swatch.
- **Settings** (depends on the kind):
  - *Colored surface*: show grid lines, grid line weight (1–16) and colour
  - *Contour*: contour line count or interval, line weight, whether bands between lines are filled
  - *Markers with text*: marker shape (circle, square, triangle), marker size in sheet units (0.5–20 mm), labels (none, all, or only the points the provider marks as predefined), text type, rounding increment
  - *Diagram*: base line, scale (value per sheet mm), outline or filled, labels
  - *Vector*: arrow head, arrow line weight, scale, and whether arrow length follows magnitude
- **Color**: *gradient* (2 or 3 colour stops) or *ranges* (bands with a colour each); *auto* range from the data, or fixed minimum and maximum; values outside the range use the end colours or a separate out-of-range colour. Colours come from theme-aware palettes, including colour-blind-safe sequential and diverging palettes; users may also enter colours.
- **Legend**: show or hide, position (corner of the view or free), title, number of steps (2–20), units and decimal places, text type, and whether the provider description is shown.

**Behaviour & rules.**
- One shared visualisation framework is used by structural results, lighting, solar, airflow and loads overlays, and by Lua add-ins.
- Add-ins publish results through the `analysis_result.publish` command.
- A style has one display kind; result sets of a different kind cannot use it, and the view's style picker offers only compatible styles.
- Each view has a default analysis display style (a view property); a published result uses the style passed to it, or the view default.
- Editing a style redraws every view that uses it. Deleting a style in use asks for a replacement style of the same kind.
- Results are view-specific graphics: they are not model elements, are not exported to IFC, and print and export to PDF and images like other view graphics. *Reveal Obstacles* (ANA-ROUTE-002) and results cannot be shown in the same view.
- Hovering a result point shows its value and units in a tooltip.

**Data (IFC mapping).** Styles are kept as **RXD document** `analysis`. Per-view assignments are part of the view's RXD data (chapter 5). Published values are kept in the result package of their job, not in the view.

**Commands.**
- `analysis_style.manage()` (opens the dialog)
- `analysis_style.create(name, settings) -> id`
- `analysis_result.publish(view_id, element_or_face_refs[], values[], style_id) -> id`
- `analysis_result.clear(view_id, id?)`

**Acceptance criteria.**
- [ ] A Lua script can publish scalar values on a floor's top face and see them in a gradient with a legend.
- [ ] Changing a gradient style to five fixed bands updates every view that uses it without re-running the analysis.
- [ ] Deleting a style used by two views asks for a replacement of the same kind, and both views then draw with it.
- [ ] A *Markers with text* style with rounding 0.5 shows the value 3.26 as 3.5.

### 4.12.12 Path of travel
**ID:** ANA-ROUTE-001 · **Priority:** P2 · **Ref:** research/03 §13.5 · screenshots/structure_mep/path_of_travel_with_schedule.png

**Workflow.** Choose *Route Analysis › Path of Travel*, then click a start and an end point in a **plan view**.

**Behaviour & rules.**
- Reviera computes the **shortest path that avoids obstacles** inside an **analysis zone**: a band between a bottom and a top offset from the level.
- Obstacles are the elements of non-ignored categories whose geometry intersects the zone. Doors are passable.
- **Waypoints** can be added and removed. Paths can be updated after the model changes, individually or all at once.
- Paths are on **one level only**. Stairs and ramps are not followed in the first release (§4.17 Q9).
- Path lines are view-specific elements that can be tagged and scheduled, with length and time (length ÷ walking speed).
- **Implementation:** build a 2D obstacle map from plan-cut geometry, then search a visibility graph or a navigation mesh. An open navigation-mesh library under the zlib licence is a **[Suggestion]**.

**Data (IFC mapping).** View-specific annotation (chapter 5) with RXD element data (`analysis`): start, end, waypoints, length and time. When exported, paths can optionally be `IfcAnnotation` curves.

**Commands.**
- `path_of_travel.create(view_id, start, end, waypoints?[]) -> id`
- `path_of_travel.update(ids[] | "all_in_view")`
- `path_of_travel.add_waypoint(id, point, index?)`

**Acceptance criteria.**
- [x] In a plan with a wall between start and end and one door, the path passes through the door, and its length is within 1% of the true shortest path that keeps the configured clearance.
- [x] A Path of Travel schedule lists length and time, and time = length ÷ walk speed. *(Listed in Analyze › Route Analysis › Paths of Travel and `path_of_travel.list`; a schedule category for annotation is not built.)*

*Built (2026-10-25):* Analyze › **Route Analysis** › *Path of Travel* (click a start, then an end, in a plan; again for more, Esc ends), *Update Paths* (the plan's paths), *Route Settings* and *Paths of Travel* (length and time). Obstacles in the analysis zone (zone bottom to top above the level): walls as their straight bodies with a gap where a door's opening reaches the zone's bottom (windows never), and placed components whose body reaches into the zone, by the hull of their vertices in plan; ignored categories are left out. Each obstacle is grown by the clearance, its corners rounded by chords outside the true arc so the route is always feasible (and at most 1 % longer than the exact one). The route is the shortest path through a visibility graph of the grown outlines' corners (Dijkstra), from the start through the waypoints in order to the end; a point inside an obstacle or its clearance, or no way through, is refused (`path_of_travel.no_route`). Paths are view annotations (`anno.path_of_travel`: view, start, end, waypoints, route, length, time = length ÷ walking speed), drawn in green with an arrowhead and their length and time, picked by clicking near them, deleted like any element. Commands: `path_of_travel.create`, `.update(ids | view)`, `.add_waypoint(id, point, index?, remove?)`, `.list`, `route_settings.set/get`. Defaults (E-35): zone 0.2–2.0 m, 1.3 m/s, 0.3 m clearance. Not yet: dragging waypoints in the view, curved walls (taken as their chord), columns and other non-component elements as obstacles, Reveal Obstacles, multiple paths, one-way indicators, people content, spatial grids, the Longest Exit Distance script, IfcAnnotation export, a Path of Travel schedule category.

### 4.12.13 Route analysis settings, obstacles and people-flow tools
**ID:** ANA-ROUTE-002 · **Priority:** P2 · **Ref:** research/03 §13.5

**Behaviour & rules.**
- **Settings:**
  - ignored categories; hidden, demolished and underlay elements are ignored by default, and a nested family needs both its own and its parent's category ignored
  - analysis-zone offsets
  - walking speed
  - clearance
- **Reveal Obstacles:** a view mode that colours the elements counted as obstacles. It is unavailable in views that show analysis results.
- **Multiple Paths:** several simultaneous routes, with a minimum separation.
- **One-Way Indicator:** a family that routing respects.
- **People Content:** occupancy families that block paths (specified in ANA-ROUTE-003).
- **Spatial Grid:** a square or hexagonal filled-region grid over a room. It does not update with the room.
- A sample Lua script "Longest Exit Distance" is supplied. It finds the most remote point in each room relative to the exits.

**Data (IFC mapping).** **RXD document** `analysis` (route settings).

**Commands.**
- `route_settings.set(params)`
- `route.reveal_obstacles(view_id, on: bool)`
- `path_of_travel.create_multiple(view_id, starts[], ends[], min_separation) -> ids[]`
- `one_way_indicator.place(view_id, point, direction) -> id`
- `spatial_grid.create(room_id, kind: "square"|"hex", size) -> id`

**Acceptance criteria.**
- [ ] A one-way indicator that points against the direct route forces the path to take an alternative door.
- [ ] Ignoring the Furniture category lets paths pass through furniture.

### 4.12.14 Interference check (cross-reference)
**ID:** ANA-CLASH-001 · **Priority:** P1 · **Ref:** research/03 §13.6

**Behaviour & rules.**
- The interference check is specified in **chapter 6** (Collaboration, linking and coordination), together with BCF export. This chapter adds discipline requirements:
  - It shall support all categories in this chapter, **including detailed steel elements (plates, bolts, welds) and fabrication parts**. The reference product excludes these (§4.17).
  - Insulation and lining coverings are included.
  - Typical discipline pairs shall be offered as presets: framing–framing, structural–architectural columns, braces–walls and openings, roofs–floors, equipment–floors, ducts–beams, pipes–ducts, and host–links.
- A clash provider interface (ANA-PLUG-001 `clash`) allows external engines. **[Suggestion]** OCCT-based distance and interference checks in parallel, with a bounding-volume hierarchy broad phase.
- **Discipline rules this chapter adds to the chapter 6 check:**
  - Connected MEP elements (ports joined by `IfcRelConnectsPorts`) never clash with each other, and a fitting never clashes with the segments it connects.
  - A host and its own hosted or embedded elements are not reported: rebar inside its concrete host, welds and bolts in the parts they join, a duct accessory inside its duct, a hanger touching the part it supports.
  - Analytical elements (analytical members, nodes, analytical segments, energy model surfaces, geometry-less analytical equipment) are never tested.
  - Placeholders (MEP-DUCT-007) are tested using a swept body of their nominal size, so early coordination works before conversion.
  - Insulation and lining are tested as separate coverings, so a report can tell "insulation clash" from "duct clash".
  - An optional **clearance** per category pair (for example 50 mm between ducts and beams for access) reports near misses as soft clashes.
- **Presets** are stored as named check definitions (RXD document `coordination/clash`, chapter 6) and can be edited and shared with *Transfer Project Standards*.

**Commands.** See chapter 6 (`interference.run`, `interference.report`). The presets above are ordinary check definitions for those commands.

*Built (2026-10-16):* the whole-model run is out of process: `compute.submit` with kind `analysis.clash` distils the model's bodies (booleans applied; related and accepted pairs left out) and the built-in runner measures them with the same overlap engine as the live checks (ARC-MOD-030), so results match `overlap.find` exactly; `compute.results` attaches them to elements. Multi-model scopes are carried in the format (each element names its model; `ClashOptions.against_models`) but not yet offered. Presets, clearances, BCF and the chapter 6 commands are not built yet.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- [ ] A bolt that intersects a duct is reported as a clash between Structural Fasteners and Ducts.
- [ ] An elbow connected to two ducts produces no clash with either duct.
- [ ] A rebar set fully inside its wall host produces no clash; the same rebar crossing a pipe does.
- [ ] With a 50 mm clearance on Ducts–Structural Framing, a duct 30 mm below a beam is reported as a soft clash and one 80 mm below is not.

### 4.12.15 People content for route analysis
**ID:** ANA-ROUTE-003 · **Priority:** P2 · **Ref:** research/03 §13.5 ("People Flow Toolkit") · web: Revit 2022 – Enhanced Feature – People flow Toolkit

**Purpose.** Represent standing, seated or queuing people in a plan so that path-of-travel routing treats them as obstacles, for occupancy, queuing and distancing studies.

**Workflow.**
1. In a plan view choose *Analyze › Route Analysis › People Content*.
2. Pick a type in the Type Selector: *Standing person*, *Seated person*, *Wheelchair user*, *Queue line* (a row of people at a set spacing) or *Group* (people on a circle).
3. Click to place; Spacebar rotates by 90° before the click. For a queue line, click a start and an end point; the count follows from the spacing.
4. Update paths (`path_of_travel.update`) to see their effect, or let auto-update re-route paths in the view.

**Behaviour & rules.**
- People content is a model family category, *People*, with a body footprint (default standing 0.6 × 0.5 m, wheelchair 0.8 × 1.3 m), an optional **personal-space radius** (default 0, editable per type, for example 1.0 m for distancing studies) and a height for 3D display.
- Route analysis treats the footprint plus personal-space radius as an obstacle in the analysis zone. Ignoring the *People* category in Route Analysis Settings (ANA-ROUTE-002) lets paths pass through them.
- A path whose start or end lies inside a person's obstacle area is refused with "start point is blocked".
- People are hosted on the level of the plan view, not on floors, and are visible in plan and 3D; they are excluded from material takeoffs, area and space calculations and interference checks by default.
- People can be counted in schedules (by room or space), which gives a quick occupancy check against the occupant load of the room.
- Starter types are authored from scratch and ship under the project's content licence.

**Data (IFC mapping).** Exported, if the user enables the *People* category in the IFC export setup, as `IfcFurnishingElement` with ObjectType "PeopleContent" and `IfcBuildingElementProxy` as fallback; off by default. Personal-space radius and kind are **RXD element data** (`analysis`).

**Commands.** `people_content.place(view_id, type_id, point, rotation?) -> id` (for a queue line, `type_id` is a queue type and `point` is the start; the end and spacing go in the type's instance parameters).

**Acceptance criteria.**
- [ ] A standing person placed in a 1.2 m wide corridor with a 1.0 m personal-space radius blocks it, and the updated path takes the alternative route.
- [ ] Ignoring the *People* category makes the same path go straight through.
- [ ] A schedule of people by room lists 12 for a room holding a 12-person queue line.

### 4.12.16 Embodied carbon analysis
**ID:** ANA-CARB-001 · **Priority:** P2 · **Ref:** research/03 §0 (2027 version map: carbon data on materials), §15.4 · web: ÖKOBAUDAT; ICE Database FAQs; Introducing Forma Carbon Insights; CarboLifeCalc

**Purpose.** Estimate the embodied carbon (global warming potential, kg CO₂e) of the model from its material quantities and emission factors taken from EPD data, by life-cycle stage, locally and without a vendor cloud service.

**Workflow.**
1. Make sure materials carry carbon assets (DM-MAT-005): either type values in the Material Browser, or use *Match materials* in the analysis dialog.
2. Choose *Analyze › Carbon › Embodied Carbon*. The dialog has four steps:
   1. **Scope**: whole model, current phase only (default: new construction, excluding existing and demolished), a selection, or a design option; categories to include; whether linked models count.
   2. **Data sources**: the active emission-factor libraries in priority order. Reviera ships none of the commercial data sets; the user imports open data sets (for example ÖKOBAUDAT in ILCD+EPD format, or an openLCA export) or a CSV in the documented Reviera factor format. Data sets whose licence forbids embedding in software (for example the ICE database's individual licence) can only be used as a user-imported file on that user's machine.
   3. **Matching**: a grid of project materials with match status (*from material asset*, *matched*, *unmatched*). *Auto-match* proposes factors by material class and name; the user confirms or picks manually. Unmatched materials are reported, not guessed.
   4. **Stages and options**: stages to report (A1–A3 always; optional A4, A5, B1–B5, C1–C4 and module D shown separately), reference study period (default 50 years, for replacement counts in B4), gross floor area for normalisation (default from area plans), and *Write results to IFC*.
3. *Run* starts a background job (ANA-GEN-001). A notification links to the results.

**UI: Results.** A dockable *Carbon Results* panel and an exportable report:
- totals: kg CO₂e for the scope, per stage, and per m² of gross floor area
- **by category** (walls, floors, structural framing, …) and **by material**, as sortable tables and bar charts; biogenic carbon and module D listed separately and never netted into the A–C total
- **by element**: a schedulable *Embodied carbon A1–A3* parameter and per-stage parameters, so schedules, colour schemes and view filters can show hot spots
- a **data quality** column: factor source, generic or product-specific, EPD validity date (expired EPDs flagged)
- *Compare*: two saved runs side by side (for example two design options), with the difference per category

**Behaviour & rules.**
- **Quantity.** For each element and material: volume from the geometry (layer thickness × area for layered types), area for factors declared per m², count for per-piece factors, mass = volume × density (`Pset_MaterialCommon.MassDensity`) for per-kg factors. A unit mismatch with no conversion path (for example a per-m² factor on a material with no area) excludes that material and reports it.
- **Calculation.** GWP = quantity × factor per stage. B4 (replacement) = (A1–A3 + C1–C4) × replacements, with replacements = ceil(study period ÷ reference service life) − 1. Transport (A4) uses a distance and mode per material when given, otherwise is not reported.
- Openings are subtracted; overlapping geometry is counted once per element; elements without materials are listed as *no material*.
- Factors are snapshotted into the run so results stay reproducible after a library update; a library update marks the run stale.
- This is a **built-in provider** (ANA-PLUG-003, family `carbon`); external LCA tools can register as providers of the same family.
- **Export:** CSV and JSON of per-element and per-category results; HTML report; the run's input quantities in a neutral CSV for third-party LCA tools.

**Data (IFC mapping).** When *Write results to IFC* is on, the factor per functional unit goes to `Pset_EnvironmentalImpactIndicators.ClimateChangePerUnit` (with `FunctionalUnitReference`) on the element type, and the element total to `Pset_EnvironmentalImpactValues.ClimateChange` on the occurrence, as DM-MAT-005 describes. The factor libraries, matching table, options and run index are **RXD document** `analysis`; the result package is a file referenced by `IfcDocumentReference`.

**Commands.**
- `embodied_carbon.run(scope?, options?) -> job_id` (`scope`: "model" | "phase" | element_ids[] | design_option_id; `options`: stages, libraries, study_period, gfa, write_ifc)
- `embodied_carbon.import_factors(path, format: "ilcd"|"csv") -> library_id`
- `embodied_carbon.match(material_id, factor_ref)`
- `embodied_carbon.export(job_id, path, format: "csv"|"json"|"html")`
- `embodied_carbon.compare(job_id_a, job_id_b) -> report`

**Acceptance criteria.**
- [x] A 10 m³ concrete wall with density 2 400 kg/m³ and a factor of 0.10 kg CO₂e/kg reports 2 400 kg CO₂e for A1–A3.
- [x] With a study period of 60 years and a reference service life of 25 years, B4 counts 2 replacements.
- [x] A material with no factor is listed as unmatched, and the total states the share of model volume left unmatched.
- [x] Module D and biogenic carbon appear in separate columns and are not subtracted from the A–C total.
- [x] Editing a wall's thickness after a run marks the run stale; re-running changes only that wall's result.

*Built (2026-10-25):* Analyze › **Carbon** › *Embodied Carbon*: the materials grid (material, volume, elements, matched or unmatched, factor or proposal) with *Import Factors…*, *Match…*, *Auto-match* (proposals listed to confirm), *Unmatch*, *Run* and *Results…* (the A–C total and each stage, module D and biogenic apart, the unmatched share, kg CO₂e/m² when a gross floor area is given, a stale notice, by category and by material, excluded materials, *Export…* to CSV or JSON). Quantities: walls (each layer's thickness × length × height less the openings' rectangles), floors and ceilings (each layer × area), roofs (the volume, as the type's material, else "Roof"); other model elements are not quantified yet. Factors come from user libraries (`embodied_carbon.import_factors(path)` in the documented Reviera CSV format: id, name, class, unit kg/m3/m2/piece, a1_a3, a4, a5, c1_c4, d, biogenic, density, service_life, source, valid_until; a library of the same name replaces its factors and keeps the matches; `embodied_carbon.add_library` takes them as JSON); Reviera ships none. Matching by material name (`embodied_carbon.match`, `embodied_carbon.auto_match` by shared words in the factor's name and class, `embodied_carbon.materials`). `embodied_carbon.run(options)` (stages a4, a5, b4, c1_c4; study period, default 50 years; gross floor area) is a compute job since ANA-ENV-001 (2026-10-25): the editor distils the quantity lines (element keys opaque, the map back to GlobalIds kept locally) with the matched factors (`carbon.quantities`), the built-in runner calculates (`analysis.carbon`), and `embodied_carbon.collect` records the results (`embodied_carbon.record`), keeping the last ten runs, named after their jobs, with the factors they used and each element's inputs; the window watches the job and opens the results when it is collected; `embodied_carbon.results(run_id?)` reports the elements whose inputs changed since (stale) and whether the factors did; `embodied_carbon.export`. Not yet: the ILCD+EPD and openLCA readers, scope (phase, selection, design option, categories, links), material carbon assets on materials (DM-MAT-005) and density from materials, transport distances for A4, B1–B3 and B5, the dockable Carbon Results panel with bar charts, per-element schedulable parameters and colour schemes, compare, writing results to IFC, the background job, the HTML report, columns, beams and other elements.

### 4.12.17 Built-in environmental providers (extrapolation)
**ID:** ANA-ENV-001 … ANA-ENV-006 · **Priority:** P2 · **Ref:** owner direction (2026-10-25): "continue advanced feature development including environmental sustainability features, add as logical extrapolations from what is already specified … keeping complex analysis logic in the remote calculation framework"; "Might as well add light, energy modeling, solar power generation estimation, etc."

**Purpose.** The analysis sections above name external engines (EnergyPlus/OpenStudio, Radiance) as the full-fidelity providers. These requirements add **built-in reference providers** (ANA-PLUG-003) for the same families, so energy, loads, daylight, solar and water studies work offline in a plain install, at a fidelity suited to early design. They are *extrapolations*: Reviera's own simplified methods from general engineering knowledge, not the reference product's. Every batch run is a **compute job** of `reviera-analysis-builtin` (DM-RPC-001 … 010): the editor distils what a run needs, the runner calculates, the editor records the results (ANA-GEN-001/002). External providers stay pluggable for the same families; §4.17 Q8 (the default loads engine) is unaffected.

| ID | Family | Built-in method | Job kind |
|---|---|---|---|
| ANA-ENV-001 | `carbon` | Embodied carbon runs (ANA-CARB-001) moved out of process: quantities and matched factors distilled, the run calculated by the runner, recorded with its inputs *(built 2026-10-25)* | `analysis.carbon` |
| ANA-ENV-002 | `solar` | Solar insolation and PV potential (ANA-SOLAR-001): hourly sun positions, isotropic sky patches, direct and diffuse irradiance from the EPW file, ray casting against the shading context, PV yield and payback per face *(built 2026-10-25)* | `analysis.solar` |
| ANA-ENV-003 | `energy` | A simplified energy model from MEP spaces (ANA-EM-003): each space an analytical space; its surfaces from the walls, floors, roofs and openings bounding it, classified exterior, interior, ground or roof, with U-values from the types' thermal properties (or schematic defaults, EXPERT_REVIEW) *(built 2026-10-25)* | — (in the editor, a distillation) |
| ANA-ENV-004 | `loads` | Design heating loads (steady state: transmission at the heating design temperature plus ventilation and infiltration) and design cooling loads (a simplified hourly design-day balance: transmission with a sol-air approximation, solar gains through glazing from the sun model, people, lighting and equipment), per space and per system-zone, written as space results *(built 2026-10-25)* | `analysis.loads` |
| ANA-ENV-005 | `energy` | Annual heating and cooling energy by a lumped hourly zone model (resistance–capacitance network per space: air, surface and mass nodes) driven by the EPW year, set points and the space types' schedules and loads; monthly profiles and totals, operational carbon from a grid emission factor *(built 2026-10-25)* | `analysis.energy` |
| ANA-ENV-006 | `daylight` | Daylight factor on a sensor grid (ANA-LIGHT-002): the sky component under a standard overcast sky through each space's windows by ray casting, plus an internally reflected component from the room's mean reflectance *(built 2026-10-25)* | `analysis.daylight` |

**Behaviour & rules.**
- Inputs and results are as in the sections they extend; anything those sections leave open is Reviera's design, documented in its *Built* note, and provisional engineering values go to EXPERT_REVIEW.
- Results become stale when the model, location or weather change (the weather's revision, ANA-EM-001).
- A run that needs data the model lacks (no location, no weather file, no spaces, a type with no thermal values) is refused naming what is missing, or runs with the documented defaults and lists them.
- Each provider has a verification test against a hand-calculated case (ANA-PLUG-003).

**Commands.** As the extended sections give them (`embodied_carbon.run`, `solar.run`, `energy_model.create`, `hc_loads.run`, `energy.run`, `daylight.run`), each returning a job id, with `…collect` to record a finished job.

*Built — ANA-ENV-005 (2026-10-25):* Sustainability › Energy › *Annual Energy* (infiltration class, thermal mass light/medium/heavy, heating by gas boiler, electric resistance or heat pump with its efficiency or COP, cooling COP, grid and gas emission factors; the last run's options are offered again) and *Energy Results* (floor area, delivered energy, EUI, building peaks, the options; a table of the twelve months and the year — heating and cooling loads, delivered heating, cooling, lighting, equipment, electricity, gas, kg CO₂e — then each space's annual loads; a stale notice). `energy.run(options)` distils the energy model's spaces as the loads do (opaque keys), the site and the weather file's 8 760 hours (dry-bulb, dew point, DNI, DHI; the first weekday from its data period) into `energy.input` and submits an `analysis.energy` job; `energy.collect` records the run on the project (`energy.record`, the last ten); `energy.results(run_id?)`; `energy.status` (stale by input hash). The method, in `annual_energy.rs` with its values in E-39: per space an air, a surface and a mass node; windows and doors to the surface node, opaque walls and roofs by sol-air temperature to the mass node, slabs to the ground at the year's mean temperature; implicit hourly steps after a January warm-up; an ideal thermostat at the space type's set points, set back 4 K unoccupied; latent from people and from dehumidifying outdoor air. Not yet: schedules from Energy Settings (ANA-EM-002) and holidays, sized systems and unmet hours, fans, pumps and hot water, temperature-dependent heat-pump COP, adjacent-space heat transfer (interior surfaces are adiabatic), monthly charts, export and the HTML report, hourly grid factors (ANA-ENV-010).

*Built — ANA-ENV-006 (2026-10-25):* Sustainability › Daylight & Solar › *Daylight Factor* (sensor height, spacing and border, threshold, ceiling, wall and floor reflectances, glazing transmittance; the last study's options are offered again) and *Daylight Results* (the sensor-weighted average and the share of sensors at the threshold; each space's sensors, average, minimum, maximum, uniformity, share at the threshold and reflected component; a stale notice; *Show on Model* colours each sensor's square in 3D views on a fixed scale, 0% blue to 2.5 × the threshold red, *Hide*). `daylight.run(options)` distils each enclosed space's sensor grid (from its floor outline in the energy model, `level_ids` to limit it), its glazing area and transmittance and its room reflectances (opaque keys), and the model's obstructing elements as triangles with each window's visible transmittance (`Pset_DoorWindowGlazingType.VisibleLightTransmittance` on its type, else the default) into `daylight.input` and submits an `analysis.daylight` job; `daylight.collect` records the study on the project (`daylight.record`, the last five); `daylight.results(study_id?)`; `daylight.status` (stale by input hash). The method, in `daylight.rs` with its values in E-40: the CIE overcast sky in patches, rays from each sensor through the panes (transmittances multiplied, any opaque element blocking), plus the split-flux internally reflected component per space. Not yet: material reflectances from the materials' appearance, obstruction angle for C, frames apart from glass, plan-view display with a legend, average daylight factor written to the spaces, export.

**External providers, exchanges and data connectors** (research 2026-10-25, RESEARCH_LOG S0845–S0857). Built-in providers above work offline; these use established engines and open services where a user has them:

| ID | What | Interface | Rules |
|---|---|---|---|
| ANA-ENV-007 | **EnergyPlus provider** (`loads`, `energy`) *(energy built 2026-10-26; loads not yet)* | Reviera writes epJSON from the energy model (ANA-ENV-003), always with `Output:SQLite`; runs `energyplus -w <epw> -d <dir> [-D] in.epJSON` as a compute job on a host where EnergyPlus is installed (found on PATH or in its default folders, version from `energyplus --version`); reads `eplusout.sql` (`ZoneSizes` for design loads, `TabularDataWithStrings` for annual end uses) | Never bundled or renamed (its licence's naming clause); its notice shown in About |
| ANA-ENV-008 | **Radiance provider** (`daylight`) | Reviera writes a Radiance scene (geometry, plastic and glass materials from reflectance and transmittance); daylight factor: `gensky -c`, `oconv`, `rtrace -I` on the sensor grid; annual: `epw2wea`, `gendaymtx`, `rfluxmtx`, `dctimestep` | Offered as an optional download; Accelerad detected only |
| ANA-ENV-009 | **Exchanges** | HBJSON export (honeybee-schema, BSD-3) for Ladybug Tools, whose runners (AGPL, separate processes) are detected and offered (`lbt-recipes run`); gbXML 8.01 export (ANA-EM-004) for other tools and OpenStudio *(gbXML export and loads import built 2026-10-25; HBJSON export built 2026-10-26; runner detection not yet)* | Runners never bundled |
| ANA-ENV-010 | **Data connectors** (user-triggered, each switchable off, nothing needed offline) | PVGIS (no key): `tmy` as EPW into `weather.import`, `PVcalc` as a cross-check of PV potential; climate.onebuilding.org station picker (its KML/spreadsheet index, download on demand); geocoding by Nominatim or a configured Photon/self-hosted endpoint; site elevation (Open-Meteo); hourly weather from Open-Meteo (opt-in, with the user's key for commercial use); grid carbon intensity (UK Carbon Intensity without a key; Ember or Electricity Maps with the user's key); emission factors from openEPD and olca-schema JSON-LD files, an openLCA IPC server, ÖKOBAUDAT (soda4LCA) and EC3 (the user's account) | Keys and accounts are the user's, kept in the system keychain (DM-RPC-011's store), never shown to MCP or Lua; Nominatim per its usage policy (searches the user starts, at most 1 per second, an identifying User-Agent, cached, no autocomplete); attribution of CC BY and ODbL data in Help › Data Sources; a bundled city list from Natural Earth (public domain); never bundled: onebuilding files (no stated licence), ICE (no embedding), EC3 data, NREL SPA code |

*Built — ANA-ENV-007, annual energy (2026-10-26):* Sustainability › Energy › *Annual Energy* has an *Engine* choice: the built-in model, or EnergyPlus with its version when `energy.providers` finds it (`REVIERA_ENERGYPLUS`, the PATH, or `/usr/local/EnergyPlus-*`, `/Applications/EnergyPlus-*`, `C:\EnergyPlusV*`, the version from `energyplus --version`), else marked not found. `energy.run(provider: energyplus)` distils the same spaces, loads, set points, opening hours and options as the built-in model and writes them as epJSON (`energyplus.rs`): geometry from the HBJSON export with zones named by the opaque space keys, `BuildingSurface:Detailed` and `FenestrationSurface:Detailed` in world coordinates, `Material:NoMass` and `WindowMaterial:SimpleGlazingSystem` constructions, `Construction:AirBoundary` for separation lines, `Schedule:Compact` for occupancy, lights, equipment and set points, `People`, `Lights`, `ElectricEquipment`, `ZoneInfiltration:DesignFlowRate`, `ZoneVentilation:DesignFlowRate` for outdoor air, a dual set-point thermostat and `ZoneHVAC:IdealLoadsAirSystem` per zone, the run period from the weather file's first weekday, ground temperatures, `Output:SQLite` and monthly and hourly `Output:Variable`s (values in E-42). The job (`analysis.energy.energyplus`, in the built-in runner) sets the installed version, runs `energyplus -w in.epw -d out in.epJSON` in a temporary folder (kept with `REVIERA_KEEP_ENERGYPLUS`), can be cancelled, logs the warning and severe counts from `eplusout.err` and fails with its severe lines, and reads `ReportData` from `eplusout.sql` (outside warm-up): the ideal loads' supply air heating and cooling energy and lights and equipment by month, peaks from the hourly rates; delivered energy, carbon and EUI follow as in the built-in model. `energy.collect` records it as an EnergyPlus run and *Energy Results* says which engine ran. Help › About carries EnergyPlus's notice; it is never bundled or renamed. The written epJSON was validated against EnergyPlus 26.2's published `Energy+.schema.epJSON` on 2026-10-26 (no errors, every field name known); EnergyPlus itself was not run in development, so the first real runs should be checked against the built-in model. Not yet: design-day loads (`ZoneSizes`, the `loads` kind), real HVAC systems and fan and pump energy, constructions with mass from the material layers, the tabular end-use summary, shading context.

*Built — ANA-ENV-009, HBJSON (2026-10-26):* File › *Export HBJSON…* (`hbjson.export(path)`) writes the energy model as a honeybee-schema `Model` (version 2.3.0, meters, tolerance 0.01): a `Room` per analytical space (identifier `sp-` + GlobalId with `$` as `-`, the same as gbXML's space id; display name, story from the level, zone from the system-zone), its `Face`s with vertices counter-clockwise seen from outside (`Wall`, `Floor`, `RoofCeiling`; separation lines `AirBoundary`), boundary conditions `Outdoors`, `Ground` for slabs on grade, `Surface` naming the twin face and room for shared walls, floors and ceilings (each room keeps its side of the element; twins are the faces of the same element facing back with the same area, paired only when both agree), else `Adiabatic` (counted in the report); windows and doors of exterior walls as `Aperture`s and `Door`s; `ModelEnergyProperties` with an `OpaqueConstructionAbridged` per class and U-value (a no-mass layer, E-41) and a `WindowConstructionAbridged` per glazing (`EnergyWindowMaterialSimpleGlazSys`: U, SHGC, visible transmittance). Returns the counts and warnings. Field names follow the published honeybee-schema (S0859); nothing of it is bundled. The test model (four rooms, a window and a door) was checked on 2026-10-26 with honeybee-core's `Model.check_all` (no errors, every room a closed solid) and written to IDF by honeybee-energy, both run outside Reviera; window and door vertices are kept 5 mm inside their wall's edges because honeybee rejects a sub-face on its parent's edge. Not yet: program types, loads and schedules, shading context, Radiance modifiers, detecting Ladybug Tools runners (`lbt-recipes`), an import back.

*Built — ANA-ENV-010, PVGIS (2026-10-25):* Sustainability › Site › *PVGIS Weather* (`pvgis.tmy(start_year?, end_year?)`: after the user confirms that the site's coordinates are sent, a typical meteorological year for the project location is fetched as EPW, kept with the saved project as `<project>.resources/weather/pvgis-<lat>_<lon>.epw` and imported by `weather.import`) and *Data Connectors* (`connectors.list`, `connectors.set(name, enabled)`: each connector with its description and attribution, switchable off per user in `connectors.json`; a connector that is off refuses to run); Sustainability › Daylight & Solar › *PVGIS Check* (`pvgis.pv(peak_power, loss 14 %, tilt 35°, azimuth 180°)`: PVcalc's yearly and monthly yield, kWh/kWp and plane irradiation, with the attribution, as a cross-check of the solar study; the azimuth is turned into PVGIS's aspect, 0 south, −90 east). PVGIS's error message is passed on (for example a location over the sea). The service address can be replaced by `REVIERA_PVGIS_URL` (plain http only for a local address); requests carry Reviera's user agent and the platform's certificate roots. Response formats were checked against the live service on 2026-10-25.

*Built — ANA-ENV-010, site connectors (2026-10-26):* Sustainability › Site › *Find Place* (`geocode.search(query, limit 5)`: Nominatim's `search?format=jsonv2`, or a compatible geocoder in `REVIERA_GEOCODER_URL` such as a self-hosted Nominatim; the user types and starts each search, requests at least a second apart, answers cached for the session, an identifying User-Agent with the project's address; the places listed with their kind and coordinates, *Use as Location* sets the latitude, longitude and place name) and *Site Elevation* (`elevation.fetch(set true)`: Open-Meteo's elevation API at the project location, written to the location after the user confirms); Sustainability › Energy › *Grid Carbon (GB)* (`grid_intensity.fetch(period month|year)`: the Carbon Intensity API's statistics in 30-day windows — its limit is 31 days — averaged, with the lowest and highest half-hour, in kg CO₂e/kWh as a grid factor for annual energy, Great Britain only); Help › *Data Sources* lists each connector, whether it is on and the credit results made with it must carry. Each connector can be switched off (`nominatim`, `open_meteo`, `uk_carbon_intensity`); a connector that is off makes no request. Response formats were checked against the live services on 2026-10-26 with generic queries. Not yet: Photon's GeoJSON answers, the onebuilding station picker, Open-Meteo hourly weather, Ember and Electricity Maps (the user's key), openEPD/olca/ÖKOBAUDAT/EC3 factors, a bundled city list, keeping the grid factor with the project.

## 4.13 P&ID integration

**Design stance.** The reference product's P&ID integration depends on a vendor cloud service. Reviera instead reads **open P&ID exchange data**: the **DEXPI** XML standard, which is based on ISO 15926 and the Proteus schema. It offers the same guided-modelling and validation workflow, working locally.

### 4.13.1 P&ID line list and guided modelling
**ID:** MEP-PID-001 · **Priority:** P2 · **Ref:** research/03 §14

**Workflow.**
1. Choose *Systems › P&ID › Line List* and open a P&ID exchange file, DEXPI XML or a CSV line list.
2. The palette's top pane previews the diagram. DEXPI graphics are rendered as 2D; for CSV, an optional PDF of the diagram can be loaded.
3. The bottom pane lists **pipeline segments**, searchable by line number or component. A status glyph shows *modelled*, *partially modelled* or *not modelled*. The glyphs use theme tokens with text labels, so they never rely on colour alone.
4. Double-click a line to list its segments, inline components and from/to equipment. Hovering highlights items in the preview.
5. Model pipes and components in the 3D model, guided by the list. Starting a pipe from the palette sets its system type and size automatically.
6. **Map** P&ID items to existing model elements.

**Behaviour & rules.** Model elements remember their P&ID tag. Re-loading an updated P&ID file keeps the mappings by tag.

**Data (IFC mapping).** The P&ID tag is written to `IfcElement.Tag`, and pipelines to `IfcDistributionSystem.Name`. The mapping table and the source file reference are **RXD document** `mep_settings` (P&ID section). The source file is referenced with `IfcDocumentReference`.

**Commands.**
- `pid.open(path) -> pid_id`
- `pid.list_lines(pid_id, filter?) -> lines[]`
- `pid.start_pipe(pid_id, line_id, segment_id) -> tool_session`
- `pid.map(pid_item_id, element_ids[])`

**Acceptance criteria.**
- [ ] Loading a DEXPI sample file lists every piping network segment with its line number, nominal size and from/to equipment.
- [ ] Starting a pipe from a 50 mm line sets the pipe diameter to 50 mm and the system type from the service mapping.

### 4.13.2 P&ID validation and mapping settings
**ID:** MEP-PID-002 · **Priority:** P2 · **Ref:** research/03 §14 ("Validate", "Mappings")

**Purpose.** Check that the 3D piping model agrees with the P&ID, and define how P&ID classes and properties translate into Reviera types, families and parameters.

**Workflow.**
1. Set up the mappings once in *Systems › P&ID › P&ID Settings* (also `mep_settings.show(kind: "pid")`).
2. Model from the line list (MEP-PID-001).
3. Choose *Validate* on the palette for one line, the selected lines, or the whole P&ID. Results appear as status labels in the line list and as a report.
4. Double-click a result to select and zoom to the model elements involved; use *Ignore* on a part that is intentionally different.

**Behaviour & rules.**
- **Validate** compares the model against the P&ID and marks each line:
  - fully modelled: every P&ID component on the line has a mapped model element, connected in the same order
  - mismatch, such as a size, spec or component difference (nominal size differs, pipe type differs from the spec mapping, or an inline component uses a different family than the mapping)
  - disconnected: the mapped elements of the line do not form one connected path (from the connectivity graph, MEP-CONN-002)
  - with ignored parts: differences the user marked *Ignore*, kept with the user name and date
  - with additional parts: model elements tagged with the line number that the P&ID does not contain (fittings and flanges added by routing preferences are not counted)

  Indicators use text and icons drawn from theme tokens.
- Validation is read-only and runs in the background; it never changes the model. Results are stale once the model or the P&ID file changes.
- **P&ID Settings** has two tabs, *System Types* and *Object Mapping*. They map:
  - piping services to pipe system types
  - pipe line specs to pipe types
  - inline assets to pipe accessory families
  - equipment classes to equipment families
  - P&ID properties to parameters (text, number and Yes/No; units converted where the P&ID states them)
- Each tab is a two-column grid (P&ID item → Reviera target) with a search box, *Auto-map by name* and *Import/Export* as CSV. Rows with no target are labelled "Not mapped" and count as mismatches during validation. A target type or family that is deleted from the project makes its row invalid; OK is allowed but the dialog lists invalid rows.
- Mappings can be saved as a named mapping set and reused across projects through *Transfer Project Standards*.

**Data (IFC mapping).** Mappings, ignore records and the last validation result are stored in **RXD document** `mep_settings` (P&ID section). Line numbers on model elements are in `IfcElement.Tag` (MEP-PID-001).

**Commands.**
- `pid.validate(pid_id, line_ids?[]) -> report`
- `pid.ignore(pid_id, item_id, ignored: bool)`
- `pid_settings.set_mapping(kind, rules[])`
- `pid_settings.auto_map(kind) -> rules[]`
- `pid_settings.export_mapping(path)`, `pid_settings.import_mapping(path)`

**Acceptance criteria.**
- [ ] Changing a modelled valve to a different family than the mapping specifies marks its line "mismatch", and the report names the valve.
- [ ] Deleting a pipe segment in the middle of a fully modelled line changes its status to "disconnected" after re-validation.
- [ ] A difference marked *Ignore* is reported under "ignored parts" and no longer causes a mismatch.
- [ ] *Auto-map by name* maps the service "CW" to a pipe system type named "CW" and leaves unmatched services labelled "Not mapped".

| Fabrication spool / hanger | `IfcElementAssembly` "SPOOL" / `IfcDiscreteAccessory` "HANGER" | `IfcRelAggregates`, `IfcRelConnectsElements` | — |
| Space | `IfcSpace` (ObjectType "MEPSpace") | `IfcRelSpaceBoundary` | `Qto_SpaceBaseQuantities`, `Pset_SpaceThermal*`, `Pset_SpaceLightingRequirements` |

**General rule.** Anything not listed above, and any value that has no standard home, is stored as RXD (see "Where data is stored" at the start of this chapter) and keyed by GlobalId. The IFC file shall stay valid and meaningful to other tools without it.

## 4.15 Optional engine integration summary [Suggestions]

| Capability | Provider kind | Built-in | Suggested open engine (external process) | Licence note (verify before bundling) |
|------------|---------------|----------|-------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------|
| Structural analysis (linear static, modal, non-linear) | `structural` | — | PyNite or Frame3DD (frames), CalculiX, Code_Aster (via IfcOpenShell's ifc2ca), Kratos Multiphysics; xara (seismic, OpenSees-based), all batch providers as compute jobs (ANA-PLUG-004, §2.17) | MIT or GPL-3.0; GPL-2.0-or-later; GPL-3.0; BSD; BSD-2-Clause (OpenSees itself: commercial licence needed, not suggested) |
| Earthquake assessment (response spectrum, time history, pushover) | `seismic` | Equivalent lateral force from the building code's spectrum (DM-CODE-001) | xara (OpenSees-based); Code_Aster | BSD-2-Clause; GPL-3.0 |
| Steel connection checks | `structural` (connection_check) | Sample Lua bolt check | Community providers | Must be GPL-compatible if in-process |
| Load combination generation | built-in rules | EN 1990 / ASCE 7-style templates as data | — | Templates authored from the published equations, not copied text |
| Energy simulation and HVAC sizing | `energy` | — | EnergyPlus via OpenStudio | BSD-style |
| Heating/cooling loads (RTS) | `loads` | Native RTS (optional, §4.17 Q8) | EnergyPlus sizing run | — |
| Daylight and electric lighting | `daylight` | Lumen method | Radiance | Radiance licence (BSD-like) |
| Solar insolation, PV, sun paths and shadow studies | `solar` | Sky-patch cumulative | Radiance; pvlib-python | BSD-like; BSD-3 |
| Hydraulic networks (domestic water, fire) | `hydraulic` | Duct/pipe friction, hydronic loops | EPANET | Public domain/MIT |
| Stormwater runoff and drainage networks | `stormwater` | Rational-method roof and gutter sizing (MEP-PIPE-010) | EPA SWMM | Public domain (verify) |
| Interior airflow and ventilation (CFD) | `airflow` | — | OpenFOAM | GPL-3.0 |
| External wind flow and facade pressures (CFD) | `wind` | — | OpenFOAM | GPL-3.0 |
| Clash detection | `clash` | OCCT + BVH | — | — |
| Route analysis | `route` | Visibility graph | Recast/Detour navigation mesh | zlib |
| Embodied carbon | `carbon` | Quantity × emission factor (ANA-CARB-001) | openLCA, for full life-cycle assessment | MPL-2.0 (verify); data sets have their own licences |
| Steel CNC | output plugin | — | DSTV NC writer | Open format documentation |
| Precast CAM | output plugin | Neutral JSON/CSV | Unitechnik / PXML writers | Depends on documentation terms |
| P&ID | importer | CSV line list | DEXPI reader | Open standard |

## 4.16 Command catalog

Every command below is registered once in the command registry and is exposed automatically to the UI, to Lua (`reviera.<command>(...)`) and to MCP (one tool per command). Commands marked "Results only" start background jobs and commit their results in a separate transaction that can be undone. Commands marked "No" are queries, exports or view/session state and leave model data unchanged.

## 4.17 Open questions and deviations from the reference

### 4.17.1 Intentional deviations

| # | Area | Reference behaviour | Reviera behaviour | Reason |
|---|------|--------------------|-------------------|--------|
| D1 | UI | Options Bar holds size, elevation and placement options (2026) | No Options Bar. Everything is on the contextual ribbon and in Properties. | Follows the reference's own 2027 direction and Reviera's UI chapter. |
| D2 | Ribbon | Separate Precast tab (2026) | One **Concrete** tab holds reinforcement and precast | Follows the 2027 direction, with fewer tabs. |
| D3 | Structural solver | Proprietary solver link and proprietary exchange file | Provider interface with IFC Structural Analysis View and neutral JSON exchange. Open engines as plugins. | No proprietary dependency; open standards (§4.3.11). |
| D4 | Load combinations | Online generation that needs sign-in | Offline, rule-based generation from editable code templates | No cloud dependency, and works offline. |
| D5 | Analytical automation | Visual-programming packages | Lua rule packages, shipped under GPL | Lua is Reviera's scripting layer (TECH_STACK §3.5). |
| D6 | Steel connections | Proprietary connection engine and content in a local database server | Open parametric connection library (manifest + Lua generator), stored as files | Proprietary content cannot be used; a database server is unnecessary. |
| D7 | Steel interop | Proprietary exchange formats with detailing software | IFC as the primary exchange, plus an optional DSTV NC plugin | Open formats only. |
| D8 | Interference check | Excludes detailed steel elements and fabrication parts | **Includes** them | Reviera writes full geometry for both, so there is no technical reason to exclude them. This removes the need for an external tool. |
| D9 | MEP fabrication | Proprietary configuration database and part files; proprietary job export | **ROFC** open content model; open job export (IFC + JSON). Proprietary part files are **not** read or written. | Proprietary formats are out of scope (00_overview). |
| D10 | Duct fitting losses | Proprietary fitting-loss database | Loss data per fitting type, with open coefficient tables from public-domain sources and user-supplied tables | The proprietary database cannot be redistributed. |
| D11 | Fixture-unit conversion and ampacity | Ships code tables from specific editions | Built-in method from public-domain sources. Code tables are user-loaded content. | Code tables may be copyrighted. |
| D12 | Lighting and solar analysis | Cloud service with subscription | Local providers (Radiance suggested) | No vendor cloud (P3 policy). |
| D13 | Systems analysis | Built-in simulation integration | Same open engine (EnergyPlus) through OpenStudio, as an optional external provider | Keeps the core GPL-clean, and the engine can be swapped. |
| D14 | P&ID | Vendor cloud P&ID collaboration | Local DEXPI (open standard) or CSV line-list import | No vendor cloud; uses an open standard. |
| D15 | Precast CAM | Built-in vendor-specific writers | Neutral JSON/CSV export, plus format plugins where documentation allows | Depends on the licensing terms of each format's documentation. |
| D16 | Legacy zones | Hidden behind an ini switch | No legacy loads tool. Legacy zones on import convert to system-zones. | Simpler; matches the 2026/2027 direction. |
| D17 | Piles | Generic foundation families | Explicit pile and pile-cap support for clean `IfcPile` export | IFC compatibility. |
| D18 | Sprinkler hydraulics | Not supported | Optional hydraulic-calculation provider | Fills a common gap; optional. |
| D19 | Path of travel | Single level only | Same in the first release; multi-level is under consideration (Q9) | Scope control. |

### 4.17.2 Open questions

| # | Question | Options / notes |
|---|----------|-----------------|
| Q1 | ~~RXD content areas~~ | **Resolved**: `model/structural` (project document) and the `structural` element section are registered in 02a §6.4–§6.5. |
| Q2 | Analytical link representation. IFC4 has no dedicated rigid-link entity. | A `USERDEFINED` curve member (chosen here) or a connection condition on `IfcRelConnectsStructuralMember`. Check against buildingSMART structural MVD guidance. |

| Q6 | Breakers per circuit | Model each breaker as `IfcProtectiveDevice` nested in the board (more faithful, many more entities) or keep breaker data on the circuit. |
| Q7 | Free-form longitudinal splicing | The reference extends this in 2027. Decide whether Reviera's first release includes it. *Deferred to the post-Alpha/POC review (owner, 2026-10-12).* |

The initial version writes only the assembly aggregation and keeps the source link in RXD (STR-PRE-002). A real decision needs advice from an IFC and precast domain expert (buildingSMART precast/structural guidance, and how receiving tools behave). Candidate to evaluate: `IfcRelAssignsToProduct` from source to pieces. |
| Q14 | Engineering defaults awaiting subject-matter expert review | **Open (owner, 2026-10-19): use the most logical provisional values and have them reviewed by a subject-matter expert.** The list, with each value, its reasoning and where it is used, is `design_documents/EXPERT_REVIEW.md`: concrete density (2.5 t/m³), precast wall and slab segmentation defaults, the default lap (50 bar diameters), coupler sleeve proportions, cover on leaning faces, concrete roofs as hosts, morphed bar placement, free-form shell cover, rebar steel mass; and for MEP (E-16 … E-18) the starter component types' sizes, flows and loads, the built-in system types' fluid temperatures, and the fitting proportions and duct and pipe roughness. Help pages call these values provisional. |

# Chapter 5 — Views, Graphics, Annotation, Schedules, Sheets and Output

**Area code:** DOC · **Status:** Draft 1 (2026-10-12) · **Primary source:** `research/04_documentation_collaboration.md` (cited as `research/04 §n`)
**Related chapters:** Chapter 1 (UI shell: ribbon, Project Browser, View Control Bar, keymap), Chapter 2 (DM: data model, families, parameters, formulas, file/IO), Chapter 2a (Reviera Extension Data, RXD), Chapter 3 (ARC: datums, rooms, areas), Chapter 6 (COL: worksharing display, links, positioning, BCF).
**Reference:** Autodesk Revit 2026/2027 documentation and output features, used as the functional reference only.

This chapter specifies how Reviera turns its IFC model into drawings and deliverables. It covers every view type, the rules that decide how each element is drawn in each view, model-reporting and drafting annotation, schedules, sheets, and every output channel. It also specifies how documentation objects persist inside the IFC file, and the hidden-line and GPU pipelines that produce the pictures.

---

## 5.0 Core principles

These principles apply to every requirement in this chapter.

| ID | Principle | Priority |
|----|-----------|----------|
| DOC-CORE-001 | **Views are live projections.** A view stores only its *definition* (type, extents, camera, graphics settings, view-owned annotation). Projected model linework, cut poché and shaded images are always derived, and they are regenerated when the model changes. Derived results may be cached, but the cache is never the source of truth. Cache entries are keyed by element revision and view-definition revision (DOC-HLR-001); a cache miss or a corrupt entry only costs regeneration time, never a wrong drawing. Closing and reopening a project discards no definition data and may discard every cache. The only stored derived result is a saved rendering image (DOC-OUT-011). | P0 |
| DOC-CORE-002 | **Paper-space sizing.** Annotation symbols, text, tag heads, dimension text, line patterns, drafting fill patterns and annotation line weights are specified in paper millimetres. They render at `paper size × view scale` in model space, so that changing the view scale resizes them automatically. Model patterns (DOC-GFX-014), model text and model lines are the exception: they are sized in real units. Annotation positions are stored in view coordinates, so a scale change keeps each tag's anchor on its host while its head grows or shrinks around that anchor; leaders are re-elbowed, never re-routed. Sheets are always 1:1, so sheet annotation is the same in paper and model space. | P0 |
| DOC-CORE-003 | **Model-reporting annotation is associative.** Tags, dimensions, spot dimensions and element/material keynotes bind to model references (element GlobalId plus a stable geometric sub-reference). They update when the referenced element changes and become *orphaned* (kept, flagged, drawn in a warning colour) when the reference disappears. A reference is re-resolved on every regeneration of the view; when a sub-reference cannot be found but the element still exists, Reviera tries the named sub-reference rules of Chapter 2a (for example the same face role on a split wall) before orphaning. An orphan can be re-hosted with *Pick new host* or deleted; it never silently attaches to another element. | P0 |
| DOC-CORE-004 | **View-owned elements.** Text, detail lines, regions, detail components, revision clouds and similar drafting items belong to exactly one view (or sheet) and appear nowhere else, except through dependent views (DOC-VIEW-011). Deleting a view deletes its view-owned elements in the same undo step; the confirmation states how many there are. Copying them to another view is an explicit act (clipboard *Paste aligned to selected views*, *Duplicate with Detailing*, or detail groups) and always creates new objects with new ids. Model elements are never view-owned. | P0 |
| DOC-CORE-005 | **One sheet per model view.** A graphical model view (plan, section, elevation, callout, 3D, drafting, rendering) can be placed on at most one sheet. Schedules, legends, keynote legends, sheet lists, view lists and note blocks can be placed on any number of sheets. The rule is checked by `sheet.place_view`, `viewport.swap_view` and `viewport.move_to_sheet`, which fail with `view.already_on_sheet` (naming the sheet) instead of placing a second copy. To show the same area twice, the user duplicates the view, usually as a dependent (DOC-VIEW-011). Assembly views follow the same rule (§5.16). | P0 |
| DOC-CORE-006 | **One draw list, many outputs.** Every 2D result (on-screen hidden-line view, print, PDF, DXF/DWG, raster image) is produced from the same intermediate *draw list* (DOC-HLR-004). Output is what you see on screen, apart from the documented print options (DOC-OUT-001). The differences allowed between screen and output are exactly: temporary display state (DOC-GFX-008, temporary view properties, reveal hidden, displacement highlight) never prints; *Thin lines* is screen-only; the print options hide or recolour the items they name; raster processing (DOC-HLR-007) changes shaded content only. Any other difference is a defect. | P0 |
| DOC-CORE-007 | **Everything is a command.** Every creation, edit and output operation in this chapter is a registered command, so it is reachable from the ribbon, Lua and MCP. Read-only queries (for example `graphics.explain`) are commands too, flagged as not undoable. Commands that open a dialog (for example `template.manage`, `revision.manage`) are UI entry points only: every change made in the dialog is applied through the undoable commands of the same requirement, so a dialog session that changes five things records those five commands as one undo step named after the dialog. Without a UI (Lua, MCP, headless), dialog commands fail with `ui.unavailable`. | P0 |
| DOC-CORE-008 | **RXD persistence.** Every documentation object defined here persists as Reviera Extension Data (RXD, §5.1, Chapter 2a), embedded in the IFC file by default and keyed to the model by IFC GlobalIds. A project opened locally or downloaded from BIMserver therefore reproduces every view, sheet and annotation exactly, and the file remains valid standard IFC. When another tool has deleted or changed elements that RXD refers to, the reconciliation pass of Chapter 2a §7 runs on open: references to missing elements become orphans (DOC-CORE-003), and nothing is deleted without a report. Session-only state (temporary hide/isolate, highlight modes, render history) is never written to RXD. | P0 |

**Acceptance criteria (core).**
- [ ] Changing a wall's thickness updates every plan, section, schedule and sheet that shows it, without the user refreshing anything.
- [ ] Changing a plan from 1:100 to 1:50 halves the model-space height of every text note in it while its printed height stays the same.
- [ ] Deleting a tagged door leaves the tag in the view marked as orphaned, and the warnings list reports it.
- [ ] Saving a project with views, sheets, schedules and annotation, closing it and reopening it gives identical PDF output (byte-identical page content streams, excluding timestamps).

---

## 5.1 Persistence of documentation objects

**ID:** DOC-IFC-001 · **Priority:** P0 · **Ref:** research/04 §11; TECH_STACK §3.1, §3.7.3; spec/02a_extension_data_format.md

**Purpose.** Views, sheets, schedules, graphic standards and annotation are not building data, and IFC entities cannot express them without loss. Reviera stores them as **Reviera Extension Data (RXD)**: versioned JSON documents with stable object ids, defined in Chapter 2a (`02a_extension_data_format.md`). By default RXD is embedded in the IFC file as valid, standard IFC, so a single `.ifc` file carries the whole project. Chapter 2a defines the carrier (property sets, payload encoding, the alternative external carrier), the object envelope, the reference syntax and the merge rules. This chapter does not redefine any of that. It only names the RXD documents this chapter uses, and specifies how documentation is *exported* as IFC annotation for other tools.

**Behaviour & rules.**
- **Loading.** On open, `views/index`, `sheets/index`, `views/templates`, `views/filters`, `views/types`, `views/color_schemes`, the `standards/*` documents and the `project/*` documents load at once. `views/<viewId>`, `views/annotation/<viewId>`, `schedules/<scheduleId>` and `sheets/<sheetId>` load lazily, the first time the view, sheet or schedule is opened, printed, exported, scheduled (view lists, sheet lists) or queried through Lua or MCP.
- **Saving.** Reviera tracks changes per RXD document. On save, only changed documents are serialised again; unchanged documents are written byte-identical, which keeps BIMserver revisions and text diffs small.
- **Damaged documents.** A document that fails its schema check on load is quarantined: its view, sheet or schedule is listed as *damaged* in the Project Browser and cannot be opened, its raw JSON is kept unchanged and written back unchanged on save, and the problem is listed in the warnings list. The rest of the project opens normally. `rxd.status` (Chapter 2) reports quarantined documents.
- **Versions.** Each document carries the RXD format version (Chapter 2a). Unknown fields from a newer minor version are kept and written back. A document from a newer major version opens read-only, with a banner naming the version.
- **Deleting model elements** never deletes RXD annotation that refers to them; the annotation becomes an orphan (DOC-CORE-003). `rxd.reconcile` (Chapter 2a) can report or remove orphans in bulk.

**Commands.** Persistence has no commands of its own: saving and opening use `file.save`, `file.save_as` and `file.open` (Chapter 2), and inspection uses `rxd.get_document`, `rxd.status` and `rxd.reconcile` (Chapters 2 and 2a). Acceptance criteria are in §5.1.3.

### 5.1.1 What lives where

| Data | Store | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Elements, types, materials, levels, grids, spatial structure, standard Psets/Qtos, parameter values | IFC entities | Chapter 2. Never duplicated in RXD. |
| Element-scoped documentation data (phase created/demolished, design option membership, per-element display flags) | element-scoped RXD on the element (Chapter 2a) | Also written as the standard `Status` property on export (DOC-GFX-017). |
| Views (all kinds), view range, crop, camera, section box, per-view overrides, hidden elements | RXD documents `views/index` and `views/<viewId>` | One document per view, loaded lazily when the view opens. |
| Navigation state: each view's latest camera and Home (UI-NAV-001) | RXD document `views/state` | Written with the next save; never makes the model modified. |
| View templates, view filters, selection sets | RXD documents `views/templates`, `views/filters`, `model/selection_sets` | |
| View-owned annotation (dimensions, spot dimensions, text, tags, keynotes, symbols, detail lines, regions, detail components, repeating details, insulation, revision clouds, plan regions, colour fill legends, matchlines, view references, elevation markers, legend components) | RXD document `views/annotation/<viewId>` | Kinds `anno.*`. |
| Object styles, line weights, line styles, line patterns, fill patterns, text/dimension/tag styles, halftone settings, detail-level map, discipline profiles | RXD documents `standards/*` | |
| Schedules (all kinds, including keynote legends, sheet lists, view lists, note blocks) | RXD document `schedules/<scheduleId>` | |
| Sheets, title block instances, viewports, schedule instances, sheet annotation, guide grids, saved positions, sheet collections | RXD documents `sheets/index` and `sheets/<sheetId>` | |
| Revisions and revision settings | RXD document `project/revisions` | |
| Phases, phase filters, phase graphics | RXD document `project/phases` | |
| Design option sets and options | RXD document `project/design_options` | |
| Print, PDF, image and export setups; view/sheet sets | RXD document `project/settings` (section `output`) | |
| Images (title block logos, image underlays, saved renderings, schedule images) | RXD assets (Chapter 2a) | |

**Rules.**
- Every documentation object in this chapter is an RXD object with the common envelope (stable `id`, `kind`, per-object `rev`, `name`, `data`, `ext`). References to model objects use IFC GlobalIds, with named geometric sub-references (for example `#face:core.ext`) for dimensions and linework overrides. References between RXD objects use their stable ids. Index-based topology references are never stored.
- Each object kind used below is registered in the Chapter 2a kind catalogue with a JSON Schema before implementation. The **Data** paragraph of each requirement names the RXD document and kind, and lists the payload fields this chapter depends on; the schema is normative.
- Derived results (hidden-line linework, cut poché, schedule cell values, rendered pixels) are never stored in RXD. Saved renderings (DOC-OUT-011) are the one exception: they are stored as image assets.
- Because RXD is merged per object by stable id (three-way, Chapter 2a and Chapter 6 COL-MRG-001), the documents are split so that two users editing different views, sheets or annotation do not conflict.

### 5.1.2 IFC export of documentation as IFC annotation

**ID:** DOC-IFC-002 · **Priority:** P1 · **Ref:** research/04 §6.4 (*Export 2D plan view elements*)

**Purpose.** Other IFC tools do not read RXD. Viewers, facility-management tools and other authoring tools may still want drawings and annotation. The export setup option *Include documentation as IFC annotation* (DOC-OUT-006) writes them as standard IFC4 presentation entities. This is an interoperability export: Reviera never treats it as its own store. When Reviera opens a foreign IFC containing such annotation, it shows that annotation read-only as imported drafting (Chapter 6, COL-LNK-001).

**Behaviour & rules.** When the option is on, for each view selected in the export setup:
- **Contexts.** Reviera creates `IfcGeometricRepresentationSubContext` instances under the `Plan` and `Model` contexts with `ContextIdentifier = 'Annotation'`, a `TargetView` of `PLAN_VIEW`, `REFLECTED_PLAN_VIEW`, `SECTION_VIEW`, `ELEVATION_VIEW` or `MODEL_VIEW`, and `TargetScale` equal to the view's scale (for example `0.01` for 1:100). Sheets, if exported, use a sub-context with `TargetView = USERDEFINED` and `UserDefinedTargetView = 'Sheet'`, in paper millimetres.
- **Grouping.** Each exported view becomes an `IfcGroup` (`ObjectType = 'DRAWING'`, `Name` = view name) whose members (`IfcRelAssignsToGroup`) are that view's `IfcAnnotation` objects. Plan annotation may optionally be contained in the view's storey (`IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure`).
- **Annotation objects.** Each annotation becomes one `IfcAnnotation`. In IFC4, its class is given by `ObjectType` (`DIMENSION`, `TEXT`, `TAG`, `SYMBOL`, `DETAIL_LINE`, `FILLED_REGION`, `REVISION_CLOUD`, `MATCHLINE`, …). In IFC4X3 exports, `PredefinedType` is set to the matching `IfcAnnotationTypeEnum` value where one exists, otherwise `USERDEFINED` with the same `ObjectType`. Model-reporting annotation is related to the element it reports on with `IfcRelAssignsToProduct` (RelatingProduct = the element), so consumers can tell which door a tag belongs to.
- **Curves.** Lines, polylines, arcs and splines are items of an `IfcGeometricCurveSet`, using `IfcPolyline`, `IfcIndexedPolyCurve` (with arc segments), `IfcTrimmedCurve` of `IfcCircle`/`IfcEllipse`, and `IfcBSplineCurveWithKnots`. Representation identifier `Annotation`; representation type `Annotation2D`, or `GeometricCurveSet` when only curves are present.
- **Fills.** Regions and poché use `IfcAnnotationFillArea` (outer and inner boundaries), styled by `IfcFillAreaStyle` containing `IfcFillAreaStyleHatching` (one per hatch line family), `IfcColourRgb` for solid and background fills, or `IfcFillAreaStyleTiles` where hatching cannot express the pattern.
- **Line appearance.** `IfcStyledItem` → `IfcCurveStyle` with `CurveWidth` (paper mm scaled by the context scale), `CurveColour`, and `CurveFont` as an `IfcCurveStyleFont` built from the line pattern's dash and gap segments.
- **Text.** `IfcTextLiteralWithExtent` (literal, placement, path, `IfcPlanarExtent`, box alignment) styled by `IfcTextStyle` with `IfcTextStyleFontModel`. Rich text is flattened to plain text, one literal per line.
- **Symbols.** Repeated symbols (tag heads, arrowheads, section heads, title block artwork) use `IfcRepresentationMap` / `IfcMappedItem`.
- **Images.** Logos and images use `IfcBlobTexture` (PNG or JPEG) on an `IfcAnnotationFillArea`, through `IfcSurfaceStyleWithTextures`.
- **Drawing linework.** With the setup option *Include 2D linework*, the view's computed draw list (DOC-HLR-004) is also written: one `IfcAnnotation` (`ObjectType = 'DRAWING_LINEWORK'`) per view, whose representation holds one `IfcGeometricCurveSet` per distinct line style (each with its `IfcStyledItem`), plus `IfcAnnotationFillArea` items for cut poché. Tools without hidden-line capability then get a finished 2D drawing.
- **Other documentation data** written on export: phase status as the standard `Status` property (DOC-GFX-017); design options and worksets as `IfcGroup` (DOC-GFX-018; Chapter 6).
- The same export setup can also *strip RXD* (a "clean" exchange file without Reviera data, DOC-OUT-006).

**Acceptance criteria.**
- [ ] An IFC4 file exported with *Include documentation as IFC annotation* validates with IfcOpenShell's schema validator with no errors.
- [ ] A third-party IFC viewer that displays `Annotation` sub-contexts shows the exported floor plan's dimensions and text at the correct position and size.
- [ ] Each exported door tag is related to its door by `IfcRelAssignsToProduct`.
- [ ] With *Include 2D linework* on, the exported plan linework overlays the model plan with no visible offset.
- [ ] Opening a stripped export in Reviera creates no native annotation; the exported annotation appears only as read-only imported drafting.

### 5.1.3 Acceptance criteria (persistence)
- [ ] A saved project is one valid IFC file that, when reopened, restores every view, sheet, schedule and annotation (RXD embedded by default).
- [ ] Switching the project to the external RXD carrier (Chapter 2a) and back gives identical documentation.
- [ ] Opening a project with 500 views opens only the views that were open at the last save; `rxd.status` shows the other view documents as not loaded.
- [ ] A view document edited by hand so that it fails its schema opens as *damaged*, the rest of the project opens, and saving writes the damaged JSON back unchanged.
- [ ] Adding one text note to one view changes only that view's `views/annotation/<viewId>` RXD document (and the RXD index metadata defined in Chapter 2a).
- [ ] Third-party IFC tools open a Reviera project file without errors, ignoring the RXD.
